data.title: Section 174 is reversed, mostly
data.author: jawns
data.article_summary:
《The Pragmatic Engineer》报道，美国税法第174条对科技公司的影响有所缓解，但并非完全取消。2017年引入的第174条在2022年生效，导致科技公司在2023年面临开发人员薪资无法当年全额抵扣的问题，需分5年（美国内）或15年（美国外）摊销，对小型企业和盈利微薄的公司影响尤为严重。

好消息是，新法案撤销了针对美国内员工的限制，企业可选择当年全额抵扣开发人员薪资，且可追溯至2022年，允许重新申报退税。然而，针对美国外开发人员的薪资仍需15年摊销，可能促使美国科技公司减少海外招聘。整体而言，这一变化对美国内企业有利，但对海外开发人员可能不利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Section 174修订对美国软件工程师薪资和就业市场的影响

不同观点：
• [g42gregory] 认为谷歌等大公司有能力影响政府决策，因此质疑单凭立法就能对公司底线产生如此大影响。他怀疑此事背后是否有更多未披露的细节。
• [avbanks] 认为Section 174的影响被低估了，并将其与近期的裁员潮联系起来，暗示该法律可能是裁员的直接原因。
• [breakyerself] 以讽刺的语气批评政府在处理此事上的失误，暗示政府通常只会把事情搞砸，而这次似乎打破了这一惯例。
• [vineyardmike] 认为该法律的修订对外包海外工作的成本增加有影响，可能有利于美国科技行业，并提出低生活成本或远程工作的美国员工可能受益，同时关注对其他行业的影响。
• [mertleee] 担心此“胜利”可能导致H1b签证上限增加，暗示可能出现更多外籍员工涌入美国市场。
• [throwawaybbq1] 希望撤销该法律能够逆转当前市场的低迷，并期待美国科技公司会因此增加招聘。
• [iooi] 质疑Section 174对FAANG公司是否真的有显著影响，认为小企业受影响更大。
• [qkeast] 关注15年摊销期是否仅适用于开发人员，询问设计师和产品经理等角色是否也受影响。
• [froggertoaster] 不理解为何15年摊销期会成为问题，暗示对该规定的反对意见可能站不住脚。
• [kevmo314] 对公司在亏损时选择摊销薪资的做法表示好奇，认为可能存在特定情况下选择摊销是有利的。
• [mlsu] 对Section 174的出台动机表示困惑，猜测可能与2022年硅谷高薪引发的不满有关，或有更深层次的政策原因。
• [spwa4] 批评政府每次增加税收时总是针对个人，而不是直接针对公司，并通过数学计算说明美国与非美国软件工程师的成本差距，认为该法律无法有效阻止工作岗位外流。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到外包和海外工作岗位的成本变化，以及该法律对美国与非美国员工的相对影响，反映出对全球化就业市场的关注。
• 一些评论（如[mertleee]和[spwa4]）提到了对H1b签证和外国开发人员的潜在影响，暗示法律修订可能带来意想不到的后果。
• 争议的焦点之一在于Section 174的影响是否被夸大，以及大公司是否真的无法通过政治手段避免此类立法的影响（如[g42gregory]和[iooi]的观点）。
• 部分评论对未来就业市场和公司决策的变化持观望态度，尤其是对大科技公司是否会因此改变招聘策略表示关注（如[throwawaybbq1]和[vineyardmike]）。

The Pulse: Section 174 is reversed! Mostly, that is
Finally, relief: tax regulation hurting the US tech industry is striked off for good - for the most part, that is.
Gergely Orosz

Hi, this is Gergely with a bonus, free issue of the Pragmatic Engineer Newsletter. In every issue, I cover Big Tech and startups through the lens of senior engineers and engineering leaders. Today, we get into one out of four topics from
last week’s The Pulse
issue, which full subscribers received seven days ago. If you’ve been forwarded this email, you can
subscribe here
.
Since early 2024, a tax change in the US named “Section 174” has been plaguing tech companies in the country. It was introduced during the first Trump administration in 2017, came into effect in 2022, and impacted businesses from the tax year of 2023. The next year, many tech companies discovered just how bad S174 is.
In short, salaries paid to software engineers can no longer be deducted as a cost, like all other employee wages are. Instead, they must be amortized over 5 years for developers in the US, and for 15 years (for developers outside the US.) This treats software development similar to physical assets like servers. The big difference is that software is
not
an asset that necessarily has re-sale value.
We published a deepdive
on why this regulation was likely to result in more developers being fired by tech companies, and fewer being hired. The regulation especially hurt small businesses, bootstrapped companies, and those making a small loss or profit. In short, a small, bootstrapped company spending $1M in developer costs that made zero profits would have suddenly owed $189K in corporate tax thanks to this tax change:
The impact of Section 174 changes on a company that has $1M in revenue and $1M in labor costs. From
The Pulse: Will US companies hire fewer engineers due to Section 174?
The regulation was designed to increase tax revenue from tech companies and entered the tax code, applying to all software developers, except those in the oil and gas sectors! Due to Section 174, the US became the only country in the world where developer salaries cannot be expensed in the same tax year.
Read more in our deepdive on S174.
But things have changed. Some great news is that part of S174 is struck off , fully for US employees.
Buried deep
inside Trump’s “Big, Beautiful Bill”
is a provision that allows companies to keep deducting expenses related to software development in the same tax year. Basically, developer salaries can be deducted just like before 2023. Companies have the
choice
to amortize salaries if they want.
In the original draft, this was planned to be a temporary relief until 2030. But in the final bill it was removed permanently.
Additional good news is that costs can be expensed retroactively.
Also added in the bill is how companies can do two years of “catch-up:” businesses can re-file tax returns using the
old
expensing rules 2022-2024. Basically, companies hurt by having to pay more tax in 2022 to 2024 can go back and claim back the surplus they paid.
This is an immediate relief to all US companies, but it’s not all good.
The remaining thing that stings for companies is how foreign devs still need to be amortized for 15 years.
US companies making foreign software development-related expenditures like hiring staff, or paying for contracts abroad, are still mandated to be expensed over 15 years. This period is very long, and will incentivize US companies to consider cutting developers abroad, or recruiting less from outside the US.
US tech companies have done plenty of hiring abroad, especially in Europe and India. The regulation makes it clear that anything considered research and experimental (R&E) that’s done outside the US
needs
to be expensed over 15 years.
I expect US companies to hire more in the US, and less outside of it.
The updated Section 174 very clearly incentivises doing so. If you’re in the US: this is great news! If you’re outside, prepare for US-based companies to be incentivized to make cuts abroad, and to hire less outside of the US.
Check out
last week’s The Pulse
and
this week’s The Pulse
for more, timely analysis on the tech industry.

data.title: Show HN: Molab, a cloud-hosted Marimo notebook workspace
data.author: akshayka
data.article_summary: mo lab 提供云端托管的 marimo 笔记本环境，支持快速使用 Python 和 SQL 进行实验。用户可以创建新笔记或参考示例笔记本，示例内容包括 marimo 简介、 markdown 编写、绘图、SQL 使用、UI 元素、HF Inference Providers、嵌入可视化工具、向量搜索、Polars 机器人检测以及自定义小组件和使用 PyTorch 等，由 marimo 团队和 Hugging Face 提供，更新频繁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Marimo.app的持久化版本及其相关功能和应用场景

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏观点**：
   - [lahuard] 认为Marimo解决了 notebook 协作中的许多问题，并表示支持。
   - [sheepy] 感谢Marimo项目，指出它解决了Jupyter的一些痛点，认为项目设计周到。

• **功能与应用场景的疑问**：
   - [anilgulecha] 询问该项目是否支持自托管，特别是用于教育用途，但在repo中未找到相关信息。
   - [elashri] 认为该工具可以帮助完成一些通常用Colab完成的任务，特别是在教学和教程分享方面，但同时关心云版本的隐私政策问题。

• **技术实现与改进建议**：
   - [matsonj] 曾希望Wasm能使项目运行得更好，但结果不如预期，不过仍对Marimo的发布表示赞赏，并询问下一步计划。

• **用户引导与教程需求**：
   - [countfeng] 建议制作视频教程以帮助用户更好地理解和使用该工具。

补充讨论：
• **幽默与调侃**：
   - [cantdutchthis] 以幽默的方式提醒大家不要在周五发布上线，隐含对技术项目上线时机的小调侃。

争议焦点：
• **隐私政策**：[elashri] 关心云版本的隐私政策，但未找到相关信息，这可能成为用户采纳该工具时的顾虑。
• **自托管可行性**：[anilgulecha] 关心是否可以自托管以满足教育用途，但目前信息不明确，可能影响部分用户的选择。

data.title: Teufel Mynd open source / open hardware Bluetooth speaker
data.author: Eduard
data.article_summary: MYND是一款新一代扬声器，具有2.1声道和波导设计，便携且具备IP67防护。产品采用完全开源设计，售价229.99欧元，现优惠至249.99欧元（含税和运费）。运费根据商品的大小、重量、目的地等因素计算，德国境内外运费不同。特别重或大的订单由货运代理交付，并需预约送货日期。送货时间通常为3-5个工作日，最长不超过14个工作日。MYND不附带USB-C充电器，需自行准备兼容的充电器。提供8周试听和免费退货服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自制蓝牙音箱的可行性、挑战以及"开源"在此背景下的具体含义。

不同观点：
• [throwaway81523] 认为使用商品化零件自制蓝牙音箱没有太大挑战，特别是如果有一个开源的蓝牙软件栈。他还提到市场上的蓝牙音箱价格过高，并以自己使用的5美元音箱为例，暗示高价产品不合理。

• [epic9x] 提供了对Mynd设计的详细解释，强调其设计的创新性和环保性。他指出该音箱具有用户可自行更换电池、模块化设计、以及使用主流供应商的组件以减少浪费等优点。此外，Teufel公司还发布了完整的原理图、PCB布局、固件和3D打印外壳文件。

• [manuel2258] 对"开源"的具体含义提出疑问，询问是否仅指3D文件，还是也包括软件部分的开源。

• [asacrowflies] 抱怨无法访问文章，因为被cookie通知和国家选择重定向拦截，未能获取相关信息。

补充讨论：
• [epic9x] 的评论提供了有关Mynd音箱设计的技术细节，特别强调了其环保和易维修的特点，这可能是对[throwaway81523]所提挑战的回应，指出在设计和可持续性方面的独特之处。

• [manuel2258] 的疑问揭示了对"开源"概念在硬件项目中的应用的关注，这可能影响到用户对该项目的自主性和使用自由的认知。

争议焦点：
• 自制蓝牙音箱的实际挑战与价值：[throwaway81523]认为价格过高且容易自制，而[epic9x]则强调了Mynd设计在技术细节和环保方面的独特性和复杂性。

• "开源"在此项目中的具体范围：[manuel2258]质疑开源的实际范围，表明用户对项目透明度和可访问性的关注。

data.title: Show HN: OrioleDB Beta12 Features and Benchmarks
data.author: akorotkov
data.article_summary: OrioleDB是PostgreSQL的存储扩展，旨在解决其可扩展性瓶颈，提升多核CPU和高性能存储系统的利用率。近期更新包括：支持非B-tree索引类型、回滚数据库近期更改、支持表空间和fillfactor、新增空间利用统计函数`orioledb_tree_stat()`，以及支持超过32列的表。性能改进包括更高效的存储分配、行级和页级撤销日志的分离、主键查找的定制扫描节点，以及B-tree内页导航的优化。通过TPC-C风格的基准测试（使用go-tpc和sysbench工具）显示，OrioleDB在多种实例类型下的性能显著优于PostgreSQL默认的Heap存储引擎，特别是在高吞吐量在线事务处理（OLTP）场景中。例如，在16xl实例下，OrioleDB的tpmC达到218,716，而Heap仅为83,653。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres数据库是否会采纳新的存储引擎（OrioleDB）以及其潜在影响和实现方式

不同观点：
• [atombender] 认为OrioleDB的性能提升非常显著，尤其是其基于undo log的系统设计可以避免Postgres当前MVCC机制导致的bloat问题。虽然这种设计可能在读取未提交数据时牺牲一些读性能，但整体上认为这种设计更优。然而，他质疑Postgres核心团队是否会因为保守而不接受如此大的改动，尤其是替换现有的MVCC机制。

• [akorotkov] 提到了OrioleDB新版本中的fastpath树搜索功能，可以加速密集键值查找的工作负载，并预告了即将发布的博客文章。

• [ksec] 表达了对OrioleDB成为Postgres官方部分的期望，认为这将使开源SQL数据库系统更加强大且无需过多定制，尤其是在结合Planetscale的工作时。

• [rickette] 关心Postgres的全文搜索（FTS）功能是否会从OrioleDB存储引擎中受益。

• [ololobus] 询问OrioleDB是否需要核心补丁，还是可以在标准上游Postgres中作为扩展安装。

• [kabes] 询问OrioleDB作为Postgres扩展的稳定性以及距离正式发布还有多远。

• [znpy] 关心OrioleDB如何融入当前的数据库生态系统，特别是能否与其他扩展（如Amazon最近发布的pgactive）一起使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Postgres核心团队是否会接受OrioleDB作为主要存储引擎，尤其是考虑到团队在引入大改动时的保守态度。
• 评论中还涉及OrioleDB的具体技术实现细节，如fastpath树搜索的性能提升，以及其在不同工作负载下的适用性。
• 用户对OrioleDB的安装方式和与其他扩展的兼容性也表示了关注。

44570389.article_content:
Since our
last public update
, OrioleDB has continued to evolve with a series of new releases. These updates refine the core engine, extend functionality, and improve performance across a range of workloads. Together, they move us closer to a beta release and lay the groundwork for broader adoption.
What is OrioleDB?
​
OrioleDB is a PostgreSQL storage extension that implements a custom
Table Access Method
as a drop‑in replacement for the default Heap storage engine. It is designed to address scalability bottlenecks in PostgreSQL’s buffer manager and reduces the WAL, enabling better utilization of modern multi-core CPUs and high‑performance storage systems.
By rethinking core components such as MVCC, page caching, and checkpoints, OrioleDB improves throughput and predictability in transactional workloads without altering PostgreSQL’s user-facing behavior.
What’s New in OrioleDB?
​
Building on this foundation, recent releases have introduced several user-facing enhancements:
Support for non‑
B-tree
index types
on OrioleDB tables.
Support for
rewinding recent changes
in the database.
Support for tablespaces.
fillfactor
support for OrioleDB tables and indexes.
orioledb_tree_stat()
SQL function for space utilization statistics.
Support for tables with more than 32 columns.
These additions improve OrioleDB/PostgreSQL compatibility and provide more flexibility for workloads with diverse schema and indexing requirements.
Performance improvements
​
Alongside these user‑facing additions, significant performance improvements have been made:
Storage and Transactional Efficiency
​
Sparse file support for more efficient storage allocation.
Separation of row‑level and page‑level undo logs.
Optimizations to avoid undo records for insertions into tables created by the same transaction
Query and Index Performance
​
Custom scan node for primary key lookups, reducing redundant index searches.
Faster
B-tree
inner page navigation for improved index performance.
To assess the impact of these changes, we benchmarked OrioleDB against PostgreSQL’s default Heap storage engine using
TPC-C
style workloads with
go-tpc
and
sysbench
. These tests measure CPU and IO scalability under mixed read‑write conditions and evaluate how OrioleDB’s architecture performs in transactional workloads.
Benchmarks
​
TPC-C is a standard benchmark for measuring how well databases handle high-throughput online transaction processing (OLTP). The test uses a database with 10 tables and includes five types of transactions:
NewOrder – for creating new orders
Payment – for processing payments
OrderStatus – for checking order status
Delivery – for handling deliveries
StockLevel – for analyzing inventory
Benchmark Infrastructure
​
We’ve run all of these instances on a
Supabase 2XL Instance using io2 storage
unless otherwise specified. Postgres configuration options use Supabase’s defaults.
The instance used for running the load test was located in the same AWS region (but in an different AZ) as the Supabase database to reduce the side effects of network latency, and to keep the scenario realistic.
We ran three different tools to assess Oriole beta12: go-tpc, sysbench, and OLTP.
Benchmark 1: go-tpc
​
go-tpc
is a Go-based TPC-C benchmark by PingCAP. It prioritizes performance and ease of deployment. The goal of go-tpc is a lightweight, scalable benchmarking tool for modern distributed databases.
Run the test yourself
Setup:
10,000 warehouses
1TB of data
1,000,000,000 rows in stock table
300,000,000 rows in customer, order, history tables
Instructions:
Prepare the database
./gotpc tpcc --warehouses 10000 prepare -T 100 -d postgres -U postgres -p 'password' -D postgres -H db.ref.supabase.com -P 5432 --conn-params sslmode=disable --no-check
Run the benchmark multiple times
./gotpc tpcc --warehouses 10000 run -d postgres -U postgres -p 'password' -D postgres -H db.ref.supabase.com -P 5432 --conn-params sslmode=disable -T <20,50,100,200,400> --time <100s,300s,1800s>
aggregate the results, calculate average numbers of tpmC (transactions-per-minute-C)
Results:
This TPC-C benchmark uses transactions-per-minute-C (tpmC) to measure the throughput of a system. This measurement is based on the number of NewOrder transactions a system can handle per minute:

Benchmark 2: sysbench
​
sysbench
is a Lua-based multi-purpose benchmark tool. Includes oltp_read_write, oltp_read_only, etc., which simulate OLTP workloads. The goal is general performance testing of transactional workloads, not strict TPC-C compliance.
Run the test yourself

A TPCC data set generated with

and

You can replicate the data following

Postgres with OrioleDB averaged ~19,000 QPS. Postgres with Heap averaged ~9,500 QPS. With gp3 storage we observed ~8500 QPS f

data.title: Every part on a bicycle is safety critical
data.author: spooky_deep
data.article_summary: 文章强调了自行车每个部件的安全关键性，警告读者不要轻视任何部件的故障风险。作者Dave Rome指出，虽然有些人认为只有部分组件如转向管和车把是安全关键的，但实际上现代自行车的每个部件都可能影响安全。他呼吁骑行者、机械师和制造商更加重视产品安全，建议定期检查和维护，并寻求专业帮助。Rome特别提到轻量材料和高端部件的使用增加了风险，例如车把和轮胎安装不当可能导致严重事故。他提醒，即便是使用扭力扳手也不能完全保证安全，需要考虑校准、部件设计和润滑等因素。文章最后呼吁将自行车视为由多个安全关键部件组成的整体，提高安全意识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自行车部件的安全性与故障影响，以及维护的必要性

不同观点：
• [HPsquared] 认为不同部件的故障模式和警告信号是关键设计特征，特别是在安全关键设备中。例如，轻量竞赛组件在山区骑行时的小故障可能导致严重事故，而通勤自行车对组件故障的容忍度更高。
• [pentamassiv] 提到现代自行车还面临网络攻击的风险，比如通过固件漏洞进行降级攻击。
• [exabrial] 强调扭矩扳手的一致性比绝对精度更重要，特别是在确保多个螺栓受力均匀方面。但对于某些关键部件，如碳杆控制，仍需严格按照制造商的建议操作。
• [donatj] 指出骑行环境和方式对部件故障的影响不同。例如，休闲骑行和下坡山地骑行的风险不同。
• [Dazzler5648] 认为讨论中忽视了许多人无法负担所谓“安全”自行车和专业维护的现实。强调骑手本身是自行车最重要的部分，许多人使用简陋的交通工具也能到达目的地。
• [andrewaylett] 分享了个人经历，链条断裂导致了严重的皮肤损伤，强调定期更换重要部件的必要性。
• [saidinesh5] 指出自行车轮胎与路面的接触有限，导致刹车时无法迅速停止，强调骑行时需更加谨慎。
• [mrob] 认为链条滑脱是令人担忧的故障模式，尤其是在躲避交通时，因此需要定期检查磨损和调整。
• [decasia] 分享了个人维护不当导致摔伤的经历，表达了对自行维护的担忧。
• [zkmon] 认为每个部件的功能性故障可能导致安全问题，但本质上是功能问题，而非单纯的安全问题。
• [dbrowne] 反对夸大恐惧，认为只要避免使用假冒部件，扭矩扳手的一致性在10%以内即可，无需过度担心。

补充讨论：
• 骑行安全不仅依赖于自行车部件，还包括骑手的技能和训练，例如如何应对刹车失灵和使用手信号。
• 有人提到通过推广“荷兰式开门法”等交通安全措施，可以提升骑行安全性。
• 讨论中还涉及自行车的社会和历史影响，如自行车在工业化进程中的革命性作用。

争议焦点：
• 自行车部件故障的风险是否被夸大，尤其是对于普通骑行者而言。
• 扭矩扳手的精确性和一致性在实际操作中的重要性。
• 骑行安全更多依赖于自行车质量和维护，还是骑手的技能和经验。

44613419.article_content:
Workshop
Threaded #43: Every part on a bike is safety-critical
An important PSA.
by
Dave Rome
Jul 18, 2025
More from
Dave Rome +
It’s common to hear horror stories about component failures that won't just leave you stranded, but can directly lead to injury, or, in rare cases, even worse.
I often hear people warn against messing around with “safety-critical components” such as steerer tubes and handlebars, but that it’s fine to buy cheap copies of other, less-critical, parts. Now, I don’t want to sound like an anxious, fear-mongering, panphobe, but I’m increasingly of the opinion that
every
part on a modern bicycle is safety-critical. More simply, I think many of us, whether you’re a rider, mechanic, designer, or manufacturer, should be taking product safety more seriously.
This edition of
Threaded
breaks the mold of tool geekery and mechanic insights. Rather, my goal is to get you thinking more broadly about your equipment and servicing choices. It’s a public service announcement that’s been on my mind for far too long. Unfortunately, much of this article is based on personal experience or firsthand reports.
In other words, like many mechanics, I’ve Seen Some Shit.
Everything can be scary
Bicycles are marvellous inventions that, for many of us, serve a purpose that extends well beyond efficient transport. However, the simplicity and minimalism that make bicycles so special also demand respect.
We’re increasingly in a time where individuals without prior experience are encouraged to take on a new task or a skill through the assistance of a YouTube buddy or Reddit thread. There’s a lot of joy in that, sometimes money to be saved, but I fear many have become numb to or even ignorant of the risks such an approach may present.
I'm not here to gate-geek who should and shouldn't work on bikes, but I do feel that too many people are taking on installation and service tasks, laughing it off as "just a bicycle", without consideration or knowledge of what's at stake.
Far too many people will ride their bike into the ground, waiting for something to play up before getting it serviced. My advice is to consider the potential safety ramifications of doing so.
Sure, a lot of this is stuff you can check yourself, but when we talk about a safety-critical mindset, it’s helpful to have an independent expert eye – someone who has Seen Some Shit and knows what to look for. If this is you, awesome. Otherwise, ask around your local area for trusted mechanics who have been at it a while and have built a trusted reputation for detail.
This especially applies in modern performance-oriented bicycles where the use of lightweight materials only increases the window of risk. For example, tightening a handlebar used to be simple, but now one needs to find the narrow window between not having a bar slip from a lack of clamping force while avoiding a bar that structurally fails through too much clamping force. Shooting on either side of the goal can be extremely dangerous.
It’s now common for many to use a
torque wrench
for parts like stem bolts, but such a tool is only as good as its user and also the quality of the parts being bolted together. I’ve seen the simplest of tasks go wrong through just a smidge of human error and/or poor design. Add in that many of us are pushing our bikes and bodies harder than ever, and the risk of component failure only grows.
And it’s not just your own safety you may be risking. Those who ride in groups should be even more aware and attentive to issues, as even the simplest skipped gear could cause a ripple in the wheels following behind if the pace is high enough.
Even a torque wrench doesn't necessarily get you to the safe zone. Differences in calibration, usage, parts design, fastener quality, lubrication, and so on all play into a simple task of doing up a bolt.

However, there are instances where a failure from any other component could result in a loss of control.

44613419.article_summary: 文章强调了自行车每个部件的安全关键性，警告读者不要轻视任何部件的故障风险。作者Dave Rome指出，虽然有些人认为只有部分组件如转向管和车把是安全关键的，但实际上现代自行车的每个部件都可能影响安全。他呼吁骑行者、机械师和制造商更加重视产品安全，建议定期检查和维护，并寻求专业帮助。Rome特别提到轻量材料和高端部件的使用增加了风险，例如车把和轮胎安装不当可能导致严重事故。他提醒，即便是使用扭力扳手也不能完全保证安全，需要考虑校准、部件设计和润滑等因素。文章最后呼吁将自行车视为由多个安全关键部件组成的整体，提高安全意识。

data.title: Zig Interface Revisited
data.author: ww520
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何在Zig语言中通过动态分派实现多态性，特别是使用虚拟函数表（VTable）接口模式。Zig没有内置的接口机制，但可以通过其他方式实现多态，如泛型和编译时调度、标记联合以及VTable接口。文章重点讲解了如何利用VTable构建接口，使得不同类型的实现（如日志记录器）能够共享同一接口并支持动态分派。文章给出了一个示例，展示了如何为控制台日志和文件日志实现独立的日志记录器，并通过VTable接口模式将它们统一起来使用。这种方法实现了接口与实现的清晰分离，且无需修改实现类型，同时支持通过函数指针进行完全的动态分派。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig 编程语言的接口支持、语法一致性以及动态分派和 vtable 的使用

不同观点：
• [lenkite] 认为 Zig 缺乏原生的接口支持，导致手动处理函数指针和分派机制非常繁琐且容易出错。建议在标准库中增加辅助工具或代码生成器来简化这些操作。虽然 Zig 是低级编程语言，但现代编程中接口支持应是基础功能。否则，用户可能会创建自定义的代码生成器，导致不一致性。

• [int_19h] 讨论了 Zig 中 vtable 设计的不同之处，指出 Zig 的 vtable 是附加在每个实例上的，而非共享的。这种设计在实现对象时仍需额外的间接调用。与传统的 C++ vtable 设计相比，这种做法显得不够优化。

• [billmcneale] 对 Zig 的语法不一致性提出批评，指出在命名约定中存在驼峰命名（Camel case）和蛇形命名（Snake case）混用的情况，并提到 "anyopaque" 等不明确的关键字，增加了语言的混乱。

• [justinhj] 表示，通常开发者会认为自己不常使用的语言如果加上自己喜欢语言的某个功能就会变得完美。暗示对 Zig 添加接口支持的需求可能只是个人偏好。

• [kingstnap] 认为将 `pub fn implBy(impl_obj: anytype)` 放在不寻常的位置是不合理的，建议学习 Zig 中分配器的做法，通过 `getLogger` 函数来创建 logger，以保持实现的私有性，并提高代码的清晰度和可维护性。

• [andsoitis] 提出关于动态分派和 vtable 使用的疑问，询问是否所有代码库都使用相同模式，以及这种设计是否会影响应用程序和库之间的互操作性。

• [ozgrakkurt] 支持使用 vtable，认为 vtable 在编译时间和代码整洁性上具有优势，相比使用泛型更加清晰。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 Zig 是否需要原生的接口支持，以及现有 vtable 设计的合理性。
• 语法一致性和命名约定也是部分开发者关注的重点。
• 动态分派和 vtable 的使用优劣在不同开发者之间存在不同看法。

data.title: OpenAI Is Building an office productivity suite
data.author: ishita159
data.article_summary: OpenAI计划推出集成生成式AI的办公生产力套件，直接挑战微软的Microsoft 365业务。这导致微软与OpenAI的关系恶化，甚至可能采取损害双方的激烈行动。微软在OpenAI的130亿美元投资价值成为争议焦点，OpenAI暗示可能通过反垄断诉讼打击微软，而微软则可能中断与OpenAI的谈判。OpenAI的生产力套件将专注于协作文档编辑、自动会议转录和团队聊天，并与ChatGPT紧密集成。虽然市场看似饱和，但OpenAI可能通过其生成式AI工具提供独特的协作体验，颠覆传统文档创建方式，成为AI驱动工作场所的未来。微软365的高昂价格使其在定价上也存在脆弱性。

44617202.article_content:
by
Preston Gralla
Contributing Editor
OpenAI goes for Microsoft’s jugular — its Office productivity suite
opinion
Jul 15, 2025
6 mins
Generative AI
Google
Microsoft
The ChatGPT maker is eyeing the launch of its own productivity suite with generative AI built in, directly attacking Microsoft’s multibillion dollar Microsoft 365 office suite business.
Credit:
Air Force photo illustration by Margo Wright
The relationship between Microsoft and OpenAI,
once the biggest bromance in the tech industry
, has deteriorated so badly that the companies
are now mulling taking “nuclear options” against one another
— actions that could seriously damage both companies.
At issue is how much Microsoft’s $13 billion investment in OpenAI will be worth if OpenAI goes public, as it plans to do. The companies are locked in an increasingly bitter battle over how Microsoft’s investment should be valued.
OpenAI has already hinted at moves that could get the US government to prosecute Microsoft for AI-related antitrust violations, which could force the company to spin off its AI products. Microsoft, in turn, might shut off negotiations with OpenAI, putting any IPO — and the company’s future — at risk.
Now OpenAI is going straight for Microsoft’s jugular: It’s considering launching a productivity suite with generative AI (genAI) tools built in, a direct attack on Microsoft’s multibillion dollar Microsoft 365 office suite business.
OpenAI’s plans for a productivity suite remain hush-hush, but some details have leaked. Here’s what we know now, and what the consequences of launching one might be.
What might OpenAI’s productivity suite include?
The little reporting done about OpenAI’s suite
says it will focus on collaborative document editing, include automated meeting transcriptions, have team chat capabilities, and be tightly integrated with ChatGPT.
Beyond that, little is known. Will it have a full suite of applications, including a word processor, spreadsheet, presentation software, and email? Will there be more than that, along the lines of Microsoft’s Clipchamp for video creation, or Project for project management? What collaboration capabilities would it have? And how would it all linked to genAI?
Most important of all: What in the suite would make enterprises abandon Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace for OpenAI’s offering? So far, mum’s the word.
At first glance, it seems as if there’s little room in the market for a third enterprise-focused office productivity suite.
Google and Microsoft take very different approaches to their suites
, which leaves OpenAI with very little to offer that either of them doesn’t have already.
Microsoft takes a maximalist, everything-plus-the-kitchen-sink approach with Microsoft 365. Each app is stacked with so many features, there’s very little they can’t do. When was the last time you needed to print envelopes or do mail merges? Probably never. But they’re available in Word if you want them. The same holds true for all the other apps in the suite.
Google has taken a different approach. Workplace isn’t nearly as feature-rich as Microsoft 365, but Google’s collaborative tools are much better than Microsoft’s.
With such a clear differentiation, it’s relatively easy for enterprises to decide which suite they prefer: Microsoft 365 for a full feature set, Google Workspace for collaboration.
That seems to leave no room for an OpenAI’s productivity suite. It’s unlikely to improve so much on Google’s traditional collaboration tools or Microsoft’s feature set that it can gain a foothold. Trying to split the difference between the suites and offer a wishy-washy application somewhere between the two won’t help at all.
So, it’s likely OpenAI’s suite will play to its strengths and offer genAI-centric collaboration for creating, editing, and finalizing documents, possibly turning the way people create documents on its head. Rather than have a single author write a document, then send links to others so they can collaborate on editing it, OpenAI’s suite might well use collaborative AI from the get-go, allowing people to use AI prompts together to create documents from scratch. They would also collaboratively edit it using AI. It could also use genAI-guided brainstorming and even genAI graphic-creation tools as well.
This way, the suite won’t need to replicate Microsoft 365’s bells and whistles or take a back seat to Google Workplace for collaboration. It could be pitched as the future of the genAI-driven workplace.
Follow the money
Just as no one knows the exact feature set of the suite, no one knows how much OpenAI might charge for it if it’s launched. Pricing is one area where Microsoft is extremely vulnerable. Enterprise versions of Microsoft 365
cost anywhere from $7.75 per user per month to $35.75 per user per month
, depending on the feature set. Adding Microsoft 365 Copilot
costs $30 more per user per month
, tripling the cost of Microsoft 365 with AI for some companies — and doubling the price or more for mos

data.title: Make Your Own Backup System – Part 1: Strategy Before Scripts
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了备份的重要性以及常见的误区和错误做法。许多人低估了备份的价值，依赖不充分的技术或未经验证的“薛定谔的备份”，导致数据丢失。现代人常依赖云存储，却忽视了保护数据的责任其实在于自己。文章强调备份应可恢复、采用开放格式并保持一致性。作者列举了多种数据丢失场景，如自然灾害、勒索软件攻击、人为破坏和操作失误等，特别指出联网服务器风险更高。

文章指出，许多人误以为简单复制文件就是备份，实际上这非常危险。正确的备份需要规划，包括评估风险、确定需保护的数据、可容忍的停机时间及存储空间。备份方案应平衡安全性与成本，考虑本地和远程备份的优缺点。关键决策在于选择备份整个磁盘还是个别文件，各有其优劣。最终，备份策略应根据具体需求量身定制，没有完美的解决方案。

• [progbits] 建议通过限制客户端只能写入新备份，不能删除，来增强安全性。备份服务器应有自己的文件系统快照。推荐使用 rsync/ssh 来实现此目的。
• [binwiederhier] 强调备份不等于灾难恢复，恢复时间目标（RTO）和恢复点目标（RPO）至关重要。指出“应用程序一致性备份”比“崩溃一致性备份”更可靠，并提到多重备份存储的重要性。

• [daneel_w] 分享了一个简单的备份方案，使用 tar+compress+encrypt 进行备份，并存储在多个地点。
• [bob1029] 推荐使用 RDBMS 的同步或异步日志复制策略来进行备份，指出这种方法可以应用于其他数据类型。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于使用何种备份和恢复策略最为可靠和高效。部分用户强调手动测试备份和使用 PULL 策略的重要性，而另一些用户则关注备份一致性和灾难恢复的实际效果。
• 另一个值得注意的点是多设备、多站点数据管理以及如何有效存储和恢复大量数据的问题。
• 用户分享了多种备份工具和自动化方案，如 restic、borg、PBS for proxmox 等，显示出社区对开源和自定义解决方案的偏好。

44618687.article_content:
Backup: Beyond the Simple Copy
For as long as I can remember, backup is something that has been underestimated by far too many people. Between flawed techniques, "SchrÃ¶dinger's backups" (i.e., never tested, thus both valid and invalid at the same time), and conceptual errors about what they are and how they work (RAID is not a backup!), too much data has been lost due to deficiencies in this area.
Nowadays, backup is often an afterthought. Many rely entirely on "the cloud" without ever asking how - or if - their data is actually protected. It's a detail many overlook, but even major cloud providers operate on a shared responsibility model. Their terms often clarify that while they secure the infrastructure, the ultimate responsibility for protecting and backing up your data lies with you. By putting everything "in the cloud", on clusters owned by other companies, or on distributed Kubernetes systems, backup seems unnecessary. When I sometimes ask developers or colleagues how they handle backups for all this, they look at me as if I'm speaking an archaic, unknown, and indecipherable language. The thought has simply never crossed their minds. But data is not ephemeral; it must be preserved in every way possible.
I've always had a philosophy: data must always be restorable (and as quickly as possible), in an open format (meaning you shouldn't have to buy anything to restore or consult it), and consistent. These points may seem obvious, but they are not.
I have encountered various scenarios of data loss:
Datacenters destroyed by fire
â I had 142 servers there, but they were all restored in just a few hours.
Server rooms flooded.
Servers destroyed in earthquakes, often due to collapsing walls.
Increasing incidents of various ransomware attacks.
Intentional damage by entities seeking to create problems.
Mistakes made by administrators, which can happen to anyone.
The risk escalates for servers connected to the internet, like e-commerce and email servers. Here, not only is data integrity crucial, but so is the uninterrupted operation of services. This series of posts will revisit some of my old articles to explain my core ideas on the subject and describe, at least in part, my primary techniques.
Many consider a backup to be a simple copy. I often hear people say they have backups because they "copy the data", but this is often wrong and extremely dangerous, providing a false sense of security. Copying the files of a live database is an almost useless operation, as the result will nearly always be impossible to restore. It is essential to at least perform a proper dump and then transfer that file. Yet, many people do this and will only realize their mistake when they face an emergency and need to restore.
The Backup Plan: Asking the Right Questions
Before touching a single file, you must start with a plan, and that plan starts with asking the right questions:
"How much risk am I willing to take? What data do I need to protect? What downtime can I tolerate in case of data loss? What type and amount of storage space do I have available?"
The first question is particularly critical. A common but risky approach is to store a backup on the same machine that requires backing up. While convenient, this method fails in the event of a machine failure. Even relying on a classic USB drive for daily backups is not foolproof, as these devices are as susceptible to failure as any other hardware component. And contrary to popular belief, even high-end uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) are not immune to catastrophic failures.
Thus, the initial step is to establish a management plan, balancing security and cost. The safest backup is often the one stored farthest from the source machine. However, this approach introduces challenges related to space and bandwidth. While local area network (LAN) backups are relatively straightforward, off-network backups involve additional connectivity considerations. This might lead to a compromise on the amount of data backed up to maintain operational speed during both backup and recovery processes.
Safety doesn't always equate to practicality. For instance, with a 200 MBit/sec connection and 2 TB of backup data, the recovery time could be significant. However, if the goal is not rapid restorability but simply ensuring the data is available, the safest backup is often the one closest to us. That is, a backup we can "touch", disconnect, and consult even when offline.
Therefore, it is essential to develop a backup policy tailored to specific needs, keeping in mind that no 'perfect' solution exists.
The Core Decision: Full Disk vs. Individual Files
When planning a backup strategy, one key decision is whether to back up the entire disk or just individual files. Or both of them. Each approach has its pros and cons.
Entire Disk (or Storage) Backup
Advantages:
Complete Recovery: Restoring a full disk backup can quickly revert a system to its exact previous state, boot loader included.

data.title: Local LLMs versus offline Wikipedia
data.author: EvanHahn
data.article_summary: 文章比较了本地运行的大语言模型（LLM）与离线版维基百科的下载大小。作者使用Ollama库中的模型和Kiwix上的维基百科下载进行对比，选取了能在普通消费级硬件上运行的模型和不含图片的维基百科包。结果显示，维基百科的精选50,000篇文章大约相当于Llama 3.2 3B模型的大小，而整体上维基百科的大小可以从数百MB到数十GB不等，具体取决于内容的选择。文章指出，这种比较存在局限性，因为百科全书和LLM有不同的目的和特性，且文件大小并非唯一考量因素，内存和处理器需求也需考虑。尽管如此，作者认为这种比较依然有趣，并建议可能同时下载两者以备不时之需。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）与Wikipedia在知识存储、检索和理解上的不同作用及其潜在应用，尤其是在信息获取受限的场景下（如“重启社会”）。

不同观点：
• dcc认为，LLM的优势不仅仅在于存储或检索知识，而在于其能够理解模糊或不明确的问题，帮助用户找到答案。LLM可以解释复杂概念、根据用户的理解水平调整回答，并在不同学科间建立联系，这在互动式理解中非常宝贵。
• simonw指出，将Wikipedia下载到USB上是一个实际的做法，并且讨论了将Wikipedia数据转换为SQLite格式以实现全文搜索（FTS）的可能性。他提到大容量USB存储设备现在已经很普遍，不用担心空间问题。
• badsectoracula分享了自己正在进行的项目，将下载的Wikipedia文件与LLM结合使用，通过LLM对未分类数据进行整理和分析，并提到使用量化的Mistral Small 3.2模型在处理速度和效果上取得了不错的成果。
• twotwotwo认为，LLM和Wikipedia等资源在功能上有所不同。Wikipedia等资源提供的信息通常是准确的且不依赖猜测，而LLM则能够处理更复杂或不明确的问题，尽管有时会生成错误信息。他还提到在离线编码场景下，调用现有库可能比重新构建更有效。
• rlupi建议构建一个结合LLM和Wikipedia的工具，利用LLM生成概述并通过全文搜索或RAG方法查找事实，以减少小模型生成错误信息的风险。
• omneity介绍了Wikipedia Monthly项目，提供按语言分类的Wikipedia数据，并指出Simple English Wikipedia内容较为浅显和不准确。
• saddat提出，可以将LLM用于类似Voyager 3的任务中，提供一个初始简易界面，背后由LLM支持，以揭示人类知识。
• antonkar质疑为何人类不能像AI公司那样，将整个网络提炼成一个新的Wikipedia，以使孩子们变得更聪明。
• hannofcart认为，理想的灾难应急信息查询数据库应结合LLM和文件档案，LLM负责理解模糊查询并提供概述，然后列出相关的Wikipedia文章供用户进一步阅读。
• fho认为，这实际上是一个“为什么不能两者兼有”的情况，可以同时使用压缩的Wikipedia作为知识库，并利用LLM作为界面。
• meander_water指出，LLM输出的质量取决于输入提示的质量和深度。如果不知道该问什么，信息可能会被锁定在模型中，而Wikipedia则可以直接搜索和阅读所有内容。
• spankibalt认为，没有讨论页和版本历史的Wikipedia快照是不完整的，尤其是在LLM增强的文本分析中，这些元信息非常重要。
• entropie分享了自己在Nvidia Jetson Nano上的实验，利用GPU支持运行LLM，并提到在没有互联网的情况下，这种设置可能非常有用。
• VladVladikoff询问是否存在结合本地LLM和本地Wikipedia的项目，并提到RAG（检索增强生成）可能是一个解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到将LLM与Wikipedia结合使用的技术方案，如RAG，以提高信息检索的准确性。
• 有争议的焦点在于LLM生成错误信息的倾向与Wikipedia相对准确但静态的信息之间的权衡。
• 一些评论者分享了具体的项目和技术细节，如数据格式转换、模型运行环境等，提供了实际应用中的见解。
• 讨论还涉及到LLM在离线场景下的潜在应用，如重启社会或替代传统知识存储方式。

44617078.article_content:
Local LLMs versus offline Wikipedia
by
Evan Hahn
,
posted
Jul 19, 2025
Two days ago, MIT Technology review published
“How to run an LLM on your laptop”
. It opens with an anecdote about using offline LLMs in an apocalypse scenario. “‘It’s like having a weird, condensed, faulty version of Wikipedia, so I can help reboot society with the help of my little USB stick,’ [Simon Willison] says.”
This made me wonder: how do the sizes of local LLMs compare to the size of offline Wikipedia downloads?
I compared some models from the
Ollama library
to various downloads on
Kiwix
. I chose models that could be run on some consumer-grade hardware, and Wikipedia bundles that didn’t have images for a better comparison. Here’s what I found, ordered by size:

Download size

Wikipedia

This comparison has many caveats:
This is an apples-to-oranges comparison. Encyclopedias and LLMs have different purposes, strengths, and weaknesses. They are fundamentally different technologies!
File size is not the only important detail. LLMs, even local ones, can use lots of memory and processor power. Offline Wikipedia will work better on my ancient, low-power laptop.
Other entries might be more useful for a specific purpose. For example, you can download a selection of Wikipedia articles about chemistry, or an LLM that’s better tuned for your hardware. (And Kiwix has lots of other things you can download, like all of Stack Overflow.)
I picked these entries based on vibes. Nothing rigorous about this comparison!
Despite those caveats, I thought it was interesting that Wikipedia’s best 50,000 articles are, very roughly, equivalent to Llama 3.2 3B. Or that Wikipedia can be smaller than the smallest LLM, and larger than the largest ones—at least in an offline scenario on consumer hardware.
Maybe I’ll download both, just in case.

• rlupi建议构建一个结合LLM和Wikipedia的工具，利用LLM生成概述并通过全文搜索或RAG方法查找事实，以减少小模型生成错误信息的风险。
• omneity介绍了Wikipedia Monthly项目，提供按语言分类的Wikipedia数据，并指出Simple English Wikipedia内容较为浅显和不准确。
• saddat提出，可以将LLM用于类似Voyager 3的任务中，提供一个初始简易界面，背后由LLM支持，以揭示人类知识。
• antonkar质疑为何人类不能像AI公司那样，将整个网络提炼成一个新的Wikipedia，以使孩子们变得更聪明。
• hannofcart认为，理想的灾难应急信息查询数据库应结合LLM和文件档案，LLM负责理解模糊查询并提供概述，然后列出相关的Wikipedia文章供用户进一步阅读。
• fho认为，这实际上是一个“为什么不能两者兼有”的情况，可以同时使用压缩的Wikipedia作为知识库，并利用LLM作为界面。
• meander_water指出，LLM输出的质量取决于输入提示的质量和深度。如果不知道该问什么，信息可能会被锁定在模型中，而Wikipedia则可以直接搜索和阅读所有内容。
• spankibalt认为，没有讨论页和版本历史的Wikipedia快照是不完整的，尤其是在LLM增强的文本分析中，这些元信息非常重要。
• entropie分享了自己在Nvidia Jetson Nano上的实验，利用GPU支持运行LLM，并提到在没有互联网的情况下，这种设置可能非常有用。
• VladVladikoff询问是否存在结合本地LLM和本地Wikipedia的项目，并提到RAG（检索增强生成）可能是一个解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到将LLM与Wikipedia结合使用的技术方案，如RAG，以提高信息检索的准确性。
• 有争议的焦点在于LLM生成错误信息的倾向与Wikipedia相对准确但静态的信息之间的权衡。
• 一些评论者分享了具体的项目和技术细节，如数据格式转换、模型运行环境等，提供了实际应用中的见解。
• 讨论还涉及到LLM在离线场景下的潜在应用，如重启社会或替代传统知识存储方式。

data.title: The curious case of the Unix workstation layout
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了1990年代UNIX工作站的机箱布局，特别提到了Silicon Graphics的Indigo²、HP 9000系列以及DEC Alphastation。作者注意到这些高端工作站的内部设计，尤其是主板和扩展卡的布局，与当时PC机（如LPX和ATX标准）的设计有相似之处。例如，Indigo²和HP 9000 Visualize系列都采用了后置接口和左侧插卡的设计，类似于当时的PC布局。文章还提到早期DEC Alphastation采用VME总线设计，但后来的型号也出现了类似PC的设计元素，如PS/2接口和标准PC内存。作者对这种现象感到好奇，不确定是各大公司独立借鉴了PC设计，还是为了降低成本而有意为之，但认为这种趋势可能反映了PC设计对工作站的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机硬件设计的历史演变和相似性，特别是工作站和个人电脑的机箱设计、总线技术以及生产制造过程中的共性。

不同观点：
• [ChuckMcM] 认为，在计算机制造的早期，由于生产工厂有限，许多机械组件被重复使用，导致不同品牌的计算机在外观和设计上出现相似性。他还解释了NRE（非重复性工程费用）在生产工具成本摊销中的作用。
• [drewg123] 纠正了对Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，指出早期Alphastation使用的是DEC的Turbochannel技术，而非VME总线。
• [don-bright] 提到S-100总线，并提供了一些相关链接，指出这是另一种值得注意的早期计算机总线标准。
• [hapless] 提出Indigo2的设计是趋同演化的结果，由于要解决相同的设计问题（如兼容全长ISA卡的小型桌面机箱），导致不同品牌的计算机设计看起来相似。他还提到ATX标准的广泛采用使得不同架构的系统在外观上趋同。
• [grewil2] 提到Amiga 3000UX工作站，强调其运行Amiga Unix的独特性及其在GNU操作系统早期开发中的作用。
• [johnklos] 将Indigo2的设计与早期的Apple II和IBM PC进行比较，指出它们在布局上的相似性，并提到Amiga 3000的设计对后来机器的影响。
• [pinewurst] 再次纠正关于SGI Indigo和早期Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，确认它们分别使用GIO32和Turbochannel总线。
• [whartung] 讨论HP 9000 712与NeXTStation的比较，考虑其在耐用性、支持性和性能等方面的优劣。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 指出，专有UNIX工作站的超高 proprietary 性质，使得像SGI这样的厂商能以高价出售其硬件，因为无法在普通硬件上运行IRIX。
• [toast0] 认为LPX桌面设计是一个好的设计，解释了其在扩展性和传统布局方面的优点，并提到设计的趋同现象。
• [weinzierl] 回顾了计算机从集成键盘和显示器到桌面机箱再到塔式机箱的演变过程，指出设计随着时间推移变得更小、更实用。
• [aoki] 提到90年代初PC时代的三大趋势（Pentium、PCI、多平台Windows NT），并指出许多厂商转向基于PC总线和组件的设计以提高成本竞争力。
• [amelius] 建议研究台湾计算机历史，以寻找一些设计和生产上的“缺失环节”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是早期Alphastation是否使用VME总线，[drewg123]和[pinewurst]都明确指出其使用的是Turbochannel总线而非VME。
• 另一个讨论点是计算机设计的趋同演化现象，[hapless]和[toast0]都提到不同品牌和架构的计算机由于解决相同的设计问题而变得相似。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 强调了专有UNIX工作站的商业模式和其高价的原因，与其他讨论中提到的硬件设计和生产成本形成对比。

44616760.article_content:
The Curious Case of the UNIX workstation layout
Posted on
2025-07-19
Contents
Background
UNIX workstations
Silicon Graphics
HP 9000
DEC Alphastation
Conclusions
Background
Cathode Ray Dude recently did an excellent video about the history of the PC case, particularly the early- and mid-1990s, and the various mainboard layouts that pre-date the ATX standard. You should watch it. Here it is.
The rest of this blog will contain some spoilers for that video.
UNIX workstations
I have a bunch of 1990's RISC/UNIX workstations. I don't really know how it happened, but I went from having literally none back in October 2024, to having:
Silicon Graphics Power IndigoÂ²
Sun Ultra 80
HP 9000 Visualize B132L+
HP 9000 Visualize C3000
HP 9000 712 (running NeXTSTEP!)
Apple PowerMac 7200/90 (ok, Mac OS 7.6 Is Not UNIX, but I could install Linux or NetBSD if I wanted to)
I also briefly had an
Alphastation 500
, but I failed to get it working so I passed it on to someone who knows much more about them than me.
And watching CRD's video. I realised something.
Silicon Graphics
The Silicon Graphics IRIS Indigo is a tower workstation of the old-school. A light make-over of the previous IRIS 4D series, it has two huge PCBs, which insert vertical into a backplane using rotating clips. I'm pretty sure it's actually a
VME bus design
, both because of that Wikipedia page but because
SGI Depot describes them
as part of the "IRIS VME Series".
(ctvoigt, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en
, via Wikimedia Commons)
But the IndigoÂ² that came after it? Desktop case. Flat mainboard with ports on the rear. PSU on the right. Card riser on the left, with cards on the left. It takes standard PC SIMMs, and has PS/2 connectors for the keyboard and mouse. By jove it looks like LPX.
Eh, maybe it's a one-off.
HP 9000
I have wanted a PA-RISC machine for a while, but now I find myself owning three. The HP 9000 series has a long and storied history, and you should just go and read
http://openpa.net
because it is an excellent resource.
My new HP 7000 712 is the machine that HP used to port NeXTSTEP OS to PA-RISC. So, obviously, I've installed NeXTSTEP 3.3 for PA-RISC. I should probably do a whole separate piece about that, because it's retro but also alarmingly familiar to this daily macOS user.
Anyway, the Model 712 looks like this inside, and at the rear.
Definitely not LPX. Much more evocative of low-cost pizza-box Apple Machintoshes of the period, like the Macintosh LC II.
But let's look at the follow-up model, the Visualize B-Class (in this case a B132L+).
It's a single flat PCB, with connectors at the rear, a card riser on the left with cards leaning to the left. The only weird thing is that the card riser has to be high enough to clear the PSU. But look - it looks really kinda of LPX-like, right? And very different to the model that came before it.
DEC Alphastation
Early Alphastations were VME based machines. Like the Indigo, I've never had one, but I saw one at RetroFest 2025 in Swindon earlier this year.
I don't have a Creative Commons picture of the insides of a DEC 3000, but here's a website with a bunch of technical details:
https://www.chilton-computing.org.uk/ccd/mainframes/p012.htm
. It's definitely nothing like a PC.
But the Alphastation 500 I had (and failed to fix)?
Connectors at the rear. A riser, with cards on the left. Sure looks LPX inspired to me. Also those power connectors look awfully like ATX power connectors (although they don't have the ATX pinout). And we've got standard PC memory, and PS/2 connectors for the keyboard.
Conclusions
I have no conclusions here. Did Digital and HP and SGI all independently copy the Packard Bell and Dell PCs of the era? Or did they get together in some secret RISC UNIX cabal to re-use PC technolog and cut the price of entry (or, make more profit)? Or is the LPX desktop just the crab of personal computer design, and all lineages will converge here eventually. I have no idea.
But now, whenever I see a machine with ports at the back and a riser card on the left, with cards on the left, I'm going to think of CRD.

data.title: Piano Keys
data.author: gametorch
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了钢琴白键和黑键宽度排列的问题。由于黑键宽度相同且白键前端宽度一致，后端宽度无法完全相同。文章提出了几种优化方案，以最小化白键后端宽度的最大差异。初始方案如设置不同宽度组合，达到最大差异为B/2、B/6、B/8等。最佳传统方案是"B/12方案"，最大差异仅为B/12。进一步放宽条件，允许黑键和白键前端宽度变化，提出一种单位划分法，将一个八度分为878472单位，优化后最大差异显著减小，白键为0.0181英寸，黑键为0.0127英寸。这种优化方案在实际制造中更精确，显著减少宽度差异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钢琴键盘设计，特别是黑键和白键的布局及其合理性。

不同观点：
• **prmph** 认为当前的钢琴键盘设计没有问题，并提出假设：如果把黑键放在白键后面并占据白键的一部分宽度，并不影响弹奏。他质疑为什么白键后部的宽度需要一致，并指出 pianists 不会按到白键的后部。

• **bruce343434** 回应称，在他的钢琴上，黑键的宽度和白键后部的宽度是一样的，这是通过调整黑键的位置实现的，而不是将黑键完全置于白键中间。

• **kazinator** 认为钢琴设计中并没有对白键后部宽度过于精细的要求，实际设计中更关注黑键的宽度和分布。他解释了黑键和白键布局的历史设计方法，并指出这种设计并不是完全对称的，例如 E-F 之间的分割并不完全在两个黑键中间。

• **ralfd** 表示对原文内容不理解，建议需要更多图片来帮助理解。

• **moefh** 认为黑键的传统布局是将八度音分为两个部分（C-D-E 和 F-G-A-B），然后根据这些部分均匀放置黑键，并指出白键在这些部分内有“镜像”关系，例如 C 和 E 的位置关系。他认为实际的钢琴键盘符合这种描述。

• **NooneAtAll3** 希望文章中能有标注音符的图片，并希望看到按键宽度的示意图，以便更好地理解讨论内容。

• **ajuc** 认为钢琴键盘设计不规则，给演奏者带来了记忆不同和弦位置的负担，例如 C 大调和 D 大调的和弦形状不同。他建议可以采用更规则的设计，例如将一个八度分为 6 个白键和 6 个黑键。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于钢琴键盘布局的历史设计合理性，特别是黑键和白键的宽度与分布是否应该一致，以及这种不规则布局是否给学习者带来了不必要的困难。
• 一些评论者（如 prmph 和 kazinator）认为当前设计没有问题，而另一些人（如 ajuc）则认为可以采用更规则的设计来简化学习和演奏。
• 图片和视觉示例在讨论中被多次提及，显示出视觉辅助在理解键盘布局复杂性方面的重要性。

44576183.article_content:
Piano Keys
If you've ever looked closely at a piano keyboard you may have
noticed that the widths of the white keys are not all the same
at the back ends (where they pass between the black keys).  Of
course, if you think about it for a minute, it's clear they
couldn't possibly all be the same width, assuming the black keys
are all identical (with non-zero width) and the white keys all
have equal widths at the front ends, because the only simultaneous
solution of 3W=3w+2b and 4W=4w+3b is with b=0.
After realizing this I started noticing different pianos and how
they accommodate this little problem in linear programming.  Let W
denote the widths of the white keys at the front, and let B denote
the widths of the black keys.  Then let a, b,..., g (assigned to
their musical equivalents) denote the widths of the white keys
at the back.  Assuming a perfect fit, it's impossible to have
a = b = ... = g.  The best we can do is try to minimize the
greatest difference between any two of these keys.
One crude approach would be to set d=g=a=(W-B) and b=c=e=f=(W-B/2),
which gives a maximum difference of B/2 between the widths of any
two white keys (at the back ends).  This isn't a very good solution,
and I've never seen an actual keyboard based on this pattern
(although some cartoon pianos seem to have this pattern).  A better
solution is to set a=b=c=e=f=g=(W-3B/4) and d=(W-B/2).  With this
arrangement, all but one of the white keys have the same width at
the back end, and the discrepancy of the "odd" key (the key of "d")
is only B/4.  Some actual keyboards (e.g., the Roland HP-70) use
this pattern.
Another solution is to set c=d=e=f=b=(W-2B/3) and g=a=(W-5B/6),
which results in a maximum discrepancy of just B/6.  There are
several other combinations that give this same maximum discrepancy,
and actual keyboards based on this pattern are not uncommon.
If we set c=e=(W-5B/8) and a=b=d=f=g=(W-3B/4) we have a maximum
discrepancy of only B/8, and quite a few actual pianos use this
pattern as well.  However, the absolute optimum arrangement is to
set c=d=e=(W-2B/3) and f=g=a=b=(W-3B/4), which gives a maximum
discrepancy of just B/12.  This pattern is used on many keyboards,
e.g. the Roland PC-100.
The "B/12 solution" is the best possible given that all the black keys
are identical and all the white keys have equal widths at the front
ends.  For practical manufacturing purposes this is probably the
best approach.  However, suppose we relax those conditions and allow
variations in the widths of the black keys and in the widths of the
white keys at the front ends.  All we require is that the black
keys (in total) are allocated 5/12 of the octave.  On this basis,
what is the optimum arrangement, minimizing the maximum discrepancy
between any two widths of the same type?
Let A, B,...G denote the front-end widths of the white keys, and
let a#, c#, d#, f#, g# denote the widths of the black keys.  I
believe the optimum arrangement is given by dividing the octave
into 878472 units, and then setting
f=g=a=b=72156 units      c=d=e=74606 units      discrepancy=2450
f#=g#=a#=72520 units     c#=d#=74235 units      discrepancy=1715
F=G=A=B=126546 units     C=D=E=124096 units     discrepancy=2450
The maximum discrepancy between any two widths of the same class is
1/29.88 of the width of the average black key, which is less than
half the discrepancy for the "B/12 solution".
The max discrepancy is 1/358.56 of the total octave for the white
keys, and 1/512.22 for the black keys.  Since an octave is normally
about 6.5 inches, the max discrepancy is about 0.0181 inches for the
white keys and 0.0127 inches for the black keys.  (One peculiar fact
about this optimum arrangement is that the median point of the octave,
the boundary between f and f#, is exactly 444444 units up from the
start of the octave.)

data.author: ascorbic
data.article_summary: "am-i-vibing" 是一个用于检测代理编码环境和 AI 辅助工具的库。它帮助 CLI 工具和 Node 应用判断是否由 AI 代理执行，并做出相应调整，如改变输出格式或日志。该库支持多种 AI 工具，如 Claude Code、GitHub Copilot、Replit 等，并能识别三种环境类型：代理环境、交互环境和混合环境。通过提供的 API，开发者可以轻松检测当前环境类型并作出相应处理。此外，该库还提供了 CLI 工具，用于快速环境检测和调试。主要功能包括输出格式选择、特定环境类型检查、安静模式和调试模式等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用代理（agent）生成和运行代码的实践及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• barbazoo：认为代理生成的代码在运行时中体现其存在是不合适的。代理只是工具，开发者应亲自编写代码，特别是错误处理和消息提示，因为当凌晨3点收到警报时，代理无法帮忙。同时，人类易于理解的内容通常也易于LLM理解。

• Timwi：指出该方法存在多个缺点，包括不可靠性（项目文档中提到存在误报）、用户混淆（AI代理报告的内容与手动运行CLI工具的结果不一致）、以及用户无法手动访问功能。建议明确提供选项以启用新行为，并教导AI在适当情况下使用这些功能，而非依赖代理。

• 0xDEAFBEAD：认为当前的做法增加了供应链攻击的脆弱性，达到了不应有的程度。

• mrKola 和 fahrradflucht：对项目命名提出批评和替代建议，mrKola 戏谑地建议命名为 "vibrator"，fahrradflucht 则提出 "prompt-injection-toolkit" 作为替代。

• CaptainFever：认为该库设想的是合作性的结果，比如代码在检测到处于代理环境时提供额外上下文，但担心有人会利用此功能限制他人。在这种情况下，AI代理可能需要一个项目特定的“隐形模式”来保护用户。

• ritzaco：强烈反对该做法，认为代理应适应人类设计的工具或使用专门为代理设计的工具。让工具在人类和代理操作下表现不同只会导致混乱。

• ofirg：批评软件包命名不当，认为不应在项目获得实际使用后因压力而更改名称。

• petesergeant：对技术实现表现出兴趣，提到可能会通过monkey patch的方式让vitest在代理使用时显示完整差异。

• SudoSuccubus：对检测代理行为的尝试表示强烈反感，认为这种做法类似于学术界的“反作弊”系统，是徒劳的。强调应与未来技术合作，而不是抗拒。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于代理生成代码在运行时的影响、用户混淆以及潜在的安全风险。
• 部分评论集中在项目命名和命名恰当性的问题上。
• 部分评论表现出对技术改进的兴趣和建议，如明确启用新行为的选项和通过monkey patch增强工具功能。
• SudoSuccubus 的评论带有强烈的情绪，反对对代理行为的检测和限制尝试。

am-i-vibing
Detect agentic coding environments and AI assistant tools. This library allows CLI tools and Node apps to detect when they're being executed by AI agents. This enables them to adapt by, for example, providing different output formats or logs.
Installation
Install as library:
npm install am-i-vibing
Run as CLI tool:

Environment Types
The library detects three main types of environments:
Agent
: Command was directly run by an AI agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Jules)
Interactive
: Interactive commands run inside an AI environment (e.g. Cursor terminal, Replit shell)
Hybrid
: Environments that combine both agentic and interactive features in the same session (e.g. Warp)
There may be false positives, such as if a user directly runs a command in an terminal opened by an AI tool, such as a Copilot terminal in VS Code.

CLI Options

data.title: Why you should choose HTMX for your next web-based side project (2024)
data.author: kugurerdem
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何在侧边项目中选择HTMX而非传统的MPA或复杂的SPA。HTMX通过允许部分页面重载，使多页应用（MPA）具备类似单页应用（SPA）的现代用户体验，同时保持较低的开发复杂度和成本。MPA简单但因全页面刷新而显得笨重，SPA则能提供流畅的体验但开发复杂。HTMX作为一种低复杂度工具，帮助开发者快速、经济地构建现代 web 应用，已成为作者技术栈（HAM Stack）的核心部分。对于个人开发者而言，HTMX能有效降低时间和金钱成本，是侧边项目的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HTMX的优缺点及其在现代web开发中的应用

不同观点：
• cjs_ac认为HTMX通过"一次请求，一次响应"的模式，简化了网络交互，使得页面加载更快，避免了在客户端运行JS来决定是否请求其他资源的复杂性。
• wibbly非常喜欢HTMX，认为它为小规模项目提供了低成本的交互性，且可以优雅地降级为普通网站，对所有用户都有利。
• rapnie提到Datastar项目，认为HTMX项目已经完成，没有新功能，而Datastar提供了更小、更快、更面向未来的解决方案，建议在选择HTMX时也考虑Datastar。
• tekkk对"HAM栈"这个术语感到不适，认为虽然可以利用无服务器后端来降低成本，但重用可信的样板代码可能是更快的选择。
• lvl155质疑浏览器中JS的使用，认为每隔几个月就出现的新框架是因为我们拒绝改变浏览器，HTML需要现代化的解决方案，但目前这些方案显得丑陋和过时。
• eric-p7宣传了自己的轻量级库Solarite，该库为原生web组件添加了反应性和本地样式。
• manchmalscott提到Phoenix LiveView也能解决类似问题，通过web socket发送轻量级事件消息，服务器只响应新的HTML。
• librasteve对HTMX带来的多语言服务器端开发机会表示赞赏，并提到了多个相关项目。
• AndrewKemendo表示对HTMX感兴趣，但承认对新框架缺乏了解，希望看到一些值得注意的例子。
• Finnucane质疑HTMX带来的用户体验是否真的更快，认为许多JS密集型网站也感觉缓慢笨拙。
• chistev建议如果用vanilla JS太麻烦，可以直接使用Svelte。
• ranger_danger指出HTMX缺乏自动解析JSON响应的功能，建议增加类似"hx-source"的属性以简化开发。
• MountainMan1312正在尝试将HTMX用于个人网站，结合知识库和版本控制功能，但对具体实现方式还在探索中。
• hungryhobbit认为HTMX像是一个寻找问题的解决方案，暗示其并非对所有项目都适用。

补充讨论：
• HTMX的优缺点：简化了网络交互，但可能缺乏一些现代功能。
• 其他类似解决方案：如Datastar和Phoenix LiveView，提供了不同的实现方式和功能。
• 新框架和技术的不断出现：反映了开发社区对浏览器和JS现状的不满，以及对更现代化、更高效解决方案的追求。
• 实际应用中的需求和挑战：如自动解析JSON响应的功能需求，以及在具体项目中的实用性探索。

(disclosures)
I build
a lot of side projects
so I'm always on the lookout for technologies and paradigms that allow me to build them faster and cheaper at a similar quality. For the last several months I've been experimenting with building web apps with
low-js tools like HTMX and Alpine
.
In this post I'll share why I think HTMX is a great choice for building web apps faster and cheaper and why it's now a core part of my tech stack -
The HAM Stack
.
MPA vs SPA
Multi-Page Apps (MPA)
In the beginning we had Multi-Page Apps (MPA).
Each URL goes to a web page
This web-page is rendered server-side and sent back to the user
If you need to update something on the page (because a user changes something or it needs to refresh) then the full page needs to reload
This works fine but it gives a very slow / clunky feel because you need to reload EVERYTHING any time one thing on the page changes. For an example of this - think of a State government website, most of those are still old-school MPAs and they feel old and clunky compared to most modern apps.
MPA Pros and Cons
Pros: Simple to build
Cons: Feels slow and clunky due to refreshes
Single-Page Apps (SPA)
To solve this, Single-Page Apps (SPA) were created.
A URL loads a large JS payload containing a bunch of app logic
This JS takes over page rendering
It uses internal state to determine what the page should look like and does data transfers behind the scenes so it only needs to update the parts of the page that need to change
This feels better to the user because changes feel faster. The page only updates where it needs to and we don't need a full page refresh to change data. Most apps / websites today feel like this because it generally provides a better user experience.
Pros: Rich "modern" user experiences
Cons: Complex at scale - dealing w data transfers (graphQL was built for this), abstractions, and app logic payload sizes
So in general:
Multi-Page Apps (MPA)
- Simple to build but hard to get rich "modern" user experiences
Single-Page Apps (SPA)
- Complex to build but can achieve rich "modern" user experiences
MPA vs HTMX vs SPA
Image inspiration from
u/Abhilash26 on r/htmx
.
HTMX has been around for several years but has really gained mass hype in the past year or so. The hype is not unfounded - it often allows you to
build modern web apps faster and cheaper than a SPA
.
HTMX essentially extends HTML so that it can do partial page reloads.
Any element can specify how it can retrieve up-to-date data and when it should do that
The element can then specify what to do with the new data - replacing itself or other elements on the page
If we look back at the MPA vs SPA comparison, we can see that the lack of partial page reloads is really the main thing holding MPAs back. So adding this capability into an MPA largely allows you to get most of the rich "modern" user experiences of a SPA with the complexity level of an MPA.
HTMX for Side Projects
The goal of a side project is often just to build the thing. You likely don't have a team of engineers or warchest of VC-money to do so - it's just you and your computer.
So lowering the cost of building - in time and money - is crucial to making a side project successful.
From my perspective, HTMX provides a great balance between allowing you to build modern apps with very low complexity (and thus time and money cost). Thus it's become a core part of my tech stack -
the HAM Stack
.

Simple Interactive Islands with F# and HTMX

44615703.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何在侧边项目中选择HTMX而非传统的MPA或复杂的SPA。HTMX通过允许部分页面重载，使多页应用（MPA）具备类似单页应用（SPA）的现代用户体验，同时保持较低的开发复杂度和成本。MPA简单但因全页面刷新而显得笨重，SPA则能提供流畅的体验但开发复杂。HTMX作为一种低复杂度工具，帮助开发者快速、经济地构建现代 web 应用，已成为作者技术栈（HAM Stack）的核心部分。对于个人开发者而言，HTMX能有效降低时间和金钱成本，是侧边项目的理想选择。

• 其他类似解决方案：如Datastar和Phoenix LiveView，提供了不同的实现方式和功能。
• 新框架和技术的不断出现：反映了开发社区对浏览器和JS现状的不满，以及对更现代化、更高效解决方案的追求。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Maps等平台上的信息不准确问题及其背后的技术与管理难题

不同观点：
• abathur认为Google Maps上的商家描述不准确，例如某家本地酒吧的描述中提到的多项设施和提供的食物饮料并不存在。尽管已经有人反馈，但问题仍未解决。这导致了一些顾客的负面体验，如想要玩桌球或飞镖的顾客感到失望。
• jwr支持abathur的观点，并指出这不仅是信息概述的问题，而是Google整体的信息管理问题。他分享了自己多年与Google Maps错误信息斗争的经历，认为Google对反馈的响应不积极，且由于其规模庞大，可能并不重视这些不一致问题。
• jh00ker则关注当相关讨论被索引后可能带来的影响，提到"Dave Barry去世但仍在辩驳"的例子，暗示信息错误可能会引发更大的误解。
• ilaksh从技术角度分析了问题的原因，认为部分错误源于名称的混淆，尤其是当多个同名人物存在时。他建议通过增加默认问题（如"其他同名人物"）来改善，并讨论了Google知识图谱的潜在应用问题。
• ChrisMarshallNY表示对Google纠正错误不乐观，但赞赏Dave Barry的幽默回应，同时提到自己对Google长期存在的问题也有类似体验。
• rapind和ciconia的评论较为简短，前者提到AI生成内容可能导致诽谤问题，后者则用讽刺的方式表达对AI交流能力的失望。
• yalogin分享了与Meta AI互动的负面体验，指出一旦AI开始“幻觉”生成错误信息，就很难纠正。
• zaptrem和_ache_的评论则引发了对"Dave Barry"身份的幽默讨论，zaptrem提到另一个同名人物的死亡事件，而_ache_则用讽刺方式建议重新咨询医生。
• h2zizzle对Dave Barry表示支持，并表达了对当前AI和Google产品的不满，认为它们经常扭曲现实，且问题难以解决。
• devinplatt提到Wikipedia在敏感话题上的特别政策，暗示Google等平台可以从中学习管理经验。
• foobarbecue则以讽刺的方式建议只在不重要的事实任务中使用AI，如写推荐信或制定政策。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Google等平台信息不准确且难以修正的问题，用户反馈常常被忽视，导致错误信息长期存在。
• 技术上的讨论涉及AI生成内容的可靠性、名称混淆问题以及知识图谱的应用潜力。
• 评论中还提到了AI“幻觉”问题，即AI生成不准确或错误的信息且难以纠正，用户对此表示强烈不满。
• 部分评论带有幽默和讽刺性质，但也反映了用户对AI和大型科技公司产品现状的深刻不满。

data.title: MIPS: The hyperactive history and legacy of the pioneering RISC architecture
data.author: rob_lh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MIPS架构的历史、技术特点、衰落原因及其与竞争架构的比较

不同观点：
• **MIPS的成功与失败**：brucehoult认为MIPS在游戏机、网络设备和超级计算机等多个领域取得了显著成功，但最终由于SGI转向Itanium而放弃MIPS，导致其衰落。这表明MIPS的技术实力和市场潜力，但管理决策失误是其失败的主要原因。

• **MIPS架构的优点与缺点**：brucehoult指出MIPS架构设计经典且具有持久的价值，但也存在一些技术上的不足，例如延迟槽和条件分支需要多条指令，这相对于一些现代ISA（如ARM）显得不够高效。

• **MIPS与ARM的竞争**：brucehoult提到MIPS在引入混合指令集（如MIPS16和microMIPS）方面落后于ARM，总是处于跟随地位，缺乏领导力，这可能是其在与ARM竞争中失利的原因之一。

• **MIPS的未来与RISC-V的兴起**：brucehoult认为，设计和维护一个独立的ISA非常昂贵且困难，MIPS虽然推出了nanoMIPS，但为时已晚，无法与已经获得关注的RISC-V竞争。他希望MIPS的工程师能在RISC-V上取得成功。

补充讨论：
• **技术幽默与竞争**：DonHopkins分享了一个关于硬件设计师间的玩笑，提到MIPS可以支持大小端（SPIM），而SPARC的小端版本被戏称为CRAPS，这反映出当时技术人员之间的竞争和幽默文化。

争议焦点：
• **MIPS的衰落是由于技术原因还是管理决策**：brucehoult明确指出MIPS的衰落主要是因为SGI在Itanium上的错误决策，而不仅仅是因为技术上的不足。这暗示了管理决策在技术产品成败中的关键作用。

data.title: Hungary's oldest library is fighting to save books from a beetle infestation
data.author: smollett
data.article_summary: 匈牙利最古老的潘诺恩哈尔马修道院图书馆正努力拯救约10万本手抄书，这些书受到甲虫侵扰。药店甲虫（也称面包甲虫）不仅出现在食物中，还被书籍的胶水和淀粉吸引。为消灭甲虫，修复人员将书籍放入密封塑料袋，抽空氧气，注入氮气，经过六周处理希望彻底消灭甲虫。处理后，每本书将逐一检查和吸尘，受损书籍将进行后续修复。虽然最古老和珍稀的书未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图书馆中未扫描和未翻译书籍的保存及昆虫侵害问题

不同观点：
• [dr_dshiv] 认为应该有一个追踪器来显示世界上所有未扫描和未翻译的书籍，特别是新拉丁语书籍中只有不到10%被翻译，这令人惊讶。
• [bob1029] 提出控制湿度是防止昆虫滋生的有效方法，建议将相对湿度保持在50%以下，以抑制生物在干燥空间中繁殖。
• [Iryna77] 描述了图书馆中严重的昆虫侵害问题，提到整个藏书需要同时处理，且一些古老书籍需要通过缺氧环境来处理，但对处理结果持怀疑态度。
• [maxloh] 认为虽然保存原件很重要，但扫描书籍可以减轻很多风险，暗示数字化可能是解决方案之一。
• [funnym0nk3y] 对使用温和的昆虫消灭方法感到惊讶，原本预期会使用大量的杀虫剂。

补充讨论：
• [ChrisArchitect] 提供了一个相关讨论的链接，引导至其他平台上的进一步讨论。
• [mdavid626] 的问题似乎与讨论主题无关，询问是否有匈牙利人。
• [EGreg] 提供了一个与讨论无关的链接，内容似乎是一个不相关的主题。

争议焦点：
• 对待图书馆昆虫侵害的处理方法存在不同看法，[Iryna77] 对缺氧处理方法的效果表示怀疑，而 [funnym0nk3y] 则对没有使用强力杀虫剂感到意外。
• 关于书籍保存的最佳方法，[dr_dshiv] 强调未翻译书籍的问题，[maxloh] 则强调数字化作为解决方案的潜力。

44583316.article_content:
Hungarian library is fighting to save books from beetles
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles.
Europe
Hungary's oldest library is fighting to save 100,000 books from a beetle infestation
July 14, 2025
1:24 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Books are kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky/AP
hide caption
toggle caption
Bela Szandelszky/AP
PANNONHALMA, Hungary — Tens of thousands of centuries-old books are being pulled from the shelves of a medieval abbey in Hungary in an effort to save them from a beetle infestation that could wipe out centuries of history.
Books We Love
NPR staffers pick their favorite fiction reads of 2025 so far
The 1,000-year-old Pannonhalma Archabbey is a sprawling Benedictine monastery that is one of Hungary's oldest centers of learning and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles burrowed into them.
The drugstore beetle, also known as the bread beetle, is often found among dried foodstuffs like grains, flour and spices. But they also are attracted to the gelatin and starch-based adhesives found in books.
Sponsor Message
They have been found in a section of the library housing around a quarter of the abbey's 400,000 volumes.
"This is an advanced insect infestation which has been detected in several parts of the library, so the entire collection is classified as infected and must be treated all at the same time," said Zsófia Edit Hajdu, the chief restorer on the project. "We've never encountered such a degree of infection before."
Abbey houses historical treasures
The beetle invasion was first detected during a routine library cleaning. Employees noticed unusual layers of dust on the shelves and then saw that holes had been burrowed into some of the book spines. Upon opening the volumes, burrow holes could be seen in the paper where the beetles chewed through.
The abbey at Pannonhalma was founded in 996, four years before the establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary. Sitting upon a tall hill in northwestern Hungary, the abbey houses the country's oldest collection of books, as well as many of its earliest and most important written records.
In this photo provided by Pannonhalma Archabbey, a restorer shows an old book with holes in its pages due to a drugstore beetle infestation, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3.
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
hide caption
toggle caption
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
For over 1,000 years, the abbey has been among the most prominent religious and cultural sites in Hungary and all of Central Europe, surviving centuries of wars and foreign incursions such as the Ottoman invasion and occupation of Hungary in the 16th century.
Sponsor Message
Ilona Ásványi, director of the Pannonhalma Archabbey library, said she is "humbled" by the historical and cultural treasures the collection holds whenever she enters.
"It is dizzying to think that there was a library here a thousand years ago, and that we are the keepers of the first book catalogue in Hungary," she said.
Performing Arts
Take a peek at Stephen Sondheim's papers, now at the Library of Congress
Among the library's most outstanding works are 19 codices, including a complete Bible from the 13th century. It also houses several hundred manuscripts predating the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century and tens of thousands of books from the 16th century.
While the oldest and rarest prints and books are stored separately and have not been infected, Ásványi said any damage to the collection represents a blow to cultural, historical and religious heritage.
"When I see a book chewed up by a beetle or infected in any other way, I feel that no matter how many copies are published and how replaceable the book is, a piece of culture has been lost," she said.
Books will spend weeks in an oxygen-free environment
To kill the beetles, the crates of books are being placed into tall, hermetically sealed plastic sacks from which all oxygen is removed. After six weeks in the pure nitrogen environment, the abbey hopes all the beetles will be destroyed.
Before being reshelved, each book will be individually inspected and vacuumed. Any book damaged by the pests will be set aside for later restoration work.

Engineers have created a new type of
robot
that places living fungi behind the controls.
The
biohybrid robot
uses electrical signals from an edible type of mushroom called a king trumpet in order to move around and sense its environment.
Developed by an interdisciplinary team from Cornell University in the US and Florence University in Italy, the machine could herald a new era of living robotics.
“Living systems respond to touch, they respond to light, they respond to heat, they respond to even some unknowns, like signals,” said Anand Mishra, a research associate in the Organic Robotics Lab at Cornell.
“That’s why we think, OK, if you wanted to build future
robots
, how can they work in an unexpected environment? We can leverage these living systems, and any unknown input comes in, the robot will respond to that.”
Researchers from Cornell University in the US and the University of Florence in Italy placed a species of edible mushroom within a robot body
(
Robert Shepherd
)
Different inputs, such as ultraviolet light, resulted in different outcomes for the way the robot moved. A video of one of the mushroom-controlled robots shows it moving slowly across a surface by pumping its robotic legs. Another biohybrid robot uses a wheeled system in order to move around.
Combining this mobility with the fungi’s ability to sense chemical and biological signals could prove useful in a range of applications, according to the researchers.
“By growing mycelium into the electronics of a robot, we were able to allow the biohybrid machine to sense and respond to the environment,” said Rob Shepherd, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at Cornell.
“The potential for future robots could be to sense soil chemistry in row crops and decide when to add more fertiliser, for example, perhaps mitigating downstream effects of agriculture like harmful algal blooms.”
Details of the biohybrid robot were published in the journal
Science Robotics
, in
a study
titled ‘Sensorimotor control of robots mediated by electro-physiological measurements of fungal mycelia’.
It is not the first time a living organism has been placed inside a robot body, though the use of mushrooms could offer a major breakthrough in the field of biohybrid robotics due to their ability to grow and survive in harsh conditions.
Previous experiments have included
an artificial worm brain placed inside a Lego robot
, which was able to recreate the creature’s movements and intentions.
Earlier this year, researchers from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) created a machine that was integrated with living muscle tissue in order to sense and adapt to its environment.

data.title: Intel to boost gross margins – new products must deliver 50% gross profit
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: Intel宣布将不再批准毛利率低于50%的新项目，以重振其利润率。CEO Lip-Bu Tan正推动公司毛利率重回50%以上，取消或调整不盈利项目，并可能进行多达20%的裁员。尽管公司整体尚未达到该目标，但未来项目如Panther Lake和Nova Lake预计将实现这一利润率。此举旨在提高盈利能力，但也引发内部对产品竞争力与成本结构的争论。Tan还计划通过裁减中层管理层和投资顶尖人才来重塑公司文化。这一策略获得投资者支持，但执行中面临挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel的战略调整及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论者对Intel专注于高利润项目表示怀疑，认为这种策略可能导致创新能力下降。例如，[0cf8612b2e1e]提到这种策略可能意味着所有实验性的研发都将被排除，只有渐进式的进步才能带来利润。[Arnt]和[tracerbulletx]通过讽刺的方式表达了类似的担忧，指出高层可能过于乐观，而现实往往不如预期。

• 部分评论关注Intel领导层变动及其影响。[bilbyx]对Intel董事会过早让Pat Gelsinger离职表示不解，并质疑Lip-Bu Tan是否是更好的选择。此外，[tchbnl]对Intel在现任领导下的未来表示悲观，甚至猜测可能会有公司收购Intel。

• 一些评论者讨论了Intel的利润策略是否意味着市场重心的转移。[ThrowawayR2]提出Intel是否会因此减少对消费级PC市场的关注，转而更多地投向服务器和企业产品。[ksec]则指出Intel在服务器市场面临AMD的激烈竞争，并认为AMD需要在各个市场进一步增加市场份额。

• 其他评论关注Intel的行业地位和历史变化。[Animats]引用了Intel CEO的话，指出Intel已经不再是十大半导体公司之一，尽管其他来源将其列为第五。[bilbyx]将Intel的现状与波音公司进行比较，认为两者都过于关注股东价值而忽视了其他重要方面。

• 还有评论讨论了Intel的人才策略。[light_hue_1]质疑Intel是否会通过提高薪酬和改善待遇来吸引和保留顶尖人才，特别是在与FAANG公司竞争的背景下。[wolpoli]则认为Intel出售其ARM CPU产品线的决策是这种短视思维的产物。

补充讨论：
• 部分评论者对新闻报道的实际内容和价值提出质疑。[roenxi]认为文章并没有提供实质性的新信息，只是重申了Intel CEO希望公司盈利并优先考虑高利润产品的常见策略。

• 一些评论通过对比其他公司的历史案例来分析Intel的现状。[cjbgkagh]将Intel的策略与Marissa Mayer在雅虎时期的做法相比较，认为这可能反映出公司在面临竞争压力时的无奈选择。

争议焦点：
• Intel新策略是否会导致创新能力的下降以及市场竞争力的削弱是主要争议点。部分评论者担心过度关注利润和高利润项目可能损害公司的长远发展，而其他评论者则认为这种调整是必要的以应对当前的市场环境。

44620774.article_content:
(Image credit: Intel)
Intel will not be entertaining any projects that do not promise to double its money going forward. Michelle Johnston Holthaus, CEO of Intel Products, announced at Bank of America's
global technology conference
that Intel is no longer approving new projects that cannot be proven to earn at least 50% gross margin "based on a set of industry expectations."
Holthaus explained Intel's new risk-averse policy as "something that we probably should have had before, but we have it now so that product doesn’t move forward; you actually don’t get engineers assigned to it if it’s not 50% or higher gross margins moving forward."
Holthaus also clarified that while Intel is not expecting or projecting 50% gross margins across all operations, it is a number the company is aspiring toward internally. All of Intel's future roadmap operations, including
Panther Lake
and
Nova Lake
, are also currently expected to reach the 50% gross profit number that the rest of the business aspires to.

The drive behind this initiative is reportedly coming from Intel's
new CEO
, Lip-Bu Tan. Tan is reportedly "laser focused on the fact that we need to get our gross margins back up above 50%." To accomplish this, Tan is also said to be investigating and potentially cancelling or changing unprofitable deals with other companies.
Intel's margins have slipped to new lows for the company in recent months.
MacroTrends
reports Intel's trailing 12 months gross margin for Q1 2025 was as low as 31.67%. Intel's gross margins had hovered around the 60% mark for the ten years leading up to the COVID-19 pandemic, falling beneath 50% in Q2 2022 and continuing to steadily fall ever since.
Holthaus predicts a "tug-of-war" to ensue within Intel in the coming months as engineers and executives reckon with being forced between a rock and a hard place. "We need to be building products that... fit the right competitive landscape and requirements of our customers, but also have the right cost structure in place. It really requires us to do both."
CEO Lip-Bu Tan has done much to streamline Intel's operation and right a rocking ship inherited from previous Intel chief Pat Gelsinger. Another
major round of layoffs
, potentially up to 20% of the remaining workforce, is coming in Q2, arriving after a major leadership change-up to remove middle management between Tan and other team leads.

Tan is also quoted as wanting to turn Intel into an "engineering-focused company" again under his leadership. To reach this, Tan has committed to investing in recruiting and retaining top talent; "I believe Intel has lost some of this talent over the years; I want to create a culture of innovation empowerment." Maintaining a culture of empowering innovation and top talent seems, on its face, at odds with layoffs and a lock on projects not projected to gross 50% margins, but Tan seemingly has Intel investors on his side in these pursuits.

44620774.article_summary: Intel宣布将不再批准毛利率低于50%的新项目，以重振其利润率。CEO Lip-Bu Tan正推动公司毛利率重回50%以上，取消或调整不盈利项目，并可能进行多达20%的裁员。尽管公司整体尚未达到该目标，但未来项目如Panther Lake和Nova Lake预计将实现这一利润率。此举旨在提高盈利能力，但也引发内部对产品竞争力与成本结构的争论。Tan还计划通过裁减中层管理层和投资顶尖人才来重塑公司文化。这一策略获得投资者支持，但执行中面临挑战。
44620774.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel的战略调整及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论者对Intel专注于高利润项目表示怀疑，认为这种策略可能导致创新能力下降。例如，[0cf8612b2e1e]提到这种策略可能意味着所有实验性的研发都将被排除，只有渐进式的进步才能带来利润。[Arnt]和[tracerbulletx]通过讽刺的方式表达了类似的担忧，指出高层可能过于乐观，而现实往往不如预期。

• 部分评论关注Intel领导层变动及其影响。[bilbyx]对Intel董事会过早让Pat Gelsinger离职表示不解，并质疑Lip-Bu Tan是否是更好的选择。此外，[tchbnl]对Intel在现任领导下的未来表示悲观，甚至猜测可能会有公司收购Intel。

• 一些评论者讨论了Intel的利润策略是否意味着市场重心的转移。[ThrowawayR2]提出Intel是否会因此减少对消费级PC市场的关注，转而更多地投向服务器和企业产品。[ksec]则指出Intel在服务器市场面临AMD的激烈竞争，并认为AMD需要在各个市场进一步增加市场份额。

• 其他评论关注Intel的行业地位和历史变化。[Animats]引用了Intel CEO的话，指出Intel已经不再是十大半导体公司之一，尽管其他来源将其列为第五。[bilbyx]将Intel的现状与波音公司进行比较，认为两者都过于关注股东价值而忽视了其他重要方面。

• 还有评论讨论了Intel的人才策略。[light_hue_1]质疑Intel是否会通过提高薪酬和改善待遇来吸引和保留顶尖人才，特别是在与FAANG公司竞争的背景下。[wolpoli]则认为Intel出售其ARM CPU产品线的决策是这种短视思维的产物。

补充讨论：
• 部分评论者对新闻报道的实际内容和价值提出质疑。[roenxi]认为文章并没有提供实质性的新信息，只是重申了Intel CEO希望公司盈利并优先考虑高利润产品的常见策略。

• 一些评论通过对比其他公司的历史案例来分析Intel的现状。[cjbgkagh]将Intel的策略与Marissa Mayer在雅虎时期的做法相比较，认为这可能反映出公司在面临竞争压力时的无奈选择。

争议焦点：
• Intel新策略是否会导致创新能力的下降以及市场竞争力的削弱是主要争议点。部分评论者担心过度关注利润和高利润项目可能损害公司的长远发展，而其他评论者则认为这种调整是必要的以应对当前的市场环境。

data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为YouTube已经形成了一种事实上的垄断，因为内容创作者聚集在YouTube上，以获取流量和广告收入。这种循环使得其他替代平台难以打破YouTube的主导地位，类似于eBay的情况。
• ksec指出，传统电视广播的内容在流媒体服务中没有得到很好的整合，本应由Apple或Google来推动这种整合，但由于各自的商业利益，他们并没有这样做。ksec还批评了Apple和Google在产品创新上的缺失，认为他们在Steve Jobs去世后缺乏对客户需求的关注，产品多由营销和销售驱动。

• al_borland提到其大多数YouTube观看行为是通过AppleTV进行的，暗示了跨平台体验的重要性。
• consumer451指出YouTube在音乐流媒体领域也处于领先地位，这一现象出乎其意料，进一步强调了YouTube的多功能性和广泛影响力。

data.title: I tried vibe coding in BASIC and it didn't go well
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
作者Paul Lefebvre尝试了使用AI进行“氛围编码”（vibe coding）来编写BASIC程序，但结果并不理想。氛围编码依赖AI生成代码，通过对话逐步完善。尽管AI在查找文档和提供思路方面表现出色，但生成的代码往往需要手动调整才能正常工作。作者选择使用Atari BASIC而非微软BASIC变种进行实验，并通过Atari800MacX模拟器测试代码。

初始简单的"Hello, World"程序成功运行，但绘制圆圈的程序需要多次修正才能准确显示。在尝试创建更复杂的绘图程序时，AI生成的代码包含多个错误，例如变量名和注释符号的使用不当。尽管AI可以最终修正这些问题，但作者认为手动编码仍更为可靠和高效。总的来说，实验表明AI在辅助编码方面有一定价值，但完全依赖其生成代码仍存在挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程任务中的表现及其局限性，特别是在"Vibe Coding"（依赖感觉和模糊提示的编程方式）中的应用。

不同观点：
• nine_k和edent认为LLM像一只“聪明的狗”，可以在某些情况下表现出色，但它们仍然是依赖训练数据的“预测机器”。如果期望过高，容易看到其局限性。nine_k特别强调了对LLM的期望决定了对其表现的评价。
• manca和recipe19则持批评态度，认为LLM在处理复杂或新颖任务时表现不佳，特别是在代码转换任务中，往往需要大量的调试，表明它们仍然是“愚蠢的预测机器”。
• ofrzeta和Radle持相对乐观的态度，认为只要提供足够的文档和上下文信息，LLM可以表现出色，并指出文章中失败的例子可能是因为缺乏这些信息。
• xiphias2对讨论的文章持怀疑态度，认为GPT-4o并非为编码设计，质疑文章受到高关注的原因。
• Yokolos提供了一种实用的方法，建议在遇到问题时重启对话以避免AI迷失方向。
• danjc提出LLM在工具使用上的不足，认为如果LLM能够使用编译工具和运行程序来捕捉错误，表现会更好。
• ilaksh强调了不同语言模型之间的差异，建议使用更大的上下文窗口和外部文档来辅助LLM。
• fcatalan分享了一个成功的实验，通过图片转换BASIC代码为C代码，并成功运行，显示了LLM在特定任务中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• Earw0rm和serf关注了特定编程语言（如x87汇编语言）的复杂性，以及提示的精确性对LLM表现的影响，指出LLM在处理需要强逻辑推理的任务中可能表现不佳。
• firesteelrain建议使用本地LLM并进行训练，以提高在特定任务中的表现。

争议焦点：
• LLM在编程任务中的实际能力和局限性。乐观者认为提供足够信息可以提高其表现，批评者则强调其在处理新颖和复杂任务时的不足。
• 对GPT-4o等模型在编码任务中的适用性的不同看法。

总体来看，讨论围绕LLM的能力和局限性展开，反映了不同用户在实际应用中的多样化体验和观点。

With the rise of LLM systems (or “AI” as they are annoyingly called), the term “
vibe coding
” is all the rage recently. Vibe coding is when you rely almost entirely on these “AI” system to write your code for you via a series of drawn-out conversations.
Putting on my cranky old man hat, I find most of it rather frustrating. Now I’m not some retro-sycophant who refuses to use modern tools. I’ve been a software professional for over 30 years at this point and I’ve used lots of tools throughout the years. Many that were cool and hip have long since disappeared or fallen out of fashion. I’ve also actually used these AI systems myself to help figure out some code. I find they function really well as a better search engine for documentation and can also serve as a way to “rubber duck” ideas and get some outlines. Any code I get back rarely seems to work as-is, but it often can provide ideas for something I hadn’t considered or perhaps point out something I did not know about.
After all, today’s technology is complex and it is not always easy to find what you need in the documentation.
But how does vibe coding work with something far simpler, such as the simplest programming language of them all: BASIC?
I suspect this might be a little tricker than it first appears. First of all, usage of BASIC largely predates the internet so there is far less BASIC code out there for LLMs to learn from. Many online retro BASIC books and docs are often scanned copies rather than easily digested plain text. Also, BASIC is not a single language, but more of an umbrella term for a family of languages all of which have the same “vibe”
1
, but often very different commands and capabilities, some of which rely heavily on PEEKs and POKEs to really take advantage of their system’s features
2
. And those ancient forms of API calls are poorly documented online.
So this should be an interesting challenge and to make it even slightly trickier, I’m going to use Atari BASIC rather than a much more common Microsoft BASIC variant, such as AppleSoft. Why? Because this is an Atari newsletter and I have plenty of Atari equipment to test things with. Alas, I don’t have any Apple II-era systems.
With that said, I will be using the
Atari800MacX emulator
because it makes it easy to paste in the generated code.
Now with all that out of the way, which LLM AI system should we try? Considering
ChatGPT
is the most commonly known and one most are familiar with, that’s I’m using for this experiment, although
Anthropic Claude
is also great for use with coding.
To do proper vibe coding, I need to refrain from correcting the generated code or even telling the AI what exactly is wrong.
Hello World
So what should be do first? Let’s start with a typical first BASIC program, the precursor to “Hello World”.
Prompt: Please write me a simple program in Atari BASIC that repeatedly prints “Hello, World” to the screen.
ChatGPT aced this simple test. I have to say, I do love seeing “GOTO 10” like that!
Draw a Circle
Atari BASIC does not have a built-in way to draw a circle so let’s ask for that:
Prompt: Write me an Atari BASIC program that draws a blue circle in graphics mode 7.
So far, the vibes are flowing. This program ran perfectly, although it only drew a rough, dotted circle.
I asked it for a solid outline instead of a dotted outline and it came back with this code:
10 GRAPHICS 7
20 COLOR 1
30 X=80:Y=48:R=30
40 A=0
50 X1=X+R*COS(A)
60 Y1=Y+R*SIN(A)
70 FOR A=0 TO 6.28 STEP .05
80 X2=X+R*COS(A)
90 Y2=Y+R*SIN(A)
100 DRAWTO X2,Y2
110 X1=X2:Y1=Y2
120 NEXT A
130 GOTO 130
That drew a solid outline using DRAWTO, but it did not set the starting position correctly.
It was able to fix things, however:
This new code draws correctly:
I then asked it to get rid of the blue bar at the bottom and it did that admirably by using GRAPHICS 7+16.
That all went well!
Create a Drawing Program
Continuing the graphics theme, let’s take it up a notch. Atari BASIC does have built-in commands for drawing lines and accessing the joystick, which are more than enough to make a simple drawing program.
Prompt: Write an Atari BASIC program that lets you draw on the screen using a joystick. It should use graphics mode 7 and allow you to rotate between colors by pressing the fire button.
The resulting code had several errors:
To use COLOR as a variable name, LET is required. The “;” is not used for comments in any version of BASIC I’ve ever seen.
Prompt: Line 30 shows this error: ERROR- COLOR=1. There are also errors on any lines that use ";" for a comment.
It fixed these errors by changing COLOR to just C and gettin

data.title: “Bypassing” specialization in Rust
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Rust中开发FAT文件系统驱动时遇到的特化（specialization）问题，以及如何通过函数指针解决该问题。Rust目前不支持稳定的特化功能，导致无法为只读和读写文件系统分别定义不同的`load_nth_sector`方法实现。作者尝试了多种方法，最终通过使用函数指针实现了类似特化的功能，从而绕开了这一限制。本文强调了在没有特化支持的情况下，如何利用其他Rust特性来实现相似的行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的特质（trait）特化及其相关问题，如重叠实例、生命周期处理等。

不同观点：
• [hackyhacky] 认为特质特化在此场景中并不合适，建议使用两种替代方案：将文件系统本身作为一个特质，通过不同实现来处理只读和读写情况；或者在文件系统对象中存储能力信息，并在运行时通过条件查询。这些方法可能更简洁和清晰。

• [maybevoid] 提出使用上下文泛型编程（CGP）来绕过一致性限制，通过提供者特质在安全的稳定Rust中实现重叠实现，并提供了一个概念验证实现链接。

• [ozgrakkurt] 建议使用特质对象，通过默认实现和特化来解决问题，认为这种方法比使用宏或增加泛型更简单，并且编译时间更好。

• [SkiFire13] 指出特化功能在处理生命周期时存在问题，特别是当某些类型根据生命周期实现特质时会导致特化不健全，这也是特化功能在稳定化过程中面临的主要障碍。

• [konstantinua00] 提出通过负特质（negative traits）来解决问题，认为可以通过定义负特质来避免特化时重叠检查的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对特质特化的争议主要集中在代码的清晰性、运行时行为、编译时间以及处理特化时出现的生命周期问题。
• 提出了多种替代方案，如使用特质对象、上下文泛型编程和负特质，展示了在Rust中解决特化问题的不同思路。
