data.title: Async I/O on Linux in databases
data.author: jtregunna
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在开发简单键值数据库过程中，对I/O性能优化的探索。最初使用内存哈希表和简单的追加日志实现持久化，但性能不佳。之后，作者转向研究Linux的io_uring机制，它通过共享环形缓冲区在应用与内核间实现真正的异步I/O，大幅提升吞吐量。然而，异步I/O导致数据持久性和一致性问题，作者通过引入双写前日志（WAL）设计解决该问题：一个记录操作意图（异步写入），另一个记录操作完成，只有两者齐备时才在恢复时应用操作，确保一致性。最终，作者使用Zig语言实现了该方案，并通过实验验证其性能和可靠性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：io_uring 与同步 API 的性能比较及其在数据库中的应用，特别是关于持久性（durability）和正确性的讨论。

不同观点：
• **quietbritishjim** 认为文章中比较的是有 fsync 调用和无 fsync 调用的性能，而不是同步 API 和 io_uring 的真正性能对比。他认为如果同步代码中去掉 fsync，也能获得类似的性能提升。此外，io_uring 也可以通过某些方法实现 fsync 的功能，因此文章的比较是不对等的。
• **jorangreef** 指出 TigerBeetle 始终使用 fsync 来保证持久性，并且他们的设计目标不是性能而是正确性。TigerBeetle 的双 WAL（写前日志）设计是为了协议感知的恢复，而不是简单的性能优化。
• **sethev** 认为文章中的逻辑有误，指出如果第4步（等待完成记录写入 WAL）正确执行，那么第3步（等待意图记录持久化）就是多余的。他怀疑第4步可能没有正确执行，导致误解。
• **jmpman** 担心如果系统崩溃后，客户端收到成功的请求可能没有对应的完成记录，这违反了 ACID 原则。
• **avinassh** 同意 jmpman 的观点，认为如果完成记录是异步的且可能未完成，那么服务器的持久性保证就会有问题。
• **tlb** 和 **BeeOnRope** 都质疑意图记录的必要性，认为如果只有完成记录是持久化的，那么单独记录意图记录似乎没有意义。
• **leentee** 认为文章中的方案不能保证持久性，并且认为好的同步代码比坏的异步代码更可取，尤其是对于现代 NVMe 存储而言，同步 IO 已经足够快。
• **lstroud** 分享了在 Linux raid 驱动中遇到的死锁问题，并通过移除 lvm 解决了吞吐量问题。
• **ptrwis** 提到目前只有一个人在为 PostgreSQL 实现异步直接 IO。
• **tobias3** 对双 WAL 操作比单个同步 IOPS 更快的说法表示怀疑，认为这可能意味着数据库根本没有持久性。
• **jtregunna** 在更新中澄清了需要等待完成记录写入后再响应客户端，并指出双 WAL 方法在批量处理时有优势，但在接近单次写入时成本更高。
• **ozgrakkurt** 分享了自己实现 crash-resilient LSM 树的经验，并好奇双 WAL 方法与 append/rename 方法的 trade-off。
• **eatonphil** 提到目前似乎没有很多数据库在生产环境中默认使用 io_uring，并希望有人能做这样一个调查。
• **jasonthorsness** 质疑 NVME 存储接口是否应该比 Linux 抽象层更简洁，并提出某些高性能应用可能更适合作为特殊用途的 unikernels。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章中比较的合理性和持久性保证，特别是 fsync 在异步和同步代码中的作用。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是双 WAL 设计的必要性和意图记录的作用。
• 一些评论者分享了实际操作中的经验和解决方案，比如 lstroud 的死锁问题和 ozgrakkurt 的 crash-resilient 方法。
• 还有评论者对 io_uring 在生产环境中的使用情况表示关注，并希望有更多调查和数据。

44622454.article_content:
I've been working on a complex multi-model database for a few weeks now, and recently I took time to simplify and test out an idea I had on a simple key-value database. I started with the basics: A hash table in memory, a simple append-only log for persistence and durability, and the classic fsync() call after every write to the log for durability.
It worked, but wasn't as fast as it could be.
In
Kevo
, that's the approach I use, but in Klay (not public yet, but will be open sourced when ready), I'm taking a different approach. What would a database look like if you treated the individual sectors on disk as unreliable, and how could you make it as fast as possible?
That's when I started reading about io_uring on Linux
here (PDF)
and
here
.
io_uring... what?
You can read
Wikipedia
as good as the next person, so let's skip ahead.
The promises seem to good to be true: truly async I/O for all types of operations, not just network sockets. No more thread pools to work around blocking disk I/O, no more complex state machines built around
epoll
... What's the catch?
Well, after doing some reading, the core insight behind io_uring clicked almost immediately. Traditional I/O interfaces force you to think synchronously--you make a system call, the kernel does work, you get a result. But modern storage hardware is inherently parallel. An NVMe SSD can handle thousands of operations simultaneously, and together, each with its own queue. The bottleneck isn't the hardware; it's the software abstraction.
io_uring exposes this parallelism through a pair of ring buffers shared between your application and the kernel. You submit operations to the submission queue (SQ) and collect results from the completion queue (CQ). Instead of one system call per operation, you can submit dozens of operations with a single
io_uring_submit
call.
My first io_uring experiment was simple: Replace my synchronous WAL writes with async ones. Instead of writing each log entry and waiting for completion, I would submit the write operation and continue processing. The results were dramatic--throughput increased by an order of magnitude almost immediately.
But then I started hitting consistency issues...
Durability
The problem with naive async I/O in a database context at least, is that you lose the durability guarantee that makes databases useful. When a client receives a success response, their expectation is the data will survive a system crash. But with async I/O, by the time you send that response, the data might still be sitting in kernel buffers, not yet written to stable storage.
My initial solution was to track pending I/O operations and only return success after the corresponding completion arrived from io_uring. This worked, but it defeated the purpose--I was back to waiting for disk I/O before completing transactions.
Clearly, I need a better approach.
Rethinking my WAL
The traditional
write-ahead log
(WAL) protocol is simple: log the change, force it to disk, then apply it. But what if we could separate the "intent to change" from the "confirmation of the change"? What if we could log our intentions quickly and asynchronously, then confirm completion separately?
That led me to a
TigerBeetle talk
being given by Joran Dirk Greef. Turns out, TigerBeetle uses the same sort of approach. The more I learned about TigerBeetle, the more I had confidence in the approach. (Note: TigerBeetle doesn't externalize commits asynchronously though, see clarification in
this X post
.)
So I set out to experiment with a dual WAL design, in a simple in-memory key-value database, that used the dual WAL design:
Intent WAL
: Records what operations I plan to perform
Completion WAL
: Records successful completion of these operations
So the protocol ends up becoming:
Write intent record (async)
Perform operation in memory
Write completion record (async)
Return success to client
During recovery, I only apply operations that have both intent and completion records. This ensures consistency while allowing much higher throughput.
Building the Dual WAL System
Alright, I'm also using Zig for this, since Klay is being written in Zig, I kept
Poro (GitHub)
using Zig as well to reduce the things I needed to keep in my head at once. In case it's not obvious, and it may not be, Poro is the experimental key-value database with the dual WAL system implemented as a demo.
Implementing this approach requires attention to several details. First, I need to separate io_uring instances--one for each WAL type. This prevents head-of-line blocking where completion writes might wait behind intent writes.
pub const WAL = struct {
intent_ring: io_uring,              // Dedicated ring for intent ops
completion_ring: io_uring,          // Dedicated ring for completions
intent_file_fd: std.posix.fd_t,
completion_file_fd: std.posix.fd_t,
intent_buffer: []u8,                // Circular buffer
completion_buffer: []u8,            // Circular buffer
};
The circular buffers are crucial for performanc

Self-Serve Invite Link Feature —
Fixes
#348
This feature enables admins to generate an invite link for contractors
Admin Flow
Generate Invite Link
Navigate to the
People
page. Click on the
Invite Link
button.
Generate or Reset Invite Link
Confirm the reset in the dialog.
Contractor Flow
Open Invite Link
The contractor opens the provided invite link in their browser.
Authentication
If not already signed in, clicking
Accept Invite
redirects the contractor to the signup/login page.
Onboarding
After authenticating, the contractor is guided through the initial onboarding steps.
Document Upload
Once onboarding is complete, the user is redirected to the document upload page to continue the process.
Confirmation
After submitting required documents, the contractor sees a confirmation screen indicating successful onboarding.
Approach
1. Invite Link Model
A dedicated model stores invite tokens, along with the inviter, company, and an optional document template ID.
This enables tracking and management of invitations independently from users.
2. Invite Link Usage Scenarios
When a user opens an invite link, two scenarios are handled:
a) Unauthenticated User:
The user is redirected to the sign-up flow.
The
invitation_token
is stored in a cookie for later use.
b) Authenticated User:
The invite accept API is called immediately.
A
company_worker
entry is created for the current user, and the company context is switched.
3. Invite Acceptance and Onboarding
For unauthenticated users:
After sign-up, the system detects the
invitation_token
and uses it to create a
company_worker
entry using the
AcceptInviteLink
service
For authenticated users:
The invite is accepted directly, and the
company_worker
entry is created.
4. Incomplete Contractor Profile
The initial
company_worker
instance created from an invite is incomplete (missing role, rates, etc.).
The user is required to complete onboarding by filling out a modal form with these details.
5. Contract Creation (if applicable)
If the invite includes a document template, a contract is generated once the onboarding form is completed.
6. Completion
After onboarding, the contractor’s profile is complete, and they can access all relevant features and actions within the company workspace.
Demo
Self.Serve.Link.Flow.1.mp4
Summary by CodeRabbit
New Features
Introduced contractor invite links, allowing company administrators to generate, copy, and reset invitation links for onboarding contractors.
Added a modal interface for managing contractor invite links, including contract options and template selection.
Enabled contractors to join a company via invite links, supporting both authenticated and unauthenticated flows.
Implemented a two-step onboarding process for contractors joining via invite links.
Added invite link verification and acceptance endpoints, with relevant UI feedback for invite status.
Improvements
Updated the People page to include both "Invite link" and "Add contractor" options.
Enhanced onboarding flows to support contractors without predefined roles.
Improved UI elements for buttons and dialogs for consistency and clarity.
Bug Fixes
Adjusted contractor listing to exclude workers without assigned roles.
Tests
Added comprehensive backend, frontend, and end-to-end tests covering invite link generation, acceptance, onboarding, and UI interactions.
Chores
Updated button labels from "Invite contractor" to "Add contractor" throughout the application and tests for consistency.

data.title: Show HN: MCP server for Blender that builds 3D scenes via natural language
data.author: prono
data.article_summary: Blender MCP（Model Context Protocol）是一个将大型语言模型（LLM）与Blender无缝整合的工具，通过简单的JSON指令让AI实时控制3D场景。它通过TCP连接实现，无需插件或手动操作，支持如Claude、ChatGPT等模型。Blender MCP使用轻量级的JSON协议，提供对3D场景、物体、材质和动画的全面控制，旨在简化AI驱动的3D创作流程。其架构包括TCP服务器、指令处理器和场景控制器。用户可以通过克隆GitHub仓库、配置Claude Desktop和安装Blender插件来设置MCP。该工具旨在让AI与人类创意无缝协作，实现自然语言和实时控制的结合。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• vunderba和WhatIsDukkha认为该项目的GitHub仓库内容空泛，仅为通用的MCP服务器，缺乏实际代码和功能实现。vunderba还提到该项目与ahujasid几个月前发布的blender-mcp项目相似，后者有完整的源代码并拥有一定关注度。

Blender
MCP
Turning AI into your creative Blender co-pilot.
Realtime 3D Control via Model Context Protocol
Watch
Demo
What is
Blender MCP
?
Blender MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a seamless integration layer that empowers Large Language Models (LLMs) to take control of Blender using simple JSON instructions. It turns AI into a real-time 3D collaborator—through a fast and open TCP-based connection.
Instant AI-to-3D Pipeline
Generate, modify, and animate Blender scenes in real time by connecting any LLM to the MCP server. No plugins, no manual clicks—just pure AI-driven creativity.
Lightweight JSON Protocol
Communicate using clean and structured JSON commands over TCP. Designed for reliability, simplicity, and extensibility—perfect for research and rapid prototyping.
Plug & Play with Any LLM
Easily hook up models like Claude, ChatGPT, or open-source LLMs to your Blender environment. Claude Desktop already supports direct MCP server input—just add your server and start building.
Scene Manipulation
Complete control over 3D scenes, objects, materials, and animations with precise command execution.
Total Scene Control
Create meshes, move objects, apply materials, trigger animations—Blender MCP gives the AI full access to manipulate your 3D world.
Why We Built Blender MCP
Blender MCP was created to establish a standardized, universal interface between Large Language Models and 3D software like Blender—making AI-powered 3D creation accessible, fast, and intuitive.
Whether you're a Blender pro looking to speed up complex workflows or a curious beginner
(like us when we started!)
trying to bring your ideas to life without wrestling with UI or scripting—
Blender MCP bridges that gap
.
We believe the future of 3D content lies in
natural language + real-time control
. This project makes that future usable today.
Project
Details
Code Architecture
TCP Server
Handles incoming connections and JSON command parsing
Command Processor
Translates JSON commands to Blender Python API calls
Scene Controller
Manages 3D scene state and object manipulation
Example JSON Payload
{
"command": "create_object",
"type": "cube",
"name": "my_cube",
"location": [0, 0, 0],
"scale": [1, 1, 1],
"material": {
"name": "blue_material",
"color": [0, 0, 1, 1]
}
}

Clone the Repository
git clone https://github.com/pranav-deshmukh/blender-mcp
cd blender-mcp-demo
pnpm i && node index.js
2
Claude Desktop Integration
Go to
Claude → Settings → Developer → Edit Config → claude_desktop_config.json
and add:
{
"mcpServers": {
"DemoServer": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["path to index.js file of cloned repo"]
}
}
}
3
Install Blender Addon
Open Blender →
Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → Install from Disk
Navigate to cloned repo →
addon
folder → Select
simple_mcp_addon.py
→ Click
Install from Disk
4
Start MCP Server in Blender
In Blender, go to the
right sidebar
→ Click on
MCP

Start MCP Server

Ready to Use!
Your Blender MCP setup is complete. You can now control Blender through Claude Desktop using natural language commands.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非侵入式脑机接口（BCI）的可行性及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• 观点1：对非侵入式BCI持怀疑态度。ACCount36认为，EEG（脑电图）作为非侵入式技术存在已有很长时间，但并未成为有效的界面系统，表明其局限性。
  - 论据：EEG技术长期存在但未能实现有用的接口功能。
  - 例子：EEG技术缺乏实际应用中的成功案例。

• 观点2：侵入式BCI是更可行的方向。ACCount36指出，像Neuralink N1这样完全侵入式的BCI，拥有超过1000个记录通道，虽然仅能提供勉强够用的控制界面，但仍是目前最先进的技术（SOTA）。
  - 论据：Neuralink N1的1000多个通道仅能提供基本可靠的控制，显示出现有技术的局限性。
  - 例子：Neuralink N1作为侵入式技术的代表，展示了当前技术的最高水平。

• 观点3：未来BCI的发展依赖于更具侵入性且通道数量更多的接口。ACCount36认为，更好的BCI发展路径在于增加通道数量和侵入性，而不是相反。
  - 论据：增加通道数量和侵入性可以提高BCI的性能。
  - 例子：目前SOTA的技术仍需更多通道和侵入性来实现更可靠的控制。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：非侵入式与侵入式BCI的技术路线选择。ACCount36明确支持侵入式技术，认为非侵入式技术如EEG不具备发展前景，而侵入式技术则是未来的方向。
• 技术现状：当前技术如Neuralink N1虽为最先进，但仍存在性能上的限制，显示出BCI技术整体仍处于发展初期。

总结：评论围绕非侵入式和侵入式BCI的可行性展开讨论，焦点在于技术路线的选择和未来发展方向，一方认为非侵入式技术缺乏实用性，另一方则看好侵入式技术的发展潜力。

• 观点1：对非侵入式BCI持怀疑态度。ACCount36认为，EEG（脑电图）作为非侵入式技术存在已有很长时间，但并未成为有效的界面系统，表明其局限性。
  - 论据：EEG技术长期存在但未能实现有用的接口功能。
  - 例子：EEG技术缺乏实际应用中的成功案例。

• 观点2：侵入式BCI是更可行的方向。ACCount36指出，像Neuralink N1这样完全侵入式的BCI，拥有超过1000个记录通道，虽然仅能提供勉强够用的控制界面，但仍是目前最先进的技术（SOTA）。
  - 论据：Neuralink N1的1000多个通道仅能提供基本可靠的控制，显示出现有技术的局限性。
  - 例子：Neuralink N1作为侵入式技术的代表，展示了当前技术的最高水平。

• 观点3：未来BCI的发展依赖于更具侵入性且通道数量更多的接口。ACCount36认为，更好的BCI发展路径在于增加通道数量和侵入性，而不是相反。
  - 论据：增加通道数量和侵入性可以提高BCI的性能。
  - 例子：目前SOTA的技术仍需更多通道和侵入性来实现更可靠的控制。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：非侵入式与侵入式BCI的技术路线选择。ACCount36明确支持侵入式技术，认为非侵入式技术如EEG不具备发展前景，而侵入式技术则是未来的方向。
• 技术现状：当前技术如Neuralink N1虽为最先进，但仍存在性能上的限制，显示出BCI技术整体仍处于发展初期。

总结：评论围绕非侵入式和侵入式BCI的可行性展开讨论，焦点在于技术路线的选择和未来发展方向，一方认为非侵入式技术缺乏实用性，另一方则看好侵入式技术的发展潜力。

data.title: First electronic-photonic quantum chip manufactured in commercial foundry
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 科学家们首次在传统电子芯片上集成了微小的光子量子系统。这个硅芯片由北western大学、波士顿大学和加州大学伯克利分校的团队开发，尺寸仅为1毫米见方，结合了量子光生成组件和经典电子控制电路。该芯片不仅能产生量子光，还内置智能电子系统以稳定光源，支持量子通信、传感和处理。这种光电集成芯片可以在商业半导体工厂大规模生产，为量子计算、传感和通信应用开辟了新途径。该研究解决了量子系统微型化的挑战，标志着量子技术发展的重要一步。研究成果发表在《Nature Electronics》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子光是否能产生单光子，以及其实际应用（特别是计算能力或运行复杂程序的能力）

不同观点：
• [gblargg] 认为量子光可以产生单光子，即光的量子。这暗示了量子光在量子计算或量子通信中的潜在应用，特别是在生成和操控单光子方面。
• [yesbut] 对此持调侃态度，用“是否能运行Doom”这一幽默提问质疑量子光的实际计算能力或实用性。这反映了对量子技术实际应用的怀疑，尤其是相对于传统计算能力而言的差距。

补充讨论：
- [yesbut] 的评论虽然带有讽刺意味，但揭示了部分公众对新兴技术（如量子技术）实际应用的期望和质疑。
- [gblargg] 的评论则更偏向于描述量子光的基础物理特性，即量子光在单光子生成方面的潜力，而没有涉及其实际计算能力。
- 争议焦点在于量子技术是否能迅速实现如经典计算机一样的实际应用，尤其是运行复杂程序的能力。

44586283.article_content:
First electronic-photonic quantum chip manufactured in commercial foundry
First time quantum light sources, control electronics are tightly integrated on a silicon chip
July 14, 2025
| By
Amanda Morris
A packaged circuit board containing the chip placed under microscope in probe station during an experiment. The first-of-its-kind silicon chip combines both the quantum light-generating components (photonics) with classical electronic control circuits — all packed into an area measuring just one millimeter by one millimeter.
Computer Science
Data Science
Innovation
McCormick
For the first time, scientists at Northwestern University, Boston University (BU) and University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) have built a tiny photonic quantum system into a traditional electronic chip.
The first-of-its-kind silicon chip combines both the quantum light-generating components (photonics) with classical electronic control circuits — all packed into an area measuring just one millimeter by one millimeter. So, not only does the chip generate quantum light, but it also has its own built-in smart electronic system to keep that light perfectly stable.
This photonic-electronic integration enables the single chip to reliably produce a stream of photon pairs — basic units that encode quantum information — required for light-based quantum communication, sensing and processing.
A commercial semiconductor foundry fabricated the chip, demonstrating its ability to be manufactured for large-scale production.
The
study was published i
n the journal
Nature Electronics
.
“Quantum experiments in the lab usually need big, bulky equipment, which requires pristine, clean conditions,” said Northwestern’s Anirudh Ramesh, who led the quantum measurements. “We took many of those electronics and shrunk them down onto one chip. So, now we have a chip with built-in electronic control — stabilizing a quantum process in real time. This is a key step toward scalable quantum photonic systems.”
This is a big deal because it’s not easy to mix electronics and photonics.”
Prem Kumar of the Center for Photonic Communication and Computing
“For the first time, we have achieved monolithic electronic, photonic and quantum integration,” said Northwestern’s
Prem Kumar
, one of the study’s senior authors. “This is a big deal because it’s not easy to mix electronics and photonics. It was a heroic effort that combined expertise from an interdisciplinary, collaborative team of physicists, electrical engineers, computer scientists, materials scientists and manufacturing experts. Our chip could open doors for not only computing but sensing and communication applications.”
An expert in quantum optics, Kumar is a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Northwestern’s
McCormick School of Engineering
, where he directs the
Center for Photonic Communication and Computing
. At the time of the research,
Ramesh was a Ph.D. candidate in Kumar’s laboratory; now he
is a
quantum systems validation engineer
at U.S.-based quantum computing company PsiQuantum.
Ramesh co-led the study with Danielius Kramnik at UC Berkeley and Imbert Wang at BU. Kramnik, who led the circuit design and electronic integration, is a recent Ph.D. graduate from the laboratory of
Vladimir Stojanovíc
, an adjunct professor of electrical engineering and computer sciences at UC Berkeley. Wang, who led the photonic device design, is a recent Ph.D. graduate from the laboratory of
Miloš Popović
, an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at BU.
Chip produces its own quantum light, stabilizes itself
With their ability to be manufactured using the same high-volume processes that create billions of transistors for everyday electronics, silicon chips are an ideal platform for light-based quantum systems. But stably operating these tiny quantum optical devices requires capabilities that are not currently standard in a commercial foundry. Slight temperature changes, imperceptible manufacturing imperfections and even heat generated by their own components can completely ruin an entire quantum system. To control these tiny variations, researchers have relied on large, external equipment to stabilize quantum optical devices — making it seemingly impossible to miniaturize full systems.
The generation of quantum light in silicon — which the team used in their foundry-manufactured devices — was first demonstrated in a decades-old experiment from Kumar’s lab at Northwestern. In a
2006 study published in the journal Optics Express
, Kumar and his collaborators demonstrated, for the first time, that shining a concentrated beam of light into tiny, appropriately designed channels etched in silicon naturally generates photon pairs. These photon pairs are inherently linked, so they can serve as qubits.

data.title: A Treatise for One Network – Anonymous National Deliberation [pdf]
data.author: simurgh_beau
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了专制政权通过分裂反对派和压制民众声音来巩固权力，导致公民感到孤立无援。为解决这一危机，文章提出了一种技术解决方案：在Telegram中加入一个新的安全功能，帮助弥合分歧并建立真正的全国共识。该工具通过一个安全、匿名、多阶段的审议过程，让公民讨论和投票重大国家议题。利用精英选拔机制，最具有共鸣和合理性的观点将脱颖而出，形成透明且可见的全国共识。该协议可在六周内将1亿人的意见精炼为100人的核心小组，旨在反映人民的真实意愿，促进团结和共同目标感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线系统是否能够有效抵抗操纵，以及如何在保护民主的同时避免多数暴政的问题。

不同观点：
• [impossiblefork] 认为该系统难以抵抗外部操纵，例如外国人涌入系统或者通过多重账户扩大影响力。即使有筛选和精英晋升机制，但如果不能解决多重账户和不合格用户的操纵问题，系统的公平性仍然存疑。同时，认为有其他系统（如线程讨论系统）也能实现类似功能，但同样面临操纵抵抗的难题。

• [JanisErdmanis] 同意匿名讨论系统的价值，但指出系统提供者有可能通过监视和欺骗参与者来牟利，从而出卖民主。因此，解决远程电子投票问题可能是实现类似系统的先决条件，以防止操控和不透明性。

• [discarded1023] 对项目的雄心表示赞赏，并提到可以参考Ehud Shapiro的相关工作，不过对其依赖的法国政治哲学基础有所质疑。尽管如此，认为Shapiro的协议可能足够中立，可以适用于该项目。

• [JimmyBuckets] 提到了与讨论相关的工具pol.is，该工具通过机器学习来综合人们的观点，识别共识和分歧。虽然pol.is值得关注，但其关注点较窄，更侧重于共识，而理解分歧同样重要。

• [constantcrying] 强烈反对该系统，称之为“奥威尔式”的系统，认为民主的核心不是简单地执行多数意见，而是保护少数派权利和通过妥协实现政府治理。直接依赖多数共识可能会导致对反对意见的压制，进而走向极权主义。同时，质疑如果伊朗70%的人支持现政权，是否意味着反对派就应该被压制，系统的设计需要考虑如何避免多数暴政。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于系统的操纵抵抗能力以及如何在保护民主的同时避免多数暴政。
- 不同评论者提到了多种相关技术工具和理论，如线程讨论系统、pol.is、电子投票解决方案等，作为参考或对比。
- 对民主本质的理解存在分歧，部分评论者强调民主中的妥协和少数权利保护，而非单纯的多数决定。

44582694.article_content:
The Crisis of Disconnected Voices
Authoritarian regimes thrive by systematically dividing their opposition and silencing the populace, creating a crisis where citizens feel isolated and powerless. This paper proposes a technological solution: a new, secure feature within Telegram to bridge these divisions and forge a genuine national consensus.
Download the Full White Paper (PDF)
Executive Summary
"The protocol is remarkably efficient, capable of distilling the views of a population of 100 million participants down to a core group of 100 in as few as six weeks. This tool is designed not only to bridge internal divisions within a populace but also to provide a clear, data-driven barometer of the people's true will, empowering them to move forward with unity and a shared sense of purpose."
This protocol establishes a secure, anonymous, and multi-stage deliberation process where citizens can discuss and vote on pressing national issues. Through a meritocratic filtration system, the most resonant and well-reasoned ideas rise to the top, culminating in a national consensus that is transparent and visible to all participants.

data.title: The bewildering phenomenon of declining quality
data.author: geox
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了现代产品质量下降的感知问题，指出从家具、服装到食品等各类商品的质量似乎都在变差，如廉价塑料味、衣物不耐穿等。文章引用了1976年一项研究，认为质量是主观概念，因消费者偏好而异，比如有人可能更看重诺基亚的耐用性而非iPhone的科技创新。这种感知与当前社会弥漫的悲观情绪有关，资本主义承诺的“努力工作即可过上体面生活”不再实现，加上社交媒体展示无法企及的生活，加剧了这种负面看法。

文章还提到“效率文化”的兴起，如埃隆·马斯克和马克·扎克伯格的大规模裁员策略，以及快时尚品牌Shein体现的一次性消费模式。同时，公共医疗系统因未适应社会变化，导致私人保险需求上升。心理学家指出，年长者更注重耐用性，而年轻一代则追求新颖，这种观念差异加剧了对质量理解的分歧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品质量是否在近年来下降以及影响质量的因素

不同观点：
• [layer8] 认为产品质量在逐年下降，尤其在成熟产品市场饱和后，企业为增加利润开始在每一代产品上偷工减料，导致质量缓慢下降。他以个人经历为例，指出新款产品往往不如旧款耐用或质量好。
• [simianparrot] 认为产品质量实际上有所提高，但价格与质量的选择范围变得更加广泛。他指出，经济舱机票、电子产品和衣服等都出现了低价低质选项，但高质量产品依然存在，只是消费者可以选择更便宜的替代品。
• [raspasov] 反驳了一些人对于过去产品质量的浪漫化看法，指出从技术角度看，现代产品（如iPhone）在各个方面都优于过去的诺基亚手机。他以自己使用诺基亚N900的经历为例，说明尽管该手机在纸面上功能强大，但实际使用体验较差。
• [jstummbillig] 认为质量在许多领域都有所提高，但质量下降的感觉来自于优先事项的转变，即更注重可负担性、效率和可访问性。他指出，虽然产品寿命可能缩短或可修复性降低，但普及度的提高是一个积极的进步。
• [markx2] 分享了一个电工的观点，指出Belling品牌的烤箱质量不如以前可靠，尽管他没有数据支持，但相信业内人的说法。
• [weinzierl] 认为质量的变化因产品而异，大规模普及通常会导致质量下降，但很多东西的质量实际上有了显著提高，例如汽车的可靠性。
• [blfr] 指出高质量产品依然存在，但价格较高，消费者习惯了廉价商品的价格。他还提到“缩水通胀”和市场上的劣质材料问题。
• [thatjoeoverthr] 提到最近购买的鞋子质量极差，认为这是“缩水通胀”和网络上假评价导致的结果。
• [bsenftner] 认为讨论的焦点文章可能是一种宣传，试图通过让人感到无力来达到某种目的。
• [esperent] 认为衣服的质量并没有明显下降，自己的衣服经过多次洗涤依然保持良好状态，并指出染料质量有了显著提高。
• [TrackerFF] 提到乐器和衣服的质量在低价位上有了显著提高，现代制造工艺使得廉价产品比过去更耐用。
• [astrobe_] 指出对于一些消费者来说，耐用性比技术创新更重要，并讨论了“计划报废”和“感知报废”的问题，认为企业通过使消费者觉得产品过时来促进销售。
• [ArtTimeInvestor] 对酒店评分的可靠性提出质疑，指出高评分酒店在实际评论中存在许多问题。
• [zkmon] 提到现代家庭装修材料的质量问题，认为过去家族企业更注重长期成功和声誉，而现代企业更注重短期目标和表面感知。

It’s as if the smell of burnt plastic from a dollar store has permeated the world. Things are worse: chipboard furniture, T-shirts unrecognizable after a second wash, packaged foods with more preservatives than ingredients. Airplane seats turned into backrests. Automatic restroom lights that turn off at a whim. But also newspaper articles shamelessly written with
ChatGPT and its algorithmic prose
. Nothing is made to be loved. Only to be bought.
In a study titled
The Concept and Measurement of Product Quality
(1976), researcher E. Scott Maynes observed that quality is an inherently subjective concept, as it depends on the preferences of each consumer. Following his reasoning, it cannot be stated in absolute terms that an iPhone 15 is of “better quality” than a 2003 Nokia. For some consumers — although we know there won’t be many — the Nokia’s extreme durability may be more valuable than the iPhone’s technological innovations. Things aren’t worse, they just seem worse to us. But why?
“There is a pessimism that permeates a large part of the population, making everything seem inferior to us,” explains Javier Carbonell, deputy director of
Future Policy Lab
, a think tank focused on designing public policies to combat economic inequalities, over the phone. “This climate affects the judgments we make about the policies implemented and also the products and goods we consume.” According to the expert, the main factor driving this criticism is that the great promise of capitalism — if you work, you can have a decent life, buy a house, and go on vacation —
is no longer being fulfilled
; the social elevator has broken down. “Added to this is the impact of social media, which shows lives unattainable for most people,” he adds.
According to Carbonell, coordinator of the book
La desigualdad en España
(Inequality in Spain)
(2024), the “culture of austerity” that emerged after the Great Recession (2008–2014) has been replaced by a “culture of efficiency,” embodied by Elon Musk, who champions a model aimed at minimizing costs. He first applied it at X (formerly Twitter) — where he laid off more than 75% of the workforce — and later, in the U.S. government.
He’s not alone: Mark Zuckerberg dubbed 2023 the “Year of Efficiency” and carried out massive layoffs at Meta. Amazon, like many other companies, has been gradually replacing human workers with robots and automated systems — to the point that in some of its warehouses, there’s no need to even turn on the lights.
When it comes to public services, the situation is different. Neither the pessimistic climate nor the supposed culture of efficiency alone explain why, between 2017 and 2022, the number of people with private insurance grew by 4% per year. According to the report
The Healthcare System: Current Situation and Future Prospects
, published in 2024, the main reason why Spaniards are turning away from the public healthcare system is the endless waiting lists.
Carbonell argues that, in absolute terms, healthcare services may not be worse than they were a few years ago. “The big problem is that they haven’t adapted to the pace of social change. They haven’t evolved enough to serve the entire elderly population, whose demographic size is increasing every year,” he argues.
Packages of clothing from fast-fashion brand Shein await shipment at a factory in Guangzhou, China, on February 12.
GILLES SABRIÉ (The New York Times / Contacto)
There’s one conclusion that comes up repeatedly throughout this report: the perception that everything is of lower quality is more pronounced among older people. The reasons are varied. One is that attributes like durability — which used to be a major factor in how people judged a product’s quality — have lost relevance.
Psychologist Albert Vinyals, author of
El consumidor tarado
(
The Disordered Consumer)
(2019), recalls that years ago, the first thing car ads highlighted was their longevity. “Now we don’t even consider it,” he notes over the phone. “My grandmother, when she went to buy clothes, looked at the type of fabric they were made of. Now, no one knows what their pants are made of. Why would they? In a year, we’ll stop wearing them because they’ll no longer be fashionable.”

La moda justa
(
Fair Fashion)
(2021), points out: “We consume clothing as if it were a disposable item.” In the last 20 years, textile production has doubled. In Spain, it is estimated that each citizen discards around
21 kilograms of clothing per year
, according to the European Environment Agency.

文章讨论了现代产品质量下降的感知问题，指出从家具、服装到食品等各类商品的质量似乎都在变差，如廉价塑料味、衣物不耐穿等。文章引用了1976年一项研究，认为质量是主观概念，因消费者偏好而异，比如有人可能更看重诺基亚的耐用性而非iPhone的科技创新。这种感知与当前社会弥漫的悲观情绪有关，资本主义承诺的“努力工作即可过上体面生活”不再实现，加上社交媒体展示无法企及的生活，加剧了这种负面看法。

主要讨论点：针对政治参与、财富增长、政治体制以及数据展示的评论和分析

不同观点：
• beej71认为选民的冷漠是一个问题，并提到Substack网站的用户体验问题（如无法缩放），对此表示不满。
• bix6指出，如果民主党在中期选举中表现出色，就有机会改变现状，并提到最高法院和下级法院之间的差异很大。
• elcritch引用数据指出，福布斯400富豪在民主党执政期间的财富增长显著（+57.1%），并特别提到在拜登任期内财富增长了64%，推测与疫情有关。同时提到特朗普任期内财富增长为15%。
• lapcat对elcritch的观点提出质疑，认为不能假设民主党持续执政会使富豪财富继续增长。他指出，共和党的减税和放松管制可能对富豪财富的长期增长有重要作用，并提出民主党执政时未完全撤销这些政策。此外，lapcat认为如果民主党稳固执政，可能会面临更多来自左翼的反富豪经济政策呼声，并建议将富豪财富增长与中等收入增长进行对比。
• vouaobrasil批评美国的政治制度，认为在只有两个主要政党之间选择，实质上更像是一种寡头政治，而非真正的民主。
• dmwood对文章内容表示赞赏，但关注内容的版权许可问题，希望知道是否在CC许可证下。
• hobs对文章的数据可视化表示赞赏，但对内容的时效性提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是富豪财富在不同政党执政期间的增长原因及其影响。elcritch和lapcat对此有不同看法，elcritch强调数据表现，lapcat则质疑数据背后的假设和长期影响。
• 另一个讨论点是美国的政治制度，vouaobrasil批评其更像寡头政治，而非真正的民主代表制度。
• 用户对数据展示（如选民投票率和财富增长图表）的质量表示赞赏，但也提到一些技术性和版权问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国政府取消非 domiciled (非 domiciled) 税务优惠政策的合理性及其影响

不同观点：
• **观点一** ([bashtoni])：政府选择关闭非 domiciled 税务优惠是因为这在政治上比真正需要的策略——对资产征税——更容易执行。对资产征税难以逃避，尤其是像梅菲尔这样的地区，资产与地点密切相关。然而，政府没有选择对包括皇室在内的贵族征税，而是选择了更容易的路径。

• **观点二** ([mickgardner])：质疑是否需要全球富人在伦敦逗留，如果他们不愿意缴税。即使税收减少，政府通过此政策向纳税人展示其公平对待所有收入者的态度，也是一种成功。

• **观点三** ([graeme])：认为伦敦吸引全球富人是因为其税务待遇，而非伦敦本身的吸引力。若提高税收，富人可能会离开，政策讨论因此变得复杂。

• **观点四** ([janice1999])：讽刺那些声称因感到“不受欢迎”而离开的超级富豪，指出他们大多并未在英国创造就业机会。此外，质疑所谓“吓跑工作创造者”的说法。

• **观点五** ([zipy124])：数据显示，非 domiciled 人数仅减少400人，但税收收入增加了1亿英镑，因此不认为富人正在大规模离开英国。

• **观点六** ([The_suffocated])：质疑为何英国要对国外赚取并存于国外的钱征税，认为这不该被视为漏洞。

• **观点七** ([elil17])：认为如果富人因为不缴税而离开，对经济并无影响，尤其是小企业主不受影响。

• **观点八** ([laweijfmvo])：认为让富人离开并重建一个支持所有人的社会是好事，因为普通人正为基本生活挣扎。

• **观点九** ([blargey])：质疑那些以避税为目的留在英国的人是否真的对英国经济有贡献，因为他们在英国经济活动中的利润原本就要被征税。

• **观点十** ([bhouston])：认为其他国家也应关闭类似漏洞，包括个人和企业的税务优惠，并提到全球最低企业税15%是一个起点。

• **观点十一** ([vjvjvjvjghv])：认为富人离开是好事。

• **观点十二** ([balderdash])：认为如果接受富人是净贡献者（缴税多于消耗的服务），且其收入和资产主要在国外并可移动，那么要么竞争以留住他们，要么失去他们。

• **观点十三** ([CjHuber])：引用塞浦路斯提供27年的非 domiciled 税务优惠为例，说明其他国家也在竞争富人。

• **观点十四** ([regularjack])：对富人离开表示欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否需要通过优惠政策留住全球富人，以及这些富人对英国经济的重要性。
• 讨论中提到了政策的政治可行性、税收公平性以及富人离开的实际影响。
• 数据被引用以支持不同观点，如非 domiciled 人数和税收收入的变化。
• 部分评论探讨了其他国家类似政策的情况，提供了一个国际视角。

• **观点九** ([blargey])：质疑那些以避税为目的留在英国的人是否真的对英国经济有贡献，因为他们在英国经济活动中的利润原本就要被征税。

• **观点十** ([bhouston])：认为其他国家也应关闭类似漏洞，包括个人和企业的税务优惠，并提到全球最低企业税15%是一个起点。

• **观点十一** ([vjvjvjvjghv])：认为富人离开是好事。

• **观点十二** ([balderdash])：认为如果接受富人是净贡献者（缴税多于消耗的服务），且其收入和资产主要在国外并可移动，那么要么竞争以留住他们，要么失去他们。

• **观点十三** ([CjHuber])：引用塞浦路斯提供27年的非 domiciled 税务优惠为例，说明其他国家也在竞争富人。

• **观点十四** ([regularjack])：对富人离开表示欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否需要通过优惠政策留住全球富人，以及这些富人对英国经济的重要性。
• 讨论中提到了政策的政治可行性、税收公平性以及富人离开的实际影响。
• 数据被引用以支持不同观点，如非 domiciled 人数和税收收入的变化。
• 部分评论探讨了其他国家类似政策的情况，提供了一个国际视角。

context42
The best code style guide is the one your team already follows.
This tool discovers it.
Let a little AI magic loose in your repo: context42 explores your codebase, chats with Google Gemini, and conjures up custom style guides for every language it finds.
How it works
Recursively discovers code files in your project, respects your .gitignore
Groups files by language extension
Runs Gemini CLI concurrently and recursively to analyze code patterns
Generates style guides (
py.md
,
ts.md
,
go.md
, etc.) based on your actual code
Quick Start
$
export
GEMINI_API_KEY=
"
...
"
$ npx context42
#
or bunx, pnpx, yarn dlx, requires Node ≥22.0
Output:
context42's style guides for this repo's
.ts
and
.tsx
code.
Usage
#
Analyze current directory, saves results to ./context42/
context42
#
Analyze specific directory
context42 -i src/
#
Custom output location
context42 -o .cursor/rules/
#
Set max concurrent Gemini processes (default: 4)
context42 --concurrency 8
#
Resume from a previous run
context42 --run 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
Why
Every codebase has implicit style rules. The problem is they're locked in developers' heads.
New team members guess. PRs get bikeshedded. Time gets wasted on "should we use
interface
or
type
?" when the answer is already in your code—if you look at the patterns.
Context42 makes the implicit explicit. It reads your code like a new developer would, but with perfect memory and pattern recognition.

data.title: Denmark card payment outage last night – Nets terminals down nationwide
data.author: khebbie
data.article_summary: Lørdag aften opstod der betalingsproblemer hos Nets, der påvirkede kortbetalinger i Danmark og Norden i to og en halv time. Problemerne med afviste betalinger medførte lange køer ved Storebæltsbroen, hvor kun bilister med nummerpladegenkendelse eller kontanter kunne passere, og lignende udfordringer blev rapporteret fra feriedestinationer som Italien, Frankrig og Tyskland. Frustrationerne udløste hærværk og dødstrusler mod personalet, hvilket fik politiet til at opfordre til ro. Problemerne blev løst senere på aftenen, og kortbetalinger blev normaliseret. Koncer turnéen Grøn var også berørt af ulemperne.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：丹麦的Nets支付系统大规模宕机事件及其影响

不同观点：
• [LarsKrimi] 认为Nets的响应非常糟糕，其状态报告页面加载时间极长且最初显示空白，最后虽然问题解决了，但过程令人尴尬。他还提出极端建议，认为Nets应该被国有化。

• [brokenodo] 分享了自己在哥本哈根亲眼看到的现象，即许多人排队在ATM取款，并推测这与Nets支付系统宕机有关。他并未直接批评Nets，但通过观察表明事件对普通民众产生了影响。

• [khebbie] 提供了更多细节，指出宕机不仅影响了POS终端和ATM，还波及了在线支付，整个丹麦都受到了影响。Khebbie引用了Nets和Zettle的声明，强调目前尚无明确的事故原因，也没有明确的预防措施，系统非常脆弱。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然没有直接的辩论，但[LarsKrimi]显然对Nets的处理非常不满，甚至提出国有化的建议，而[khebbie]则更关注技术故障本身及其对社会的影响，强调了系统脆弱性和缺乏透明度的问题。

• 宕机影响广泛：多个评论都提到了事件对不同支付方式的影响，包括POS终端、ATM和在线支付，显示出该事件对整个社会的广泛影响，尤其是在一个几乎无现金的社会中。

• 技术故障原因不明：[khebbie]特别指出，尽管系统已经恢复，但故障原因仍然不明，也没有明确的预防措施，这引发了对未来类似事件可能再次发生的担忧。

• 国有化建议：[LarsKrimi]的观点较为独特，提出了国有化的建议，这可能反映了对私营企业在处理重大技术故障时的不满和不信任。

44622378.article_content:
Betalingsproblemerne skabte lang kø i begge retninger ved Storebæltsbroen.
Læs op
Ordbog
Tekst
Af
Rasmus Jungersen
Lauge Jung Lassen
I går kl. 20:07
Opdateret
I går kl. 23:31
Opdateret efter at kortbetalinger igen er blevet normaliseret. Det oplyser pressechef i Nets, Søren Vinge klokken 22.30.
Et problem hos Nets gav lørdag aften store problemer med kortbetaling i Danmark og resten af Norden.
I de to og en halv time problemerne varede, var det ikke muligt at foretage kortbetalinger.
- Vi kan konstatere, at der er rigtig mange betalinger, der bliver afvist - ikke kun i Danmark men også i Norden. Vi prøver at undersøge, hvad årsagen kan være, lød det fra pressechef hos Nets, Søren Vinge, kort efter at problemerne var begyndt.
Flere danskere på ferie har skrevet til DR, at de også oplevede problemer med kortbetalinger. Det var blandt andet i lande som Italien, Frankrig og Tyskland.
Gav problemer på Grøn og Storebælt
Problemerne hos Nets var især tydelige på Storebæltsbroen. Her var det kun bilister med nummerpladegenkendelse eller kontanter, der kunne passere betalingsanlægget, og det skabte massiv kø i begge retninger.
Hornet blev flittitgt taget i brug, som man kan høre på videoen her, men for nogle bilister kogte frustrationerne over. Sydsjælland og Lolland-Falsters Politi skriver på X, at bilister har forsøgt at flå bommene op, og derfor er to af banerne lukket på grund af hærværk.
Der skulle også være blevet ytret dødstrusler mod personalet.
'Dødstrusler mod personalet og unødig brug af hornet hjælper IKKE på løsningen. Vi har forståelse for frustrationerne, men opførslen er ikke i orden. Det er heldigvis kun et fåtal af bilisterne, der opfører sig sådan, men det er ikke i orden,' skrev politiet på X, inden problemerne var løst.
Også koncertturnéen Grøn, der i dag er i Aarhus var ramt.
- Det påvirker os selvfølgelig på den vis, at vi ikke kan yde den service, vi ønsker, siger Nikolai Milman fra Grøn til TV 2 Østjylland.

data.title: My Self-Hosting Setup
data.author: mirdaki
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者在自托管设置上的经验和最终方案。作者经过多年尝试不同的方法，如使用Docker Compose和Ansible，最终选择了“足够好”的方案，而不是追求完美的设置。文章详细描述了作者的目标和需求，包括保护数据隐私、减少配置错误的影响、使用开源选项、方便家人和朋友使用、以及配置尽量声明式等。技术选择上，作者采用了NixOS，因其强大的配置管理和版本控制优势。文章还分享了具体的技术问题和解决方案，并提供了下一步的计划，旨在帮助其他有类似需求的人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭实验室（Homelabbing）的技术选择、易用性、安全性及维护成本

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为 Linux 和开源软件在客户端和群件协调方面存在困难，但具有强大的系统整合能力。他提到 FreeIPA 或 OpenID 类型解决方案的可能性，认为这些技术能解决目录基础设施的问题。
• [mirdaki] 分享了自己建立满意配置的过程，强调了不同技术选择和个人目标对配置的影响，并希望自己的经验能帮助他人。
• [jstrebel] 对 self-hosting 的复杂性和操作强度提出质疑，认为需要大量硬件和基础设施支持，且对家庭环境中的安全性表示担忧。
• [xyzzy123] 从家庭网络长期维护和遗产处理的角度出发，将家庭实验室与模型铁路等爱好相比，指出其中控制欲的心理驱动因素。
• [weitendorf] 讨论了自我托管的法律和基础设施需求，如 IPv6 块和成为 ISP 的可能性，并提出使用 STUN/TURN 和 "magic links" 进行认证的方案。
• [meehai] 介绍了自己的简化配置，使用单机和 nginx 代理运行多个服务，并通过 HTTP 基本认证和 OAuth 进行安全控制。
• [sylens] 对使用 Tailscale 和 VPS 反向代理的优缺点进行权衡，并寻求用户友好的监控和安全解决方案。
• [evnix] 表示由于时间限制，选择付费云服务以避免维护和升级负担，询问其他人是否有类似情况。
• [master_crab] 质疑 SSO 的必要性，认为 WireGuard 客户端可以更简单地实现家庭网络访问，无需 SSO。
• [dakiol] 对使用 Node 和 React 构建的 Flame 项目提出质疑，认为其引入过多第三方依赖，不如单一的 HTML 页面简单安全。
• [djhworld] 考虑使用 NixOS 但最终选择简单的 Docker 和 Ansible 配置，认为当前方案升级维护容易，不值得投入精力迁移到 NixOS。
• [sandreas] 对 ZFS 存储池配置提出替代建议，认为 RAID1 方案更具成本效益，并强调 RAID 不能替代备份。

A blog on technology, Star Wars, and other random thoughts. Plus some half way decent photography!
© 2025. All rights reserved.
Code Captured
My Ultimate Self-hosting Setup
Jul 7, 2025
“The circle is now complete. When I left you, I was but the learner, now I am the master (of this setup anyway)."
Iâve spent a few years trying different approaches for
self-hosting
, such as using multiple Docker compose files or Ansible. Iâve done some neat things (such as setting up
Pi-Hole with Docker and Traefik
), but I never really committed to any approach. I wanted to find something that was âperfectâ and that meant I spent a lot of time tinkering and received little actually benefit from self-hosting.
So I did some self-reflection and decided it was time for âgood enoughâ. I laid out my goals and requirements to stay focused. I put together a step by step plan. And then after quite a bit of work, Iâve actually achieved my goal and been running this setup without major issue for over six months!
Iâve written this to share a little about the process I went through as well as some specific problems I solved along the way. Iâve really benefited from the content and software folks have freely shared, and hope I can continue that and help others.
Table of Contents
Goals
Requirements
Important Tech Choices
Layout Design
Specific Problems and Solution
Next Steps
Goals
There are a lot of reasons folks get into self-hosting. Some to learn skills they can use in their career. Others to create an autonomous smart home. And yet others just love to tinker.
I primarily want control of my data and the services that use it. Itâs better for privacy and can reduce the ability for companies to pull a Darth Vader and shut down services I depend on or drastically change them. Having that control makes me feel comfortable actually incorporating those services into my life. And I want to offer the same benefit to my family and friends.
Requirements
To actually achieve that goal, I put together some requirements that balance various factors (security, usability, and complexity). Here is what I came up with in roughly priority order:
Keep as much as I can off the public facing internet
I donât want to be the lowest hanging fruit for a malicious actor. Literally preventing connecting to a service helps to achieve that. It also gives me room to make mistakes and not severely endanger myself
Reduce the likelihood that me misconfiguring something would bring down the core âinfrastructureâ of my setup for an extended period of time
Iâm human, Iâm going to make mistakes. So I should build something that accounts for it
This means I avoid circular dependencies, make it easy to revert changes, treat certain things as appliances, and may not even host something myself
I fully own the core components, no Darth Vader altering the deal should break that
In this case it means things like authentication, networking, and domain names
Limiting this to open source options means that in the worst case where a project dies or is bought out, the code is still there for me to use. That gives me time to plan next steps instead of scrambling to something else or just losing the ability to use something
Relatively easy for family and friends to use
This means keep one login per person, ideally with SSO, for as many services as I can
Me working with someone to setup things once is fine. But my users shouldnât need me to regularly fix things for them
In certain cases, this might mean I do make something public facing on the internet for usability sake
Configuration should be declarative when possible
Great for putting into version control and getting all the benefits from it like backups and reverting changes
It makes it easier to understand what Iâve done
Itâs also easier to find other peopleâs config and adapt it (which I’ve done a lot of)
Updates should be easy and safe enough that I actually do them
Too many manual steps or too precarious an update and I might delay things longer than I should
And some anti-requirements:
Things do not need to be super modular or clean
The desire to make it perfect is strong, but for this case, often just adds complexity and uses time without benefit
Not everything needs to be open source
To be clear, I certainly prefer open source software, but if there is something that is just better for my use case (and still meets my other requirements), then I should allow myself that
I don’t need high availability services
Achieving high availability is really neat, but I can deal with occasional down time if it means my setup is much simpler
General Approach
Important Tech Choices
Before going to far, let’s go over some specific technology that are at the core of my setup.
NixOS
NixOS
is a Linux distribution that uses the Nix language and package manager to configure everything about the OS. It certainly has a learning curve (and itâs error messages leave much to be desired), but itâs very powerful

data.title: Assembling a Retro Chip Tester Pro
data.author: celso
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者组装Retro Chip Tester Professional（RTC）的经历。作者一直想在实验室中添加一个芯片测试器，但觉得BackBit的Chip Tester Pro V2价格较高。后来，作者了解了Luís Correia推荐的Retro Chip Tester Professional，并决定购买。由于作者在葡萄牙，而制作者Stephan Slabihoud不直接寄送，作者通过荷兰的朋友代为购买。

作者收到裸PCB板和相关文件后，自行采购元件并开始组装。在详细文档的帮助下，组装过程顺利，仅遇到小问题（如显示屏型号错误），并成功解决。组装完成后，作者成功测试了一块4164 DRAM内存芯片，并使用RTC读取和转储了一块C64 BASIC ROM的内容。

RTC不仅可以测试多种芯片，还能读取(E)(P)ROM并编程，具有很高的扩展性和社区支持。尽管它并非开源，但文档非常详尽。与BackBit Chip Tester相比，RTC采用向量测试方法，适用于不同类型的芯片测试。总体而言，RTC是一款非常 versatile（多功能）的工具。

44620363.article_content:
Assembling a Retro Chip Tester Pro
Posted on Jul 19, 2025
I’ve been considering adding a chip tester to my lab for some time now, but I’ve never quite taken the plunge. BackBit, whom I know well because I have a BackBit Pro cartridge that I use to load software onto my 8-bit computers, has the
Chip Tester Pro V2
. I was close to buying one, but I found it somewhat expensive, and importing it from the US didn’t help, so I waited.
Recently, though, I learned about the
Retro Chip Tester Professional
from my friend
Luís Correia
, and I started researching it. Needless to say, I was hooked and had to have one for myself.
Buying it wasn’t easy. After
contacting the author
, Stephan Slabihoud, and informing him of my requirements, I received a quote and payment instructions. However, even though Stephan is in Germany, he doesn’t ship to Portugal. Reasons
are here
. So I had to proxy the order through a friend in the Netherlands who then brought it to me when he visited Portugal.
Typically, he’ll send you the bare PCBs of the mainboard with the ATmega2560 and the PCBs of the adapters you want, along with credentials to download all the documentation and firmware files. Then, you’ll do the rest: order all the components from Digikey, Mouser, or a similar supplier, and assemble it yourself, which I did.
The PCBs have arrived
At some point, I finally had all the necessary items ready to start assembling the kit.
It's Christmas, courtesy of DigiKey
I began soldering the components one by one while reading the highly detailed and professional documentation that Stephan provided, and had exactly zero technical issues or questions in the process. The documentation is top-notch, with clear instructions and pictures of the components to use, as well as interactive BOM lists, so I was able to follow it without any problems.
Interactive layout to identify the BOM parts on the motherboard
A few hours of soldering later
Of course, no technical project of mine is complete without the occasional #celsada. I purchased a 2-line display instead of the required 4-line version. Amazon to the rescue, problem solved two days later.
Srsly Celso!
After assembling everything, I proceeded to set the fuses of the ATmega2560 and flash it with the latest firmware using
avrdude
and my
AVRISP MKII
programmer, which was connected to the ISP headers on the mainboard.
Flashing the firmware
I then finally turned it on for the first time using the 5V micro USB connector. The menu was shown on the display. The DC/DC converter lit the 12V, 5V, and -5V voltage LEDs. Everything was working fine.
First boot
I then tested the first chip, a 4164 DRAM memory. I placed the chip in the ZIF socket, selected the 4164 from the menu, and pressed the test button. The tester executed the tests, beeped, and showed “Test passed” on the display. Success.
This 4164 DRAM seems OK
But the RTC is so much more than a tester. It can also read (E)(P)ROMs and dump their contents into an SD Card. It can even program them, with small adapters. Let’s go ahead and read the content of a C64 BASIC ROM, the
251913-01
, which is compatible with the 2764 EPROM. I placed the ROM in the ZIF socket, selected the 2764 from the menu, and pressed the read button. The tester read the ROM and saved it to the SD Card.
Dumping the contents of the 251913-01 C64 ROM
Looking at the dump file on my computer, I can confirm that it’s indeed the C64 BASIC ROM.
I have a multitude of adapters that I haven’t assembled yet, but I will do so as needed. For example there’s one adapter to dump C64 cartridges, another one to test SIMM modules, and many more.
Retro Chip Tester Pro adapters
Even though the RTC is technically not open-source, Stephan did a fantastic job documenting every detail, including the schematics and BOMs of all the boards. The user manual alone spans 170 pages. It has a thriving
community on Reddit
, where the author provides updates and answers questions. The boards get new revisions periodically, and new firmwares come with new features and bug fixes.
It is essential to note that the RTC and the BackBit Chip Tester are two distinct products, with different target use cases and testing techniques. While the RTC employs a pure vector-based testing technique, where it expects specific outputs for different inputs, but is unaware of the chip’s logic, other testers, such as the BackBit Chip Tester, have specific logic tailored to certain chips. These tests are often more complex and require more memory and different specs. This is why it isn’t easy for the RTC to test things like a
MOS 6522
,
MOS 6502
, or other custom chips.
On the other hand, the list of chips that the RTC can test is quite extensive, and it continues to grow with firmware updates and small adapters. The community is great and very active. And I’ll repeat, the RTC is not just a tester; it is also a ROM dumper and a programmer. You can connect it to a breadboard and use it to test your circuits. It is a very versatile tool.

data.title: Detour: A detour through the Linux dynamic linker
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary: Detour 是一个小型静态库，旨在打破 Linux 上静态链接和动态链接之间的界限。它允许你在构建静态可执行文件的同时，在运行时访问动态链接器（`ld-linux.so`），从而实现动态加载库、解析符号，甚至在同一进程中混合使用不同的 C 运行时（libc）。Detour 通过模拟操作系统的行为，利用一个最小的 ELF 加载器和动态链接器交互，使得静态链接的程序也能具备动态链接的功能，而无需直接依赖 `libc`。这种方法解决了纯静态链接导致的无法使用动态加载功能（如 `dlopen` 和 `dlsym`）的问题。目前，Detour 仅支持 `x86_64` Linux，且需要编写特定汇编代码才能支持其他架构。

Detour
On Linux, the traditional divide between statically and dynamically linked executables can feel like a hard wall. Either you bundle
everything
into your binary, or you accept full dependency on the system's libc and dynamic linker. But Detour, a tiny static library, blows a hole clean through that wall.
Detour lets you build statically linked executables, with no dependency on glibc
or musl while still giving you access to dynamic linking at runtime. You can
dlopen
libraries, resolve symbols, and even mix multiple C runtimes in the
same process, all without ever linking against libc directly.
What Is Detour?
At its core, Detour is a minimal bootstrap layer that gives your application access to the system dynamic linker
ld-linux.so
without requiring libc at all. It allows:
Dynamically loading libraries without linking libc
Capturing
libdl
functionality (e.g.,
dlopen
,
dlsym
) inside a fully static executable
Mixing different libcs in one process
Creating freestanding, zero-libc ELF executables
All while remaining entirely under your control, with no extra dependencies or runtime overhead.
Note:
Detour is not limited to freestanding or static use. You can also use it in dynamically linked applications that use an alternative libc such as musl. Detour works in both static and dynamic contexts.
Note:
Detour only works with
x86_64
Linux currently. Other architectures can be supported but will require writing assembly for system calls, setjmp/longjmp, and the indirect jump into the ELF entry point. See
loader.c
.
Why Static Linking Alone Is Not Enough
While fully static linking may sound appealing, it comes with major tradeoffs. When you bundle everything into your binary, you lose access to essential system components that rely on dynamic linking. This includes things like:
GPU drivers (e.g., OpenGL, Vulkan ICDs)
Window systems (X11, Wayland)
Audio subsystems
Input libraries
PAM modules and NSS services
Almost any plugin-based runtime
These components expect a working dynamic linker environment. If you statically link a libc, you cannot also have a dynamic linker in the same process. That means
dlopen
and
dlsym
will not work, and neither will anything that depends on them.
Detour solves this by letting you statically link your core application while still setting up a dynamic linker for runtime use.
How It Works
To understand Detour, it helps to understand how dynamic executables work under the hood on Linux.
When you run a dynamically linked
ELF
binary, the kernel does not actually execute your binary. Instead, it reads the
ELF Program Header Table
to find a segment of type
PT_INTERP
. This segment specifies the program interpreter to use, typically
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2
. The kernel then executes
that
interpreter, passing it:
The full path to your executable
All command-line arguments
Environment variables
Auxiliary vectors
From there, the dynamic linker takes over. It maps your executable into memory,
resolves shared library dependencies, performs relocations, sets up
TLS
, runs
constructors, and finally jumps to libc's initialization which then jumps to
your binary's
main
function. In effect, the dynamic
linker is the real program, and your application is just a payload it sets up
and transfers control to after initializing everything.
Detour leverages this system by pretending to be the OS.
It works like this:
We provide a tiny stub ELF executable that
is
dynamically linked against the system dynamic linker.
Your actual program (which Detour bootstraps) loads this stub ELF using a minimal ELF loader.
Detour reads the stub executable's
PT_INTERP
segment and loads the specified dynamic linker, just like the kernel would.
Before jumping into the dynamic linker, Detour calls
setjmp
to capture its current state.
It then jumps into the dynamic linker, forwarding the stub ELF and original arguments as if it were the kernel.
The dynamic linker maps in and initializes the stub ELF, then calls its
main
function. That
main
receives a string argument containing a function pointer encoded as a hex string. It decodes the address, casts it to a function pointer, and calls it.
This function captures symbols like
dlopen
,
dlsym
,
dlclose
,
dlerror
, and then calls
longjmp
to return to the original application.
Now, back at your main program's entry point, you have full access to the d

data.title: Say No to Gnulib
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary: 本文批评了GNU工具（尤其是Gnulib）的构建复杂性和维护问题，指出Gnulib难以正确构建，导致软件不易调试和重现，还可能对操作系统造成负面影响。作者认为GNU工具链的构建工具不完善，特别是对现代语言如Rust的支持不足。文章还批评Debian的软件打包方式过时，无法有效处理Rust等现代编程语言的依赖管理。作者提倡使用如Rust和uutils等现代工具替代GNU工具，以实现更好的可重现性和稳定性，并呼吁GNU改进其工具链。同时，作者建议打包现代语言项目时应采用自动化工具简化流程。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44619542.article_content:
If you are a GNU maintainer and are not willing to be criticized by people sick
of your bullshit software, do not read this post.
Also, obligatory notice on every post that touches GNU: No, nothing in this post
is political. I am perfectly fine with using GNU licensed software, and find it
more favourable than MIT licensed software as it protects user freedoms. (My
personal choice however is MPL, as it doesn't deem your software dead on arrival
at places that actually make money and feed hungry mouths)
Say NO to Gnulib
The commonly overlooked but also very important argument for dropping GNU
coreutils (or any other GNU tool that depends on Gnulib) for anything other than
the most core-level bootstrapping needs is that it depends on Gnulib.
Gnulib is a huge blob of C and 80 thousand lines of m4 that has crusted over 30+
years and is almost impossible to build correctly and hermetically, has to be
manually patched in every single program that embeds it (if trying to be
hermetic, and correct),
^1
rewards bad OSes, makes good OSes shrivel in pain,
makes packagers go bald & makes issues hard to diagnose and debug.
It's so incredibly easy to build it wrong and create a shitty non-reproducible
distro (and it is built non-hermetically by default). At least in Rust (or in
other ecosystems, such as Go) and the general ecosystem of Rust,
Cargo.toml
is
pretty well-defined and
build.rs
scripts don't do anything that insane. (Hell,
even the
C compilation tools used inside crates
are shared
deps and are well-defined).
I don't trust the average distro to build any toolchain made by GNU properly,
and I do not trust them to produce a proper set of system tools either because
of Gnulib and other bad build tools.
I do however trust the average distro (not Debian, they are lower than average
and suck at packaging
(Yes, really.)
) to build
Uutils tools & any other Rust tool correctly, because it is pretty relatively
straightforward compared to hundreds of thousands of lines of hard to audit &
ancient m4. It also won't misbehave or segfault when you interact with a
misbehaving NTFS partition.
I hope Uutils coreutils & Uutils findutils and so on achieve near perfect
compliance so I do not need to serve GNU tools to my users.
Also, keep in mind that it doesn't have to be Rust or uutils or anything that
is shilled by the "Rust Strike Force" in particular. I would also welcome the
GNU people fixing up their shitty build tooling & making their software behave
correctly. But that isn't happening any time soon, so we are starting from
scratch & fixing (quite) a few itches on the way.
Read more about this on the
Sortix wiki.
Debian sucks at packaging
Yes, really.
From
Phoronix, on bcachefs-tools being "impossible to maintain in a package collection":
So, back in April the Rust dependencies for bcachefs-tools in Debian didnât at
all match the build requirements. I got some help from the Rust team who says
that the common practice is to relax the dependencies of Rust software so that
it builds in Debian. So errno, which needed the exact version 0.2, was relaxed
so that it could build with version 0.4 in Debian, udev 0.7 was relaxed for
0.8 in Debian, memoffset from 0.8.5 to 0.6.5, paste from 1.0.11 to 1.08 and
bindgen from 0.69.9 to 0.66.
I found this a bit disturbing, but it seems that some Rust people have lots of
confidence that if something builds, it will run fine. And at least it did
build, and the resulting binaries did work, although Iâm personally still not
very comfortable or confident about this approach (perhaps that might change
as I learn more about Rust).
With that in mind, at this point you may wonder how any distribution could
sanely package this. The problem is that they canât. Fedora and other
distributions with stable releases take a similar approach to what weâve done
in Debian, while distributions with much more relaxed policies (like Arch)
include all the dependencies as they are vendored upstream.
Incredibly foolish. You are not supposed to package every single crate manually,
and you should not be anyway.
The way you should package any programming language that has a widely used and
generally well-defined and static build system is to generate (unlisted) package
definitions from packages using a script or tool (such as
cargo metadata -> parse json -> puke out package manifests
), and only add
extra configuration to packages that depend on anything external (such as a C
library, or CMake, or perl, or Go for some godforsaken reason (Why,
aws-lc-sys
, why?)).
It's also not hard to use a dependency solver algorithm to try and deduplicate
all crates required in the whole package repository using a pre-made library,
such as
lib.rs/pubgrub
. You can have the best
of all worlds.
In general - Debian is a distro stuck in the 90s that assumes every language
ecosystem is as fragmented, differing and inconsistent as C's. That's not the
case anymore, Debian maintainers should wake up from their slumber and modernize

data.title: Hyatt Hotels are using algorithmic Rest “smoking detectors”
data.author: RebeccaTheDev
data.article_summary: 文章指出，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致在x.com（推特）上出现问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。这有助于解决因扩展程序干扰而产生的故障。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：酒店使用Rest传感器自动检测吸烟行为并收取罚款，引发的各种问题和争议。

不同观点：
• [lxgr] 认为公司应因错误收费受到惩罚，尤其是当消费者没有密切监控账单时，酒店通过自动收费系统可能导致不公平的收费。建议酒店应在收费前进行人工检查，而不是依赖算法自动判定。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 指出黑盒算法的不可挑战性，以及这些算法错误有利于机构获利的问题。酒店因错误的传感器读数收取罚款，引发大量投诉和差评。
• [cpard] 质疑Rest传感器的准确性及是否存在大量误报，指出酒店通过该系统大幅增加吸烟罚款收入，并怀疑酒店和传感器公司利用误报谋取利益。
• [recipe19] 分享个人经历，提到类似自动收费系统在冰箱物品取出时也会产生误报，认为这些误报可能是有意设计来增加收入的。
• [rdtsc] 引用酒店员工的反馈，认为酒店知道这些收费是不合理的“骗局”，但仍继续使用，因为其能带来额外收入。
• [DudeOpotomus] 表示会抵制使用这种系统的酒店，认为这种做法会导致客户流失，尤其对经常旅行的客户而言。
• [hinkley] 将此问题与城市通过缩短黄灯时间从红灯摄像头中获利相比较，指出这种做法不仅没有提高公共安全，反而增加了危险。
• [pnw] 指出Rest传感器还涉及隐私问题，因其原本用于监测噪音，现扩展到监测空气质量，引发对隐私侵犯的担忧。
• [lcnPylGDnU4H9OF] 询问在遭遇误报时，消费者应收集哪些证据以提出法律诉讼，如诽谤或欺诈。
• [BlackFly] 表示会拒绝支付不合理的罚款，并在必要时通过信用卡拒付和消费者保护机构投诉来维护权益。

补充讨论：
• [MaintenanceMode] 和 [4b11b4] 都将此问题与Hertz租车公司使用AI扫描仪检测车辆损坏的做法相比较，认为这是通过技术手段增加收入的普遍趋势。
• [Animats] 提供了更多技术细节，解释了传感器的工作原理，包括空气颗粒和CO2检测，认为虽然技术本身不神秘，但其实施可能存在问题。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于Rest传感器的高误报率和自动收费系统的不公平性，消费者可能因未及时检查账单而被错误收费，酒店则通过这种系统获得不正当收入。
• 另一个争议点是隐私问题，传感器监测空气质量和噪音，可能侵犯住客隐私。

data.title: Cancer DNA is detectable in blood years before diagnosis
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章报道了科学家发现癌症的基因痕迹可以在患者确诊前三年多通过血液检测到。约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的研究人员利用高度敏感的技术，分析了20世纪80-90年代收集的血样，在26名确诊癌症患者的血液中，8人在确诊前六个月的血样中已显示癌症DNA特征，甚至在三人确诊前三年多的血样中也发现了这些痕迹。尽管样本年代久远且数量有限，研究团队依然成功检测到了极微量的癌症DNA。这一发现表明，早期筛查癌症可能成为现实，有助于在症状出现前进行诊断和治疗。不过，研究人员正在更大范围人群中验证这些结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多癌早期检测（MCED）测试的技术挑战、成本效益及其在实际应用中的可行性

不同观点：
• **技术挑战与检测精度**：[biotechbio] 指出，ctDNA（循环肿瘤DNA）检测面临的挑战在于实现足够高的灵敏度和特异性。即便能检测到低频突变，如何处理这些信息仍然是个问题。许多人的体内随着年龄增长会有一些背景性体细胞突变，这使得检测结果难以解读。此外，MCED测试（如Grail的Galleri测试）使用甲基化状态等信号来提高检测性能，但其在人群层面的实用性仍存疑。

• **成本效益与保险问题**：[siliconc0w] 认为，美国健康保险 unlikely 会为预防性护理买单，因为假阳性结果的后续成本高昂，且保险公司希望其他人（如政府）将来承担费用。提出通过全民医保选项来调整财务激励，并强调投资于预防和改善健康的紧迫性。

• **市场可行性与测试成本**：[mikert89] 指出，尽管早期癌症检测技术上可行，但高昂的筛查成本和后续诊断费用使得这些测试难以大规模应用。此外，这些测试目前并非为大规模使用而设计。

• **未来应用前景**：[octaane] 认为，CfDNA测试有可能成为年度体检的标准部分，因其具有预测和预防潜力，尤其是在免疫疗法的背景下。

• **创新治疗试验建议**：[tangerine_beet] 建议利用早期癌症检测技术进行创新治疗试验，如使用天然提取物预防癌症发展，并通过试验验证其效果。

• **实际应用中的不确定性**：[ceph_] 分享了一个实际案例，说明尽管检测结果阳性，但无法找到癌症来源，导致患者长期处于监测状态，最终结果却是虚惊一场，这表明检测结果并不总是可操作的。

• **测试结果的使用方式**：[bookofjoe] 和 [Peteragain] 讨论了如何使用这些测试结果，提出由全科医生（GP）决定进一步的测试或治疗，而不是直接告知患者测试结果，以避免不必要的焦虑和误导。

• **商业机会与市场推广**：[andsoitis] 提供了Galleri测试的商业链接，而 [andrewstuart] 则认为血液测试是一个潜在的创业机会。

• **检测的独立验证与过度炒作担忧**：[cpncrunch] 质疑该测试是否经过独立验证，并提供了相关研究的链接，指出该研究未提及对照组的假阳性率，暗示可能存在过度炒作的问题。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的技术、成本和实际应用问题反映了多癌早期检测在医疗系统中广泛应用的复杂性。
- 假阳性结果及其对患者心理和经济负担的影响是争议的焦点之一。
- 创新治疗试验和预防策略的建议展示了早期检测技术在癌症防治中的潜在价值。

By
Meghan Rosen
June 20, 2025 at 1:00 pm
Cancer’s genetic fingerprints may lurk in people’s blood long before they find out about the disease.
It’s possible to spot
tumor DNA more than three years before a person is diagnosed with cancer
, researchers report May 22 in
Cancer Discovery
. “We were shocked that we could find DNA,” says Yuxuan Wang, an oncologist and cancer researcher at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine.
The findings suggest that hunting for these telltale traces using highly sensitive and accurate technology could be a powerful tool in early cancer screening efforts. It could one day help doctors detect cancers before any other signs or symptoms of the disease appear, she says. Even a diagnosis that’s a few months earlier than usual might mean more treatment options for patients. And a yearslong head start could be lifesaving. “It would dramatically change outcomes for our patients,” Wang says.
Sign up for our newsletter
We summarize the week's scientific breakthroughs every Thursday.
Scientists have known for years that
tumor cells can shed DNA fragments into the bloodstream.
But finding these fragments early in the disease’s progression is “like looking for a needle in a haystack,” Wang says. That’s because newly formed tumors are tiny and shed just infinitesimal amounts of DNA into the bloodstream.
Her team wanted to find out just how early it could spy this DNA in the blood. The researchers relied on samples collected during the 1980s–1990s in a study that has been tracking participants’ health for decades. They analyzed samples from 26 people who were diagnosed with cancer within the six months after the blood draw.
Blood from eight of the 26 study participants carried genetic signatures of cancer, lab tests revealed. That meant the team could spot cancer months before it was diagnosed. But was it possible to detect the disease even earlier? To find out, Wang’s team tapped into blood samples collected from participants more than three years prior to their cancer diagnosis.
The researchers used a technique called whole genome sequencing that let them spell out the individual letters that make up DNA. The team was able to pick out hallmarks of cancer DNA, alterations in the human genome that are cancer-specific. These were present at such low levels that the other lab tests would have missed them.
It wasn’t a given that the team would be able to detect cancer in those early samples. Not only were they roughly 40 years old and stored in tubes not designed to preserve DNA, but the team had only about a teaspoon of plasma, the cell-free portion of blood, to work with per sample. With larger and better-preserved samples, it’s possible that the genetic tests could be even more sensitive.
The fact that Wang’s team could detect cancer so early in the samples is “pretty provocative,” says William Grady, a gastroenterologist who studies and treats colon cancer at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle. He can imagine a
Star Trek
–style future where patients with tumor DNA in their blood are given some sort of “therapy that would basically eliminate those precancers.”
That day is probably still years away, Grady says. In the meantime, he’d like to see the results validated in a larger population of people — something Wang’s team is currently working on. The current study was a proof of concept, she says.
“The results are promising enough that we’re going to go back and look at more patients.”

不同观点：
• **技术挑战与检测精度**：[biotechbio] 指出，ctDNA（循环肿瘤DNA）检测面临的挑战在于实现足够高的灵敏度和特异性。即便能检测到低频突变，如何处理这些信息仍然是个问题。许多人的体内随着年龄增长会有一些背景性体细胞突变，这使得检测结果难以解读。此外，MCED测试（如Grail的Galleri测试）使用甲基化状态等信号来提高检测性能，但其在人群层面的实用性仍存疑。

• **成本效益与保险问题**：[siliconc0w] 认为，美国健康保险 unlikely 会为预防性护理买单，因为假阳性结果的后续成本高昂，且保险公司希望其他人（如政府）将来承担费用。提出通过全民医保选项来调整财务激励，并强调投资于预防和改善健康的紧迫性。

• **市场可行性与测试成本**：[mikert89] 指出，尽管早期癌症检测技术上可行，但高昂的筛查成本和后续诊断费用使得这些测试难以大规模应用。此外，这些测试目前并非为大规模使用而设计。

• **未来应用前景**：[octaane] 认为，CfDNA测试有可能成为年度体检的标准部分，因其具有预测和预防潜力，尤其是在免疫疗法的背景下。

• **创新治疗试验建议**：[tangerine_beet] 建议利用早期癌症检测技术进行创新治疗试验，如使用天然提取物预防癌症发展，并通过试验验证其效果。

• **实际应用中的不确定性**：[ceph_] 分享了一个实际案例，说明尽管检测结果阳性，但无法找到癌症来源，导致患者长期处于监测状态，最终结果却是虚惊一场，这表明检测结果并不总是可操作的。

• **测试结果的使用方式**：[bookofjoe] 和 [Peteragain] 讨论了如何使用这些测试结果，提出由全科医生（GP）决定进一步的测试或治疗，而不是直接告知患者测试结果，以避免不必要的焦虑和误导。

• **商业机会与市场推广**：[andsoitis] 提供了Galleri测试的商业链接，而 [andrewstuart] 则认为血液测试是一个潜在的创业机会。

• **检测的独立验证与过度炒作担忧**：[cpncrunch] 质疑该测试是否经过独立验证，并提供了相关研究的链接，指出该研究未提及对照组的假阳性率，暗示可能存在过度炒作的问题。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的技术、成本和实际应用问题反映了多癌早期检测在医疗系统中广泛应用的复杂性。
- 假阳性结果及其对患者心理和经济负担的影响是争议的焦点之一。

Overview
ggc is a Git tool written in Go, offering both traditional CLI commands and an interactive interface with incremental search. You can either run subcommands like ggc add directly, or launch the interactive mode by simply typing ggc. Designed to be fast, user-friendly, and extensible.
Features
Traditional command-line interface (CLI): Run ggc  [args] to execute specific operations directly.
Interactive interface: Run ggc with no arguments to launch an incremental search UI for command selection.
Simple commands for common Git operations (add, push, pull, branch, log, etc.)
Composite commands that combine multiple Git operations
Interactive UI for branch/file selection and message input
Implemented using the Go standard library and:
golang.org/x/term
– for terminal interaction
golang.org/x/sys
– for low-level OS interaction
gopkg.in/yaml.v3
– for parsing
~/.ggcconfig.yaml

command must be installed

data.title: Behind the ballistics of the 'explosive' squirting cucumber
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 新研究探讨了喷瓜（Ecballium elaterium）的爆炸性种子传播机制。这种植物通过高压爆炸将种子高速弹射至远处，以减少亲子植株对空间和资源的竞争。德国基尔大学的研究团队利用微型计算机断层扫描和高速摄影技术，创建了喷瓜果实的3D模型，并记录了果实爆炸的细节。研究发现，种子速度可达每小时29英里，射程可达12米。果实茎在成熟过程中变直，形成约53度的角度，接近理论上能最大化射程的50度。此外，种子外有一层粘液 coat，遇湿变粘，有助于发芽。该研究在2025年7月8日的实验生物学学会年会上发表，并可能为生物启发发射系统和软体机器人提供借鉴。

主要讨论点：不同用户对植物种子传播机制及其相关现象的讨论，特别是对喷瓜（squirting cucumbers）种子传播方式的观察和联想。

不同观点：
• [x______________] 分享了自己对办公室种植的三叶草种子传播的观察，指出三叶草种子通过干燥后爆裂的机制将种子传播出去，类似于喷瓜。他还推测较重的种子可能需要不同的传播机制，比如借助液体来辅助，并感叹进化的神奇。

• [firesteelrain] 对进化选择的种子发射角度（53°）表示惊叹，称之为“自然的弹道优化”，暗示自然界在物理规律上的精确性。

• [Sharlin] 对喷瓜种子喷射速度（29英里每小时）和距离（12米）表示惊讶，并幽默地提到自己学到了新词“mucilaginous”（粘液的），暗示对植物传播机制的复杂性感到意外。

• [lolc] 对文章中提到的“可能应用”部分表示调侃，认为人类喜欢观看慢动作的爆炸现象，暗示人们有时更关注视觉效果而非实际科学应用。

• [sMarsIntruder] 对文中混合使用英制和公制单位表示不满，特别指出“29英里每小时”和“12米”的单位冲突，关注点在于度量单位的标准化问题。

• 讨论中涉及了进化和自然选择在种子传播机制中的作用，特别是干燥爆裂和液体辅助传播的对比。

The GIST
Behind the ballistics of the 'explosive' squirting cucumber
by
Society for Experimental Biology
edited by
Gaby Clark
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies

Editors

fact-checked

Squirting cucumber (Ecballium elaterium). Credit: Helen Gorges
New research into the biomechanics of explosive seed dispersal in squirting cucumbers (Ecballium elaterium) reveals how these plants have adapted a suite of unique traits that help propel their high-speed seeds far and wide.
Seed dispersal comes in many forms, and much is known about animal, wind and water-assisted dispersal—but less is known about the self-propelled dispersal mechanisms of plants. One of these is the ballistic dispersal of the squirting cucumber, which uses high-pressure explosions to eject its seeds at high speed across large distances.
"Many factors have to interact perfectly to disperse the seeds in the most efficient way, while not destroying the whole plant too early," says Helen Gorges, a Ph.D. student at the Department of Functional Morphology and Biomechanics in the Zoological Institute of Kiel University, Germany.
To reduce direct competition for space and resources between parent and offspring plants, there is an evolutionary drive for plants to disperse their seeds as far as they possibly can. The research conducted by Gorges aimed to explore the mechanisms that control the cucumber's fruit during ripening and maximize its chances of successfully dispersing.
Gorges and her team used microcomputed tomography to create a 3D-model of the whole fruit, as well as micro-CT imaging and high-speed videography to capture the exploding fruit in fine detail.
Squirting cucumber explosive seed dispersal (over 300x slowed down). Credit: Helen Gorges
"We recorded the explosion of the fruit with high-speed videos at 1,000 fps and 10,000 fps to calculate the speed of the seeds and the possible shooting distances," says Gorges. "We also analyzed pictures during the ripening of the fruits to measure the curvature of the fruit stem and the angle between fruit and stem."
Gorges and her team found that the seeds can achieve speeds up to 29 miles per hour and reach shooting distances up to 12 meters. "It's super interesting to watch the explosions through high-speed recordings, as the explosions happen way too fast to see anything in real-time," says Gorges.
The experiments also revealed that the fruit stem straightens up during ripening, creating an average 53° angle that is close to the theoretical perfect angle of 50° that would maximize shooting distance.
Additionally, the team found that the seeds always exit the
fruit
facing the same way and produce a mucilaginous coat when they get wet, which becomes an adhesive when it dries and improves conditions for germination.
Squirting cucumber explosive seed dispersal in real time and slowed down. Credit: Helen Gorges
These findings have potential applications for bio-inspired launching systems as hydrogel-based actuators for medical tools and micro-robots. "There are also many applications in soft robotics,
drug delivery systems
and similar devices, where energy-efficient launching systems are desired," says Gorges.
This research is being presented at the
Society for Experimental Biology Annual Conference
in Antwerp, Belgium on the 8th July 2025.

• [x______________] 分享了自己对办公室种植的三叶草种子传播的观察，指出三叶草种子通过干燥后爆裂的机制将种子传播出去，类似于喷瓜。他还推测较重的种子可能需要不同的传播机制，比如借助液体来辅助，并感叹进化的神奇。

• [firesteelrain] 对进化选择的种子发射角度（53°）表示惊叹，称之为“自然的弹道优化”，暗示自然界在物理规律上的精确性。

• [Sharlin] 对喷瓜种子喷射速度（29英里每小时）和距离（12米）表示惊讶，并幽默地提到自己学到了新词“mucilaginous”（粘液的），暗示对植物传播机制的复杂性感到意外。

• 讨论中涉及了进化和自然选择在种子传播机制中的作用，特别是干燥爆裂和液体辅助传播的对比。

data.title: The Minecraft game score unexpectedly became big business for its composer
data.author: tunapizza
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作曲家Daniel Rosenfeld（艺名C418）为独立游戏《Minecraft》创作音乐的经历。2009年，19岁的Rosenfeld在工厂工作之余为《Minecraft》创作了配乐，当时只收到了少量报酬，但保留了配乐的全部版权。随着《Minecraft》大获成功，微软在2014年收购了开发商Mojang，Rosenfeld拒绝了微软购买其配乐的提议。他与经理Patrick McDermott合作，继续独立管理《Minecraft》相关音乐，并取得了显著成绩，包括金唱片认证和国会图书馆收录。虽然Rosenfeld因此可能失去了为《Minecraft》未来作品创作的机会，但他认为自己的选择是正确的，可以追求其他令他兴奋的音乐项目。文章还探讨了游戏配乐行业的特殊性以及音乐与游戏的跨界潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Minecraft音乐的影响、作曲者的变更以及相关经济利益

不同观点：
• **n20benn**：推荐C418为Wanderstop创作的新专辑，认为其风格与Minecraft音乐相似，甚至个人觉得更喜欢。具体推荐了几个曲目，并提到专辑时长较长，值得深入聆听。

• **pityJuke**：强调Minecraft原声音乐的力量和情感影响，特别是Mice on Venus的混音版本，能够引发情感共鸣。同时提到该音乐常用于Technoblade的纪念视频中，增加了情感价值。

• **donatj**：对微软引入新作曲者的决定表示不满，认为这放弃了使Minecraft成为今天的样子的重要部分，暗指原作曲者的独特贡献不可替代。

• **chrisdalke**：赞赏Minecraft音乐的怀旧和专注功能，特别是作为背景音乐在编程时使用。推荐了Sweden和Aria Math这两个曲目。

• **rollcat**：认可后期加入的作曲者，特别是Lena Raine的作品，并提到Pigstep音乐碟在速度运行结束时的使用，以幽默方式指出其受欢迎程度。

• **bearjaws**：关注C418的经济收益，通过Spotify和YouTube的版税收入估计其收入约200万美元，并猜测微软收购音乐版权的动机是为了完全拥有IP。

补充讨论：
• **neonate和eps**：分享了与讨论相关的存档链接，但未提供具体评论。

• **neko_ranger**：个人喜好，表示Sweden是其最喜欢的曲目。

• **Deeksha676**：对分享付费墙文章表示不满，并提供了一个非付费墙的文章链接，以便其他人阅读。

争议焦点：微软更换作曲者的决定引发不满，部分用户认为原作曲者的作品是Minecraft成功的重要部分，而新作曲者可能无法达到相同的效果。

44581725.article_content:
Daniel Rosenfeld and Patrick McDermott
Phoebe Wilson
I
n 2009, in between full-time shifts at a local factory, then-19-year-old musician
Daniel Rosenfeld
composed a score for an independent video game. “It was just a side hustle, maybe not even that. It was a hobby, really,” explains Rosenfeld, who records under the name
C418
.
Related
Jack Black Teams With Dave Grohl For Rocking ‘Minecraft’ Soundtrack Song ‘I Feel Alive…
03/24/2025
The game,
Minecraft
, turned out to be successful beyond Rosenfeld’s wildest dreams. In 2014, Microsoft purchased
Minecraft’s
Swedish developer, Mojang Studios, for $2.5 billion, and through 2023, it had sold 300 million copies of the game, making it the best-selling video game of all time. Now, it’s the latest one to receive a movie adaption, and even that has been wildly successful:
A Minecraft Movie,
starring
Jack Black
, is the biggest box office hit of 2025 to date, having already grossed $550.6 million since it opened on April 4.
Because no one anticipated the game’s whirlwind success, or had the budget to properly pay him back in 2009, Rosenfeld was compensated for his work with a small fee and 100% ownership over
Minecraft
’s now-iconic score. Then, when Microsoft came calling, Rosenfeld made a fateful decision: he refused to sell the score to the tech behemoth, opting instead to bring on game composer manager
Patrick McDermott
to help him navigate building a business as an independent composer of
Minecraft
.
Trending on Billboard
McDermott counts himself as one of the rare folks who understands how to navigate both games and music. He started his career at Captured Tracks, and from 2015 to 2020 he built Ghost Ramp, a label which specialized in releasing game soundtracks on vinyl. At the time he was brought in to help Rosenfeld, he was also managing a number of other games composers, too.
Though McDermott says deals like Rosenfeld’s, where composers retain ownership of their IP, are increasingly rare, his
Minecraft
soundtracks have proven to be big business. The score,
Minecraft Volume Alpha,
which is distributed via TuneCore, was certified gold by the RIAA in 2023, and this month, it was inducted into the Library of Congress by the National Recording Registry, which cited it as an “audio treasure worthy of preservation.”
Related
C418 Hits No. 1 on Emerging Artists Chart Thanks to ‘Minecraft: Volume…
08/03/2023
Since its release on digital service providers, streams of
Minecraft Volume Alpha
and its companion
Volume Beta
have averaged 38% year over year growth, and they have been streamed 2.8 billion times worldwide, according to McDermott. McDermott and Rosenfeld have built a surprisingly formidable vinyl business, too. The album, distributed by Ghostly, has sold over 200,000 units to date globally. Rosenfeld even has fans of his own who often congregate in a Discord server devoted to talking about his work, which includes the scores for other games such as
Catacomb Snatch
and
Wanderstop
.
But it’s not all fun and games for Rosenfeld. He thinks that by not selling the score to Microsoft, he might have sacrificed his chance to make future soundtracks for the
Minecraft
franchise — and it’s true that since he declined Microsoft’s offer once and for all, Rosenfeld has not written anything for the game, with Microsoft instead turning to other composers. But because many
Minecraft
players are nostalgic for his original soundtrack, the score for
A Minecraft Movie
, composed by
Devo
’s
Mark Mothersbaugh
, interpolates it — giving Rosenfeld some upside from the blockbuster’s success.
In the end, Rosenfeld feels he made the right choice. “I don’t want to be stuck with the same thing for the next 50 years,” he says of
Minecraft
, and now, he can turn his attention to the new scoring gigs that excite him.
Here, Rosenfeld and McDermott speak to
Billboard
about the strange business of scoring for games and building a living off of
Minecraft.
“I know it’s hard to believe, but there’s a real argument that Daniel’s music is up there for the most heard audio by humans in history,” says McDermott.
Related
The Crossover Potential Between Music & Gaming Is Clear – But It Requires a Thoughtful Approach…
06/08/2023
How were you compensated for the original
Minecraft
game?
Daniel Rosenfeld:
I asked for a share of the game, and I didn’t get a share. I got a tiny, tiny amount of salary for the music itself. The good thing, though, is that I owned the rights to the music, and that’s still persistent to this day. At the time, like 2010, people liked doing [revenue] shares for indie games as payment — like the musician gets 10 percent [of the game’s IP], the visual artist gets 20, and then the main developer gets 40 or whatever. That’s usually what happened back then. Mine was a little different.
Back in the day, when you made this score, is this also how larger game scores worked? Would Nintendo, for example, offer a deal like this?
Rosenfeld:
Absolutely not. Nintendo is a Japanese company and in

data.title: Roman Roads Research Association (UK)
data.author: countrymile
data.article_summary: 罗马道路研究协会（RRRA）致力于研究和推广罗马道路网络及其遗产，特别是在英国。协会继承了Ivan D. Margary的开创性工作，利用现代技术如LiDAR进行研究，揭示被植被遮盖的考古遗迹。协会出版同行评审期刊《Itinera》，聚焦罗马道路及交通基础设施的新发现和研究，并举办在线讲座系列。协会还计划推出新网站，并持续更新其研究项目和出版物。

不同观点：

The Roman Roads Research Association was formed to advance knowledge of the Roman road network and promote the study of Roman roads and Roman heritage throughout the British Isles. Our work is inspired by Ivan D. Margary whose âRoman Roads in Britain â (1955) remains the most comprehensive gazetteer ever compiled.
We continue Margaryâs work by researching Roman roads using modern technology such as LiDAR, which uses lasers fired from an aircraft to create an incredibly accurate model of the earthâs surface beneath any vegetation, revealing surviving archaeology otherwise not visible. The example below is a Roman road in Lincolnshire, just east of Grantham, where until recently it was assumed that the A52 followed the course of a Roman road, which it almost certainly doesnât. Instead, a different road leads from the same junction on Ermine Street, apparently serving an entirely local function.
