members alike for use on this page, and for use in the gazetteer as it develops. As the Gazetteer develops, we will need a huge number of good quality images from all over the country
The fifth volume of the Roman Roads Research Associationâs own peer reviewed journal,
Itinera
, will be released in digital form to our members in June 2025, with printed versions available to
purchase
for delivery in late May. We are now accepting submissions for Volume 6.
Itinera
is the only journal in the world dedicated to publishing research, fieldwork, and new discoveries that relate to Roman roads or Roman transport infrastructure more broadly, both in Britannia and the rest of the Roman Empire.
We welcome papers which contribute to a better understanding of the road network and its place within the wider context of Roman studies, whether in the UK or internationally.
Itinera includes reports of excavations, new discoveries from lidar, aerial photography, and geophysics, designation of 'new' routes through an expanded Margary system, and a range of peer-
reviewed scholarly articles exploring the wider context of roads as related to military and civilian activity, forts, planning, surveying and all aspects of Roman life. Itinera 6 will include
Roman Roads in 2025
, providing an overview of all archaeological work involving Roman roads in Britain during the coming year. Full details, including Notes for Contibutors, can be found

data.title: A Tour of Microsoft's Mac Lab (2006)
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文是David Weiss对微软Mac实验室的介绍，分享了该团队如何开发和测试Mac软件。实验室面积约2000平方英尺，拥有大量苹果硬件，包括旧型号的iMac、iBook以及古董级Mac，如Macintosh SE/30和Power Macintosh G3。实验室设有"沙盒"区域，用于测试不同硬件配置，并配有等离子显示屏用于培训和展示。此外，实验室使用ADIC备份机器人及Veritas Backup Exec软件进行数据备份，虽偶有故障但总体可靠。自动化测试系统是Mac Office项目的重要组成部分，每天利用249台自动化机器对Office新版本进行数千次测试，以确保软件质量。实验室还处于不断发展和过渡中。

David Weiss
19 April 2006
A Tour of Microsoft's Mac Lab
Today I'll stop my
3rd person
perspective
. I'm going to write a little bit more about what I do to help MacBU ship great software and provide some color around what's it's like to work on Mac software at Microsoft. Often when we have press events or special visits from our MVPs I'll give them a tour of the Mac Lab and explain what we do. They've always found it very interesting and so I thought I'd share a virtual tour of our Mac Lab. Let's get started:
Lab Door
We start with the door. The Mac Lab is about 2000 square feet of solid computers. The calendars you see down the side of the wall we use to mark team birthdays as well as special events. The CD on the door is an old Apple Software Restore CD from the last beige Mac Apple produced, the Power Macintosh G3.
The "Sandbox" and Plasma display
The first area in the Mac Lab is what we call the Sandbox. This is where we keep all significant hardware configurations Apple has released that run our products. We'll use the Plasma display to, watch DVDs and play games, uh er, I mean, do important training presentations. ;-) It's actually very useful because everyone can be in front of a computer and still see the main screen and follow along. Often other groups at Microsoft (the games group, hardware drivers group and even the Windows media group) will come and schedule time in the Mac Lab to test their software on the different hardware configurations.
Old iMacs and iBooks in the distance
More Macs
We have lots of Apple hardware. You can see here the old colorful iMacs along with some of the old iBooks. You can also see two of our Lab Technicians working on the backup systems, but more about that later. Up until a few months ago we had every significant hardware revision Apple has ever released since the dawn of time. We even had a section of the Lab we affectionately called the "Mac Nursery" where we kept all the older Macs going. We even had an old SE/30 and IIci and super expensive Mac II all connected via PhoneNet running
Spectre
, just for fun. It's always super fun to boot Word 1.0 or Excel 1.0 on these old machines and see how much things have changed. Due to lack of space in the Lab we had to put all of these older machines into storage and recycled the following:
Macintosh (original)
Macintosh SE
Macintosh SE/30
Macintosh Classic
Macintosh Centris 610 <-- I had this one in my room during high school
Macintosh IIci
Macintosh IIsi
Power Macintosh 7100/66
Power Macintosh 7100/80
Power Macintosh 7500/100
Quadra 650
Power Macintosh G3
Duo Dock with Powerbook Duo 2300c
Power Computing PowerCenter Pro 210
May they rest in peace.
ADIC Backup Robots
One of the realities of working with computers is that things fail. More often then you might think. We've used different backup robots, but ever since we moved to ADIC we've never had a robot failure. They just make great stuff. We have 3 robots and use
Veritas Backup Exec
. It works pretty well, as you can see:
Lots of backup tapes
We also do offsite backups just incase "The Big One" hits, but for regular use these tapes work just great, except when they don't. Recently we had a failure and lost 400 GB of data! We restored it from the tapes and then discovered that the Mac version of the Backup Exec agent had a corruption bug causing the restores to be compromised! Veritas folk were super responsive and they should have a new Mac agent out soon. Backup software and file systems are in the class of software that simply must work, all the time. Alas,
this is not always the case
.
I'm going to skip the "Build Lab" section of our Lab since it's very much in
transition
. Maybe I'll post about that later. For now, on to our automation system!
Mac Office is one of those "software in the large" projects. There's really no way a team of our size would be able to adequately test all of Office without the use of automated testing. Every day we get a new build of Office from the build machines, we copy it to our Xserve RAID connected to our dual G5 Xserve for access by our 249 automation machines. We then run thousands and thousands of tests on the new build. Typically we get 4 builds of Office each day: English Ship, English Debug, Japanese Ship and Japanese Debug. We run our entire battery of tests against all the builds and then report any failures to testers via email. The testers investigate the failures, log any bugs and then move on to their other duties as testers. This turns out to be very effective, if used properly, and over time it allows testers to focus on things humans do best, while letting computers verify the repetitious and mundane, but necessary, testing. It all started with our Blue and White G3s years ago. At first when testers would upgrade their test machines, instead of recycling the machines, "The Lab" would get them to add them to our automation machine pool. I think we had about 20 machines to begin with.
Venerab

主要讨论点：对基于硅的生命形式及其潜在影响的讨论

不同观点：
• [chmod775] 认为基于硅的生命形式即便可能，也可能不如碳基生命形式高效。他指出，地球环境中碳的分子复杂性远超硅，并且碳基生命在进化过程中表现出更大的适应性和多样性。他还用人类肺细胞的复杂性与现代CPU进行对比，强调碳基生物的复杂性。

• [omneity] 提出了对硅基生命形式的生长模式的疑问，质疑这种生命形式是像生物一样真正生长，还是像珊瑚群一样通过集群组装来扩展。这表明对硅基生命形式的定义和性质存在一定疑惑。

• [datameta] 以一种半开玩笑的方式提到资源消耗问题，提到只要在食物链的最低层有足够的资源（如回形针），人类就能安然无恙。这暗示了对硅基生命形式可能带来的资源消耗问题的担忧。

• [gavinray] 引用了科幻小说《Mortal Engines》系列，表达了对这种技术发展的兴趣，并将其与自己成长过程中喜爱的科幻小说联系起来。他似乎对这种技术发展持开放态度，但同时也隐含了对未来潜在影响的思考。

• [littlestymaar] 引用了电影《侏罗纪公园》中的一句台词，质疑科学家是否在追求技术实现的同时，忽略了伦理和道德层面的考虑。这表明对科学家是否应该进行此类研究存在质疑。

• [targetx] 提到了游戏《Horizon Zero Dawn》，认为科学家应该从中吸取教训，重新考虑此类技术的发展。他暗示这种技术虽然技术上令人印象深刻，但可能不是一个好主意，暗示了对技术发展潜在负面影响的担忧。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对硅基生命形式的可行性、复杂性、生长模式以及资源消耗的担忧。
• 部分评论通过引用科幻作品，表达了对未来技术发展的期待和警惕。
• 争议的焦点在于科学家是否应该继续探索硅基生命形式，以及这种技术发展是否会带来不可预见的负面影响。

data.title: I'm betting against AI agents in 2025, despite building them
data.author: Dachande663
data.article_summary:
文章作者基于过去一年构建多个AI代理系统的经验，对2025年将成为“AI代理年”的炒作持怀疑态度。他指出三个关键现实问题：

1. **错误率复合增长**：在多步骤工作流中，即便每步的可靠性为95%，20步后的成功率仅为36%，而生产系统需要99.9%以上的可靠性。当前技术下，自主多步骤工作流在数学上是不可能的。
   
2. **上下文窗口的成本问题**：长对话导致代币成本呈二次方增长，使得会话代理在经济上不可行。一个100轮对话的成本可达50-100美元，无法大规模应用。

3. **工具设计挑战**：构建适用于代理的生产级工具是另一大工程挑战，大多数团队低估了这一难度。

作者总结，成功的代理系统并非完全自主，而是由离散、可验证的操作组成，并在关键节点加入人工确认。最有效的“代理”往往是简单、无状态的工具，而非持续对话的代理。

44623207.article_content:
Everyone says 2025 is the year of AI agents. The headlines are everywhere: "Autonomous AI will transform work," "Agents are the next frontier," "The future is agentic." Meanwhile, I've spent the last year building many different agent systems that actually work in production. And that's exactly why I'm betting against the current hype.
I'm not some AI skeptic writing from the sidelines. Over the past year, I've built more than a dozen production agent systems across the entire software development lifecycle:
Development agents
: UI generators that create functional React components from natural language, code refactoring agents that modernize legacy codebases, documentation generators that maintain API docs automatically, and function generators that convert specifications into working implementations.
Data & Infrastructure agents
: Database operation agents that handle complex queries and migrations, DevOps automation AI systems managing infrastructure-as-code across multiple cloud providers.
Quality & Process agents
: AI-powered CI/CD pipelines that fix lint issues, generate comprehensive test suites, perform automated code reviews, and create detailed pull requests with proper descriptions.
These systems work. They ship real value. They save hours of manual work every day. And that's precisely why I think much of what you're hearing about 2025 being "the year of agents" misses key realities.
TL;DR: Three Hard Truths About AI Agents
After building 12+ production systems, here's what I've learned:
Error rates compound exponentially in multi-step workflows. 95% reliability per step = 36% success over 20 steps. Production needs 99.9%+.
Context windows create quadratic token costs. Long conversations become prohibitively expensive at scale.
The real challenge isn't AI capabilities, it's designing tools and feedback systems that agents can actually use effectively.
The Mathematical Reality No One Talks About
Here's the uncomfortable truth that every AI agent company is dancing around: error compounding makes autonomous multi-step workflows mathematically impossible at production scale.
Error Compounding in AI Agent Workflows
Let's do the math. If each step in an agent workflow has 95% reliability, which is optimistic for current LLMs,then:
5 steps = 77% success rate
10 steps = 59% success rate
20 steps = 36% success rate
Production systems need 99.9%+ reliability. Even if you magically achieve 99% per-step reliability (which no one has), you still only get 82% success over 20 steps. This isn't a prompt engineering problem. This isn't a model capability problem. This is mathematical reality.
My DevOps agent works precisely because it's not actually a 20-step autonomous workflow. It's 3-5 discrete, independently verifiable operations with explicit rollback points and human confirmation gates. The "agent" handles the complexity of generating infrastructure code, but the system is architected around the mathematical constraints of reliability.
Every successful agent system I've built follows the same pattern: bounded contexts, verifiable operations, and human decision points (sometimes) at critical junctions. The moment you try to chain more than a handful of operations autonomously, the math kills you.
The Token Economics That Don't Add Up
There's another mathematical reality that agent evangelists conveniently ignore: context windows create quadratic cost scaling that makes conversational agents economically impossible.
Here's what actually happens when you build a "conversational" agent:
Each new interaction requires processing ALL previous context
Token costs scale quadratically with conversation length
A 100-turn conversation costs $50-100 in tokens alone
Multiply by thousands of users and you're looking at unsustainable economics
I learned this the hard way when prototyping a conversational database agent. The first few interactions were cheap. By the 50th query in a session, each response was costing multiple dollars - more than the value it provided. The economics simply don't work for most scenarios.
Token Cost Scaling in Conversational Agents
My function generation agent succeeds because it's completely stateless: description → function → done. No context to maintain, no conversation to track, no quadratic cost explosion. It's not a "chat with your code" experience, it's a focused tool that solves a specific problem efficiently.
The most successful "agents" in production aren't conversational at all. They're smart, bounded tools that do one thing well and get out of the way.
The Tool Engineering Reality Wall
Even if you solve the math problems, you hit a different kind of wall: building production-grade tools for agents is an entirely different engineering discipline that most teams underestimate.

2. **上下文窗口的成本问题**：长对话导致代币成本呈二次方增长，使得会话代理在经济上不可行。一个100轮对话的成本可达50-100美元，无法大规模应用。

3. **工具设计挑战**：构建适用于代理的生产级工具是另一大工程挑战，大多数团队低估了这一难度。

作者总结，成功的代理系统并非完全自主，而是由离散、可验证的操作组成，并在关键节点加入人工确认。最有效的“代理”往往是简单、无状态的工具，而非持续对话的代理。

data.title: AI is killing the web. Can anything save it?
data.author: edward
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AI技术，特别是ChatGPT及其竞争对手，如何对互联网的经济模式构成威胁。媒体公司向Cloudflare的CEO Matthew Prince表达了对AI生成内容影响其业务的担忧。文章还探讨了AI对网络安全的挑战，以及Nvidia等公司如何试图说服政府投资"自主"AI。此外，文章提及了其他商业话题，如特朗普的铜关税政策、Kraft Heinz的困境以及酒店品牌在印度的发展机遇。整体反映了AI对互联网和全球商业的广泛影响及潜在应对措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网的现状、问题以及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• **kristianc**：认为大量在线内容已经是为SEO优化的低质量内容，但精英出版商如《纽约时报》等并不依赖谷歌流量。未来内容可能会更多地被放置在受限访问的空间中，可能比当前免费但难以阅读的状态更好。
• **sharpfuryz**：互联网已经失去了原有的开放和真实性，如今被算法和机器人控制。问题根源在于当前的互联网模式服务于平台而非用户，可能需要构建一个新的互联网，优先考虑用户、隐私和真实表达。
• **nonvibecoding**：互联网的独特性和灵魂在十多年前开始消失，现在所有网站看起来都相似，缺乏个性。
• **alganet**：主张减少协作和竞争，鼓励个人发展独特的观点，而不是同质化的 masses。
• **mmcconnell1618**：引用Yanis Varoufakis的观点，认为“云资本主义”正在取代传统资本主义，少数玩家在主导平台上建立自己的领地。互联网缺乏有效的微支付系统，导致注意力经济盛行。
• **amelius**：建议像阿米什人一样创建一个完全独立的互联网版本。
• **anilgulecha**：认为联邦化的互联网可以拯救当前状况，但鉴于极少数人能自托管，中央化服务似乎会胜出。可能需要全球法律来抑制中央化和网络效应。
• **senectus1**：认为经济学将拯救互联网，AI并不具备成本效益，投资者将因外部经济影响而要求回报，许多AI初创公司将倒闭或缩减规模。
• **SalariedSlave**：认为互联网早已成为商业基础设施，质疑是否有值得拯救的东西。
• **_nalply**：认为利润导向和无约束的商业行为是互联网问题的根源，AI只是新的工具，问题在于公司为了竞争优化而造成损害。
• **tobyhinloopen**：认为互联网已经死亡，现代网站访问体验糟糕，充满侵入式广告和垃圾信息。
• **kkfx**：认为搜索引擎是发现信息的最佳工具，LLMs并没有杀死互联网，而是从中获取数据。真正杀死互联网的是社交网络等封闭的平台和ISP不提供开放的主机服务。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：互联网是否需要被拯救以及如何拯救。不同用户对理想互联网的定义和实现方式存在分歧。
• **重要论据**：
  - 精英出版商是否依赖谷歌流量。
  - AI和SEO对互联网质量的影响。
  - 互联网的联邦化和去中心化是否可行。
  - 经济学和投资回报对互联网发展的影响。
  - 用户隐私、真实表达和开放性在互联网中的重要性。

这些观点共同描绘了当前互联网面临的多重挑战，以及不同用户对解决方案的探索和思考。

data.title: How to write Rust in the Linux kernel: part 3
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于如何在Linux内核中使用Rust编程的第三部分，重点介绍Rust与C之间的接口以及内存分配机制。文章指出，Rust代码可以通过外部函数接口（FFI）调用C函数，但由于C和Rust在内存释放和锁定方面的差异，直接调用内核C函数存在问题。为了解决这些问题，内核文档建议为每个子系统创建一套集中的Rust绑定接口，以提供标准化和安全的接口。在内存分配方面，Rust内核代码使用`kernel::alloc`模块提供的接口，支持三种分配方式：Kmalloc、Vmalloc和KVmalloc，并允许指定分配标志和处理失败情况。这些接口实现了`Allocator`特性，并提供了便捷的别名如`KBox`和`VVec`用于不同类型的内存分配。文章还提到，根据不同场景，内存分配时可能需要考虑阻塞、交换或从特定区域获取内存等问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言的"userspace"开发及其对初学者的友好性

不同观点：
• [mmastrac] 认为当前的Rust版本保持了与标准Rust方言足够接近的特点，使得作为"userspace"开发者能够保持高效。他还提到，内存分配似乎更显式化，并表示希望有一些对初学者友好的任务，以便尝试参与这种开发工作。

• [a5c11] 对该评论进行了标记，但未提供具体意见或反驳，可能对该评论内容有异议或认为其不符合讨论规范。

• [amy214] 也对该评论进行了标记，同样未提供具体反馈或进一步讨论，可能出于与[a5c11]类似的原因。

补充讨论：
- [mmastrac] 的评论中提到了对初学者友好的任务需求，表明社区中可能存在对新手引导的关注。
- 标记行为表明评论中可能存在争议，但具体原因不明，可能需要进一步核查标记理由。

By
Daroc Alden
July 18, 2025
Rust in the kernel
The interfaces between C and Rust in the kernel have grown over time; any
non-trivial Rust driver will use a number of these. Tasks like allocating memory,
dealing with immovable structures, and interacting with locks are necessary for
handling most devices. There are also many subsystem-specific bindings, but the
focus of this third item in our series on writing Rust in the kernel
will be on an overview of the bindings that all kernel Rust code
can be expected to use.
Rust code can call C using the
foreign function interface
(FFI); given that, one
potential way to integrate Rust into the kernel would have been to let Rust
code call kernel C functions directly. There are a few problems with that
approach, however:
__always_inline
functions, non-idiomatic APIs, etc.
In particular, C and Rust have different approaches to freeing memory and
locking.
During the early planning phases, the project
proposed
adopting a rule that there should be a
single, centralized set of Rust bindings for each subsystem,
as explained in
the kernel documentation
. This has
the disadvantage (compared to direct use of Rust's FFI)
of creating some extra work for a Rust programmer who wishes to
call into a new area of the kernel, but as more bindings are written that need
should go away over time. The advantage of the approach is that there's a single
set of standardized Rust interfaces to learn, with all of the documentation in
one
place
, which should make building and understanding the bindings less work
overall. The interfaces can also be reviewed by the Rust maintainers in one
place for safety and quality.
Allocating memory
Like C, Rust puts local variables (including compound structures)
on the stack by default. But most programs will
eventually need the flexibility offered by heap allocation and the limitations
on kernel-stack size mean that even purely local data may require
heap-allocation. In user space, Rust
programs use automatic heap allocations for some types — mainly
Box
(a smart pointer into the heap) and
Vec
(a growable, heap-allocated
array). In the kernel, these interfaces would not provide nearly enough control.
Instead, allocations are performed using the interfaces in the
kernel::alloc
module, which allow for specifying allocation flags
and handling the possibility of failure.
The Rust interfaces support three ways to allocate kernel memory:
Kmalloc
,
Vmalloc
, and
KVmalloc
, corresponding to the
memory-management API functions
with similar names.
The first two allocate physically contiguous memory
or virtually contiguous memory, respectively.
KVmalloc
first tries to allocate
physically contiguous memory, and then falls back to virtually contiguous memory. No matter which
allocator is used, the pointers that are exposed to Rust are part of the virtual
address space, as in C.
These three different types all implement the
Allocator
interface, which is similar to
the unstable user-space trait
of the same name. While the allocators can be used to directly create a
[u8]
(a sized array of bytes; conceptually similar to how
malloc()
returns a
void *
instead of a specific type),
the more ergonomic and less
error-prone use is to allocate
Box
or
Vec
structures. Since memory allocation is so common, the interfaces provide short
aliases for boxes and vectors made with each allocator, such as
KBox
,
KVBox
,
VVec
, etc. Reference counted allocations can be made
with
Arc
.
The choice of allocator is far from the only thing that kernel programmers care
about when allocating memory, however. Depending on the context, it may or may
not be acceptable to block, to swap, or to receive memory from
a particular zone
. When allocating, the flags in
kernel::alloc::flags
can be used to
specify more details
about how the necessary memory should be obtained:
let boxed_integer: Result<KBox<u64>, AllocError> = KBox::new(42, GFP_KERNEL);
That example allocates an unsigned 64-bit integer, initialized to 42, with the
usual set of allocation flags (
GFP_KERNEL
).
For a small allocation like this, that likely means the
memory will come from the kernel's slab allocator, possibly after triggering
memory reclamation or blocking.
This particular allocation
cannot fail
, but a larger one using the same API could,
if there is no suitable memory available,
even after reclamation.

44610468.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于如何在Linux内核中使用Rust编程的第三部分，重点介绍Rust与C之间的接口以及内存分配机制。文章指出，Rust代码可以通过外部函数接口（FFI）调用C函数，但由于C和Rust在内存释放和锁定方面的差异，直接调用内核C函数存在问题。为了解决这些问题，内核文档建议为每个子系统创建一套集中的Rust绑定接口，以提供标准化和安全的接口。在内存分配方面，Rust内核代码使用`kernel::alloc`模块提供的接口，支持三种分配方式：Kmalloc、Vmalloc和KVmalloc，并允许指定分配标志和处理失败情况。这些接口实现了`Allocator`特性，并提供了便捷的别名如`KBox`和`VVec`用于不同类型的内存分配。文章还提到，根据不同场景，内存分配时可能需要考虑阻塞、交换或从特定区域获取内存等问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人口控制与可持续发展的关系，以及与此相关的风险和经济挑战

不同观点：
• [unearth3d] 认为人口应该回落到约17亿，这是地球基于自然氮循环的承载能力。引用Vaclav Smil的研究指出，合成氮并非解决方案，因为它在同位素上与自然氮不同，并对植物细胞结构有害。这表明人口减少是应对环境危机的一个必要措施。

• [smt88] 则关注母亲身份的风险，指出包括生育死亡、财务不安全和绝望感等具体问题。这些风险在讨论人口问题时被忽视了，尤其是与生育控制和堕胎等问题相关联时。

• [mytailorisrich] 同意人口减少对环境有益，但指出经济系统依赖于人口增长，因此面对人口下降的现实是一个巨大挑战。他认为尽管人口减少是可持续的解决方案，但社会拒绝接受这一现实。

补充讨论：
• [unearth3d] 的观点基于科学研究和历史数据，强调环境承载能力的限制和合成氮对农业的负面影响。
• [smt88] 强调了人口问题讨论中的性别和健康风险，特别是母亲在生育过程中面临的具体危险，这与环境讨论同样重要。
• [mytailorisrich] 提出了经济系统与人口增长之间的依赖关系，认为改变现有经济思维是应对人口下降的关键挑战。

争议焦点：
• 人口减少是否是解决环境问题的最佳途径，尤其是在面对经济系统依赖于人口增长的情况下。
• 在讨论人口控制时，是否充分考虑了母亲身份相关的具体风险和健康问题。
• 合成氮的使用及其对环境和农业的长期影响。

data.title: Ccusage: A CLI tool for analyzing Claude Code usage from local JSONL files
data.author: kristianp
data.article_summary: "ccusage" 是一个命令行工具，用于分析本地 JSONL 文件中的 Claude 代码使用情况，包括 token 用量和成本。它支持多种报告模式，如每日、每月和会话报告，并提供实时监控和按项目分组的功能。该工具具有小巧、快速、支持离线模式和 JSON 输出等特点，且可以通过多种方式运行，如使用 bunx、npx 或进行本地安装。主要功能包括详细的模型跟踪、费用显示、缓存 token 支持和多实例分析等。完整文档可在 ccusage.com 查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Anthropic的API定价、性能以及安全性方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [关于Anthropic的API定价和成本效益] extr认为Anthropic的API定价过高，尤其是Sonnet和Opus的价格，并对其利润率表示质疑。他指出自己每月在使用费上花费$600-$800，但仍远未达到使用上限，因此怀疑Anthropic可能在API上多收了5到10倍的费用。然而，他也表示尽管Sonnet和Opus在编码性能上不如O3/Grok4，且不如Kimi K2便宜，但Anthropic的模型在指令执行、可靠性和可预测性方面表现出色，具有独特的"心智理论"。

• [关于Anthropic模型的性能] extr指出，虽然Anthropic的模型在某些方面不如竞争对手，但在指令执行和可靠性上表现优异，并且具有独特的"心智理论"。这表明他对Anthropic的总体表现持积极态度，尽管存在一些价格上的不满。

• [关于安全性的担忧] thebestmoshe对使用bunx、pnpx、npx等工具运行代码的安全性表示担忧，认为这可能让代码获得对系统的完全访问权限。然而，他也提到这与安装npm包并没有本质区别，暗示这种做法在开发者社区中是常见的。

补充讨论：
• [工具的易用性] thebestmoshe赞赏Anthropic的工具易于使用，可以通过bunx、pnpx、npx等工具轻松运行。

• [关于Anthropic未来发展的看法] extr对Anthropic的未来持乐观态度，认为他们有动力降低推理成本而不是引入更严格的限制。但他同时也对Anthropic能否实现这一目标表示不确定，暗示这可能需要"奇迹"。

• [关于网站资源的推荐] ryoppippi作为ccusage的作者，提供了相关的网站链接以供参考，为讨论提供了额外的资源。

争议焦点：
• Anthropic的API定价是否过高以及其利润率的真实情况是讨论的争议焦点。extr认为定价存在过高问题，而其他人可能认为这是合理的成本。

• 使用bunx、pnpx、npx等工具运行代码的安全性也是讨论的一个争议点，thebestmoshe对此表示担忧，而其他人可能认为这是常见的开发实践。

Basic usage
ccusage

Project analysis

Group by project/instance

data.title: A 14kb page can load much faster than a 15kb page (2022)
data.author: truxs
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了TCP慢启动算法对网页加载速度的影响。尽管小网站加载更快是常识，但文章解释了为何14kB的页面可能比15kB的页面快612毫秒，而15kB和16kB之间的差异却很小。这是因为TCP慢启动算法：当浏览器请求网页时，服务器起初不知道连接的带宽，因此从少量数据开始发送，逐步增加，直到出现丢包现象。每个TCP包最大1500字节，其中1460字节为有效数据，初始发送10个包，总计约14kB。如果网页能控制在14kB内，可以节省一个往返时间，特别是在高延迟的网络环境下（如卫星互联网），这一时间可能非常显著。因此，优化网页大小对加载速度至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页性能优化、尤其是初始页面加载大小对用户体验的影响，以及在不同技术条件下的实现方式和其限制。

不同观点：
• **tonymet**：认为开发者应更加关注媒体层及网络层的可靠性和延迟问题，尤其是在3G/5G网络下。强调了HTTP请求的重试机制和数据包顺序对UI更新的影响，建议通过优化API和UI大小来提升响应速度。

• **susam**：分享了自己网站的优化成果，通过手写HTML、CSS及使用静态网站生成器，保持页面较小。但也指出在使用KaTeX时，客户端渲染会增加大量KB，考虑未来使用服务器端渲染。

• **crawshaw**：提出可以通过配置服务器来调整初始窗口大小，从而优化网页加载速度，例如将初始拥塞窗口设置为20个包，从而允许45KB的数据传输。

• **GavinAnderegg**：提到14KB是一个理想目标，建议将页面大小控制在前10个包以内。同时介绍了一个关注页面大小的项目512kb.club，并分享了自己的网站优化经验。

• **tgv**：引用Cloudflare的分析，指出在某些地区（如俄罗斯），网络限制使用户只能加载前16KB的网页内容，强调了页面大小优化的重要性。

• **9dev**：认为大多数开发者不需要过分关注TCP慢启动问题和毫秒级的页面加载优化，尤其是初创公司，应该专注于核心业务，而大公司会有专门的团队来处理性能优化。

• **firecall**：分享了自己在Rails构建的网站上进行优化的经验，尽管达到了100/100的Lighthouse评分，但页面大小仍有17.2KB，认为优化体验非常值得。

• **hackerman_fi**：批评文章中的两个论点，认为没有对比更大页面和14KB规则的实际效果，且文章没有明确说明图片内联到初始加载中的情况。

• **Alifatisk**：感叹现代开发者更倾向于使用Next.js等框架，而忽略了简单的HTML+CSS开发方式，认为这是一种退步。

• **simgt**：提出除了延迟问题，减少资源消耗也是可持续发展的重要考虑，强调网络对环境的影响，呼吁更多关注优化带来的附加效益。

• **ksec**：认为不一定需要最快响应时间，而是需要一致的响应时间，比如每个页面都精确地在1秒内完全渲染。

• **the_precipitate**：以旧技术为例，指出在现代技术中也可以找到类似的字节节省方法，但与当前讨论的网页性能优化无直接关联。

• **mikl**：质疑在HTTP/3支持下，TCP慢启动的相关性，因为HTTP/3使用UDP而非TCP，因此文章的建议可能不再适用。

• **xg15**：指出文章的建议仅适用于未加密的TCP连接，而在使用TLS加密的情况下，初始握手会超过14KB限制，且需要额外的往返交换，因此认为文章建议在现代加密连接下不再有效。

补充讨论：
• 文章建议的适用范围和限制是争议的焦点，尤其是在现代加密技术（如TLS）和HTTP/3下，文章的14KB规则是否仍然有效存在分歧。
• 多个评论者分享了具体的优化经验和工具，提供了实际操作中的参考。
• 有评论者提醒优化不仅是为了性能，还应考虑对环境的影响。

44613625.article_content:
Having a smaller website makes it load faster — that's not surprising.
What is surprising is that
a
14kB
page can load much faster than a
15kB
page
— maybe
612ms
faster — while the difference between a
15kB
and a
16kB
page is trivial.
This is because of the
TCP slow start
algorithm.
This article will cover what that is, how it works, and why you should care.
But first we'll quickly go over some of the basics.
What is TCP?
#
Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
is a way of using the
Internet Protocol (IP)
to send packets of data reliably — sometimes this is referred to as
TCP/IP
.
When a browser requests your website (or an image or a stylesheet) it makes that request using
HTTP
.
HTTP is built on top of TCP and a single HTTP request is usually made up of many TCP
packets
.
On its own IP is just a system for sending packets of data from one location on the internet to another. IP doesn't have a way of checking if a packet has successfully arrived at its destination.
When it comes to websites, knowing that all the data has arrived is important — otherwise we could end up with missing chunks of web page. There are other uses of the web where this doesn't matter so much — like streaming live video.
TCP is an extension of IP that allows a browser and your website's server to tell each other which packets have successfully arrived.
The server sends some packets, then waits for a response from the browser saying it has received the packets (this is called an acknowledgement or ACK), then it sends some more — or if it hasn't received an ACK it can send the packets again.
What is TCP slow start?
#
TCP slow start is an algorithm used by servers to find out how many packets it can send at a time.
When a browser first makes a connection to your server — the server has no way of knowing the amount of
bandwidth
between them.
Bandwidth is how much data can be transmitted over a network per unit of time. Usually it's measured in bits per second (
b/s
). Plumbing is a common analogy — think of bandwidth as how much water can come out of a pipe per second.
Your server doesn't know how much data the connection can handle — so it starts by sending you a small and safe amount of data — usually 10 TCP packets.
If those packets successfully reach your site's visitor, their computer sends back an acknowledgement (ACK) saying the packets have been received.
Your server then sends more data back, but this time it doubles the amount of packets.
This process is repeated until packets are lost and your server doesn't receive an ACK. (At which point the server continues to send packets but at a slower rate).
That's the gist of TCP slow start — in real life the algorithm varies, but that's essentially how it works.
So where does 14kB come from?
#
Most web servers TCP slow start algorithm starts by sending 10 TCP packets.
The maximum size of a TCP packet is
1500 bytes
.
This maximum is not set by the TCP specification, it comes from the
ethernet standard
Each TCP packet uses
40 bytes
in its header —
16 bytes for IP
and an additional
24 bytes for TCP
That leaves
1460 bytes
per TCP packet.
10 x 1460 = 14600 bytes
or roughly 14kB!
So if you can fit your website — or the critical parts of it — into 14kB, you can save visitors a lot of time — the time it takes for one round trip between them and your website's server.
How bad can one round trip be?
#
People are very impatient — and one round trip can be surprisingly long. How long depends on latency…
Latency is the time it takes a packet of data to travel from its source to it's destination.
If bandwidth is how much water can go through a pipe per second — latency is the time it takes a droplet of water to enter the pipe and then exit the other end.
Here's a fun example of how bad latency can be:
Satellite internet
#
Satellite internet is provided by a satellite in orbit around the earth. It's used by people in very unpopulated areas, on oil rigs, cruise ships, and for inflight WiFi on airlines.
To illustrate this example of bad latency, let's imagine a bunch of oil rig bros have forgotten their dice at home and need to use the excellent (under 14kB)
missingdice.com
to play Dungeons & Dragons.
First one of them uses their phone to make a request for the web page…
The
phone
sends that request to the rig's
WiFi router
— which sends that data to the on-rig
satellite dish
— lets be nice and say that takes
1ms
.
The satellite dish then has to send that data to the
satellite
in orbit above the earth.
Typically, this is achieved using a satellite in
geostationary orbit
at
35786km
above the earths surface. The speed of light travels at
299792458 m/s
, so a message sent from earth to the satellite takes
120ms
. The satellite then sends the message back to a
ground station
, which takes another
120ms
.
Then the ground station has to send the request to wherever the
server
is on earth (light slows down to
200000000 m/s
when it's in a fibre optic cable). If the distance between the ground station and the s

data.title: Why I Hate Azure with a Passion
data.author: tylersuard
data.article_summary: 文章作者分享了使用Microsoft Azure的糟糕经历，主要问题包括错误文档、无能的技术支持和开发团队对用户反馈漠不关心。作者提到，设置Azure的Web和Function Apps初期就遇到困难，之后的网络问题在耗费5小时与4位支持人员沟通后仍未解决。文档常常出错，例如Python web app教程无法在VS Code中正常运行。作者还抱怨开发团队对产品问题的反应迟缓，即使反馈后也未见实质性改进，比如AI Search Indexer和CosmosDB的问题长期未解决。此外，自动生成的GitHub Actions YAML文件也有错误，且未得到有效修复。作者最终对Azure的质量和支持深感失望，甚至向CTO发送邮件也无回应。整体上，作者认为Azure的开发团队懒散、不关心软件质量和用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对微软Azure相关问题的不同视角和责任归属的争议

不同观点：
• **moremsthrw243（微软开发者）**：
   - 认为问题不在于开发团队或技术能力，而在于公司激励机制和决策层。
   - 指出高层领导和企业买家在技术选择中的决定性作用，开发者往往只是执行者。
   - 提到短期决策和销售策略（如捆绑销售、激励措施）对技术选择的影响。
   - 强调开发者面临的困境：在公司决策失误时承担责任，且因公司市场力量强大，责任很难归到正确的层面。
   - 提到公司内部资源分配问题，如过度关注领导优先事项，导致开发者超负荷工作。
   - 对支持团队的效率提出批评，暗示问题比外界看到的更严重。

• **GianFabien**：
   - 持批评态度，认为这是微软的一贯作风。
   - 暗示技术选择是高层管理（如CTO）的决策，外界不应质疑其“智慧”。
   - 嘲讽高层可能在社交场合与销售团队做出重要决策。

• **tylersuard**：
   - 简单直接地表达对Azure的不满，没有详细论述问题具体内容。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：责任归属问题，moremsthrw243认为应该追究高层领导和企业买家的责任，而不是让开发者承担后果。GianFabien则暗示这是高层决策，外界无需质疑。
• **讨论深度**：moremsthrw243提供了详细的内部视角和具体例子，如销售策略、资源分配问题和公司文化的影响，而GianFabien和tylersuard的观点更为简短和批判性。
• **支持团队问题**：moremsthrw243提到支持团队的效率低下，暗示问题不仅限于技术选择，还涉及内部管理和支持机制。

总体来看，评论主要围绕责任归属和公司内部决策机制展开，不同评论者对问题根源和责任承担有不同的看法。

44622979.article_content:
Why I Absolutely HATE Microsoft Azure with a Passion
Tech Talk with Tyler
5 min read
·
Just now
--
Listen
Share
Hello. 2 years ago, I had the good fortune to walk into a job that I love. However, I had the bad fortune that this particular company uses Azure for almost everything. When I first started out, I thought, “Cool! I get to try something new.” Nope. It quickly devolved into a 2-year nightmare of wrong documentation, clueless support agents, and devs who frankly don’t seem to give a shit about your problems. Here is my Microsoft Azure story.
When I first started setting up Web Apps and Function Apps, it was a little tough going, but I thought that was just because of my inexperience. After a few months I found a problem that I could not solve: a networking issue with one of my apps. Not to worry, I thought. My company pays for the premium support plan, so we should be able to find help. I spent 5 hours on the phone with 4 Azure support reps, and they could not solve the problem. I felt frustrated and angry, because these people are paid to know how to guide us through Azure, and they were completely clueless. That has unfortunately been my impression across the board: the support representatives are always friendly and eager to help, but completely clueless when it comes to actually helping.
The rot doesn’t stop there at the branches, no, it goes all the way down to the roots. The documentation is often wrong: for example, try creating a Python web app using this tutorial:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/quickstart-python?tabs=flask%2Cwindows%2Cazure-cli%2Cazure-cli-deploy%2Cdeploy-instructions-azportal%2Cterminal-bash%2Cdeploy-instructions-zip-azcli
In my repeated attempts to do this in june and july of 2025, it fails when you try to use VS Code, which also is owned by Microsoft, so it should be compatible.
Next up, it appears to me that the devs sincerely do not give a shit about their customers, and the leadership does not give a shit either. For example, I complained extensively to the PromptFlow dev team about how awful and unintuitive their product is. To their credit, they booked 2 one-hour calls with me so they could watch me try and use their garbage bag of a program, and they finally agreed that nobody should use the online web interface. They also promised to make changes and fix the major issues I had pointed out. That was a year and a half ago. And guess what… I have not observed any meaningful fixes to the issues I raised since then.
I had the same experience dealing with a particular tool called AI Search Indexer. I complained for weeks to the team behind it, and they spent around an hour listening to me on the phone. I really lit into them, telling them it is unprofessional to put out code this bad, and they thanked me, and promised to change, and… that was 6 months ago, and all the bugs I reported are still there, it seems to me they have not been changed in the slightest.
Once upon a time, I tried using Azure’s CosmosDB for MongoDB. Its vector search could not find what we wanted in the top 100 results. I contacted support, they had no idea what to do, so I was escalated to the dev team. They told me to increase a parameter that I did not find anywhere in the documentation. So I did, and we still did not get the right answer anywhere in the top 10 results. I contacted the developer team again, and they changed their tune, and recommended I use full text search instead of vectors. That did not help, because full text search would find “Product ABC-X” when we were just looking for “Product ABC”. I even got to talk to the head of that product. He was friendly but seemed too relaxed to me, no sense of urgency, he just said “There’s nothing we can do”. That was a phrase I heard a lot from Azure support. When they had a service that cannot do something which I thought was obvious, they would say, “I’m sorry but there is nothing we can do.” They would keep the ticket open until I agreed to close it. I have dozens of tickets with them that never got resolved, but I closed them anyway because I knew Azure would not help me.
We had one ticket open for 3 months, with no progress, until I just got sick of it and closed it.
Recently, I realized that when I create a Web App and hook it up to GitHub, Azure automatically creates a GitHub Actions YAML file that deploys your code directly from GitHub to the Web App. That YAML file is WRONG, it does not work (A Microsoft support rep confirmed that for me), and if it were me I would be embarrassed to publish that code. Did they not test it before deploying it to potentially millions of customers?
Oh, and by the way, after a year and a half of having to deal with all of this, I emailed Azure’s CTO, pleading with him to PLEASE make Azure more usable… no response.

   - 强调开发者面临的困境：在公司决策失误时承担责任，且因公司市场力量强大，责任很难归到正确的层面。
   - 提到公司内部资源分配问题，如过度关注领导优先事项，导致开发者超负荷工作。
   - 对支持团队的效率提出批评，暗示问题比外界看到的更严重。

• **GianFabien**：
   - 持批评态度，认为这是微软的一贯作风。
   - 暗示技术选择是高层管理（如CTO）的决策，外界不应质疑其“智慧”。
   - 嘲讽高层可能在社交场合与销售团队做出重要决策。

• **tylersuard**：
   - 简单直接地表达对Azure的不满，没有详细论述问题具体内容。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：责任归属问题，moremsthrw243认为应该追究高层领导和企业买家的责任，而不是让开发者承担后果。GianFabien则暗示这是高层决策，外界无需质疑。
• **讨论深度**：moremsthrw243提供了详细的内部视角和具体例子，如销售策略、资源分配问题和公司文化的影响，而GianFabien和tylersuard的观点更为简短和批判性。
• **支持团队问题**：moremsthrw243提到支持团队的效率低下，暗示问题不仅限于技术选择，还涉及内部管理和支持机制。

总体来看，评论主要围绕责任归属和公司内部决策机制展开，不同评论者对问题根源和责任承担有不同的看法。

data.title: Microsoft Office is using an artificially complex XML schema as a lock-in tool
data.author: firexcy
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了文档格式应尽可能简单和易于访问，即使其基于隐藏的XML schema。然而，XML schema可能被人为复杂化，包含过度嵌套、非直观命名、过多可选元素等特征，使得实现变得困难。微软365的文档格式就是一个例子，其复杂性超出了显示内容的实际需要，目的是锁定用户到特定供应商。这种人为复杂性类似于铁路系统中控制系统的复杂规格，使得只有主要制造商能提供服务。文章批评微软通过这种策略迫使用户从Windows 10升级到Windows 11，而这种升级并无技术理由，只是为了锁定用户到其生态系统。文章最后强调，开发基于XML的系统时，应避免不必要的复杂性，追求简单和清晰。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对OpenDocument和OOXML（Microsoft Office的Open XML）格式复杂性、开放性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **OpenDocument简洁 vs OOXML复杂**：jonathaneunice认为OpenDocument的XML结构简洁、逻辑清晰，而OOXML则过于复杂，特别是在处理简单文本样式时显得笨重。他通过具体的代码示例展示了OpenDocument和OOXML的差异，强调OpenDocument在可读性和逻辑性上的优势，尤其是在大规模使用时更加明显。

• **放弃WYSIWYG模式**：jpalomaki主张放弃所见即所得（WYSIWYG）的文档编辑方式，认为这种模式导致用户被特定厂商锁定。他建议关注内容本身，而非形式，推崇像Markdown这样简单的格式，认为它们更适合现代信息消费方式。

• **历史遗留问题导致OOXML复杂**：flohofwoe认为OOXML的复杂性并非故意为之，而是因为需要兼容Office工具的历史遗留特性。同时，Microsoft选择XML可能是受早期2000年代XML hype的影响，而非出于技术优越性。

• **XML和HTML的复杂性对比**：wvenable指出，虽然XML可以设计得简单，但像HTML和CSS这样的开放格式也可能会变得复杂和难以理解，暗示OOXML的复杂性并不是其独有的问题。

• **Microsoft的复杂性不可避免**：bob1029为Microsoft辩护，认为其文档格式的复杂性是不可避免的，因为Office需要在全球范围内支持各种功能和场景。他认为，考虑到其功能范围，OOXML文档只有8000页的规格说明已经是个奇迹。

• **锁定效应与市场垄断**：markus_zhang认为，Microsoft的锁定效应更多是由于其与学校、政府和企业的合同关系，而非技术本身的复杂性，并表达了对大公司垄断的反对。

• **使用自定义XML格式与长期归档**：mcswell分享了自己在自然语言语法项目中使用DocBook XML的经验，认为XML格式可以提供长期可读的文档归档，并且支持多脚本的排版，这在某些专业领域非常重要。

• **复杂性导致第三方难以实现**：cranberryturkey指出，虽然OOXML是公开发布的，但其复杂性使得第三方开发者难以完全实现，实际上造成了锁定效应。相比之下，OpenDocument在简单文档交换中更为轻量和易用。

补充讨论：
• **早期Microsoft的SpreadsheetML更简洁**：donatj提到，Microsoft早期有一个更简单的XML电子表格格式SpreadsheetML，但在实际应用中由于文件扩展名问题导致与Excel的兼容性不佳。

• **AI生成解析器可行性**：another_twist提问是否可以通过AI代码生成工具来自动生成解析器，暗示技术进步可能有助于解决复杂格式的实现问题。

• **软件是否有提供互操作性的义务**：catmanjan提出一个哲学性问题，询问软件是否有义务提供文件格式的互操作性，这涉及到技术厂商的社会责任和用户权利。

争议焦点：
• **复杂性与锁定效应**：讨论的核心争议在于OOXML的复杂性是否故意导致厂商锁定效应。一方认为复杂性是历史遗留问题和功能需求的自然结果，另一方则认为这种复杂性实际上造成了技术垄断和第三方实现的困难。

44612569.article_content:
18 Jul 2025
A document format is a tool for sharing knowledge and, as such, should be as simple and accessible as possible in relation to the complexity of the document content itself. This remains true even when the format is based on an XML schema that is hidden from users when the document is displayed on screen.
Unfortunately, while an XML schema can be simple, it can also be unnecessarily complex, bloated, convoluted and difficult to implement without specific knowledge of its features. This is true even if the on-screen documents are identical. In this case, complexity is an intentional tactic used to lock users into a vendor, as is the case with the Microsoft 365 document format.
An XML schema comprises the structure, data types and rules of an XML document and is described in an XML Schema Definition (XSD) file. This tells the PC what to expect and checks that the data follows the rules. In theory, XML and XSD together form the basis of the concept of interoperability. However, in practice, an XML schema can be made so complex that it becomes a barrier rather than a bridge.
An “artificially complex” XML schema goes beyond the level of complexity needed to display even the most intricate content on screen. In fact, it is completely disconnected from the actual complexity of the content, to the extent that even a simple sentence such as “To be, or not to be, that is the question” becomes an inextricable sequence of tags that users cannot access.
This artificial complexity is characterised by a deeply nested tag structure with excessive abstraction, dozens or even hundreds of optional or overloaded elements, non-intuitive naming conventions, the widespread use of extension points and wildcards, the multiple import of namespaces and type hierarchies, and sparse or cryptic documentation.
In the case of the Microsoft 365 document format, the only characteristic not present is sparse or cryptic documentation, given that we are talking about a set of documents totalling over 8,000 pages. All the other characteristics are present to a greater or lesser extent, making life almost impossible for a developer trying to implement the schema.
To illustrate how this translates into a lock-in strategy, consider a railway system where the tracks are accessible to all, but the main train manufacturer imposes its own incredibly complicated control system. In theory, anyone could build a train compatible with the tracks, but the control system specifications are so convoluted that only the main train manufacturer can ultimately offer rail services.
The worst thing is that passengers don’t realise they are being held hostage by technical constraints that they cannot understand until ticket prices rise or the number of cities served declines. At this point, the main manufacturer can dictate its terms, which passengers are forced to accept.
This is very similar to what is happening in the world of information technology, where Microsoft is effectively forcing its customers to switch from Windows 10 to Windows 11 against their will. This switch has no technical justification and locks customers into using Windows 11 and Microsoft 365. This is because customers have completely ignored the problems that arise from using proprietary technologies.
If, over the years, the millions of Microsoft users who uncritically accepted a narrative that was credible to non-technical users but divorced from technological reality had taken a critical stance towards this monopoly, which would have raised doubts in any other sector, we would be in a very different situation today.
Instead, these users – including governments and supranational organisations – have allowed lock-in strategies, in which Microsoft 365’s artificially and unnecessarily complex XML document schema plays a fundamental strategic role, to become increasingly sophisticated and pervasive.
Therefore, if you are developing or choosing an XML-based system, bear in mind that complexity imprisons people, whereas simplicity and clarity set them free.

data.title: Broadcom to discontinue free Bitnami Helm charts
data.author: mmoogle
data.article_summary: Bitnami将于2025年8月28日对其公共目录进行更改。届时，Debian基础镜像的生成将被禁用，现有镜像将逐步迁移到Bitnami Legacy存储库。社区用户将只能使用有限的、经过强化的“最新”标签镜像，这些镜像可在https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure获取。企业用户需订阅Bitnami Secure Images以获得安全更新和支持。旧版镜像将移至Bitnami Legacy存储库，不再更新。用户需在2025年8月28日前调整CI/CD管道和镜像引用，以确保顺利迁移。Bitnami免费镜像仍会提供，但仅限于社区强化版。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bitnami容器镜像和Helm图表的迁移及相关影响

不同观点：
• 前Bitnami联合创始人ridruejo对技术团队表示认可，但对该商业决策感到困惑，并未直接评论技术细节，仅表达对决策的不解。
• KronisLV对镜像迁移表示不满，尤其是因为需要手动迁移到上游镜像，并提到具体受影响的软件（如Apache2、MariaDB、MongoDB等）。他还提到会避免使用与Broadcom相关的产品，但注意到开源代码仍会在GitHub上维护。
• remram对公告的措辞和时间表感到困惑，指出不同来源信息之间存在不一致，特别是关于镜像迁移的具体时间。
• chuckadams以幽默的方式批评Broadcom，暗示这种变化是该公司一贯作风的一部分。
• janjongboom关注镜像迁移可能导致依赖它们的系统崩溃，并提到曾参与创建的稳定构建服务（stablebuild.com）以应对类似问题，提供透明缓存机制。
• dpkirchner表示可能会因此放弃使用Helm charts，正在探索其他技术选项（如Quarkus、Helidon等）。
• ntqz预见到这一变化，已经开始将代码库迁移出Spring框架，测试多种替代技术。
• Youden指出开源代码仍可用，认为可能会出现社区支持的二进制构建，类似于AlmaLinux/Rocky Linux的情形。
• moorow提到Bitnami镜像在安全方面的历史问题，特别提到一个严重的安全漏洞CVE 9.4。
• sseveran关注镜像迁移将带来的 disruptions，询问替代方案。
• sbstp和js4ever对变化表示不满，尤其对Broadcom的决策感到失望。
• mfreeman451和iotapi322抱怨此变化对他们的工作流造成影响，特别是对Bitnami某些特定镜像（如RabbitMQ和Postgres的repmgr）的负面评价。

补充讨论：
• 公告措辞和时间表的不一致导致用户困惑，remram指出不同来源的信息存在矛盾。
• 用户对Broadcom的不满情绪较为明显，chuckadams和js4ever都表达了对Broadcom决策的批评。
• 技术替代方案成为关注点，KronisLV、dpkirchner和sseveran都在探讨或寻求其他技术选项以应对Bitnami的变化。
• 镜像迁移可能带来的系统崩溃风险被多次提及，janjongboom特别提到其参与创建的稳定构建服务以应对这一问题。
• 安全问题也被提出，moorow指出Bitnami镜像曾有严重安全漏洞，增加了用户的不满情绪。

📢 Overview
As of August 28th, 2025, the Bitnami public catalog will undergo the following changes:
Community catalog
Disable images generation for Debian-based images and gradually move existing ones to a
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
A focused set of more hardened, more secure images. These free images are intended for development and are only available on the “latest” tag. You can find them at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
.
Helm charts and container images' open-source code will continue to be maintained up-to-date and accessible on GitHub under the Apache 2 license.
Bitnami Secure Images
Production-ready, enterprise-grade containers and Helm charts will move under the Bitnami Secure Images offering.
Benefits include:
Hardened, low-attack-surface operating system
Continuous rebuilds with the latest security patches (SLSA Level 3)
Industry-standard CVE transparency (VEX, KEV)
SBOMs and compliance artifacts
Enterprise support and LTS branches
Access to the entire catalog of applications (over 280)
Minimal distroless runtime images
Legacy repository migration
All existing container images, including older or versioned tags (e.g.,
2.50.0
,
10.6
), will be moved from the public catalog (
docker.io/bitnami
) to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
(
docker.io/bitnamilegacy
). This legacy catalog will receive no further updates or support and should only be used for temporary migration purposes.
Suppose your deployed Helm chart is failing to pull images from
docker.io/bitnami
. In that case, you can resolve this by subscribing to Bitnami Secure Images, ensuring that the Helm charts receive continued support and security updates. As a temporary workaround, you can upgrade to the same version and update the repository parameter for each container image to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
🗓️ Timeline
Now – August 28th, 2025
You will see deprecation notices in READMEs and documentation.
Plan your migration: Update CI/CD pipelines, Helm repos, and image references.
Start trying out the new hardened images available to the community today at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
.
August 28th, 2025
The
public catalog
switches to the limited community-tier subset of container images (the same images that are initially available at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
).
Legacy assets are archived in the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
Post-August 28th, 2025
For development purposes, community-tier users are restricted to pulling only the most recent ‘latest’ tags of the limited community-tier subset of container images.
Production users should subscribe to Bitnami Secure Images for full version support at
https://www.arrow.com/globalecs/uk/products/bitnami-secure-images/#CTA
.
FAQ
Q: What is the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
?
A:
The
Bitnami Legacy
repository
is an archive that will host all older container images, including versioned tags (e.g.,
2.50.0
,
10.6
) that are no longer maintained in the main Bitnami catalog. These images will not receive updates, fixes, or support and should only be used as a temporary fallback for migration purposes. Although there are no updates to the container images, the Bitnami project continues to make its source code available at
bitnami/containers
under the Apache 2 license.
Q: How is
Bitnami Legacy
repository
different than
Bitnami Mainline
repository
?
A:
The
Bitnami Mainline
repository
(
docker.io/bitnami
) currently hosts regularly updated and supported container images, including free and enterprise-grade offerings.
The
Bitnami Legacy
repository
will contain archived versions that will no longer receive updates. It is provided solely to help with migration during the transition.
After August 28th, 2025, only a limited set of hardened images will remain in the
Bitnami Mainline
repository
. All others will be moved to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
Q: What do users of
Bitnami Mainline
repository
need to do before August 28th, 2025?
A:
Users should:
Review and update CI/CD pipelines to avoid relying on deprecated images.
Consider subscribing to Bitnami Secure Images if they need continued support, security updates, or access to full version history at
https://www.arrow.com/globalecs/uk/products/bitnami-secure-images/#CTA
.
Upgrade their deployments
If the deployed application belongs to the limited set of hardened images available under the new free community tier, double-check that the used tags are still updated.
Otherwise, point to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
as a temporary workaround.
Q: Are Bitnami’s free images going away?

data.article_summary: 《从洞穴人到化学家》是探索人类文明关键技术的课程，涵盖从火和石器到塑料和半导体的技术发展。课程通过项目形式进行，学生需制作如纸张、金属、电池等物品，并通过相关测验。项目分为不同类型：有些只需通过测验（Q），有些需撰写论文（P），有些可团队合作（T），还有通过展示行为完成的项目（B）。成绩根据完成的项目数量确定，从6个项目（D）到15个项目（A）不等。全勤和万圣节前完成7个项目可额外加分。课程设有每日只能尝试一个项目的限制，以避免积压到最后一天。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对链接、化学教育、网站设计以及特定课程项目的评论和个人感受

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun提到原链接损坏，但通过自行搜索找到了相关书籍（如Dunn的肥皂制作书和Caveman Chemistry）。他对自行找到资源表示满意，并提供了亚马逊的链接。
• globalnode表达了对化学的新理解，特别是通过学习化学知识理解了火、燃料和能量的关系，并幽默地表示自己可能错过了成为化学家的机会。
• quibono认为化学本应是一个可以通过引人入胜的方式教授的科目，但现实中学校和大学的教学往往枯燥无味。他推测这可能与成本、安全性和所需的努力有关。
• mrKola对新网站的设计不满意，认为新网站比旧网站更难看。
• ludicrousdispla引用了一个具体例子，提到从石器工具项目页面了解到BB弹击中玻璃窗产生的裂痕与锥形裂痕的相似性。

Suppose one minute were spent recounting the events of the past year.  What would you
include in a one minute summary of 1995?  1945?  1865?  A lot can be told in a minute.
If we were to allow one minute for each year, all of recorded history could be recounted in
a mere three days (of continuous talking)!  Here, then, are the Cliff Notes for human civilization:
one year = 1 minute.  The present moment is 11:59:59 PM of December 31.  January began

Chemistry 104
, "From Caveman to Chemist" is a course exploring landmark
technologies on the road to modern industrial civilization.  We will begin by
learning to make fire and stone tools and progress up through plastics and
semiconductors.  Your grade in the course will be determined by the
number
of technologies which you master. Although this is not a lab course, it is very
much a course about
doing
things. You will not only read about
these landmark technologies, you will be expected to make things like paper
and metals and batteries from scratch. By the time you have completed the course,
you will have an intimate knowledge of most of the
top 25 chemicals
used in
modern industry.

Many of these projects can be completed in your own time and in a place of your choosing.
Others, however, are most easily accomplished using tools such as beakers and

only
during V period (2:30-4:00, Mondays).
You are not allowed in the

The best time to take quizzes and turn in projects is during the last half hour

me.
While all of these projects are pass/fail, you may attempt any of them as many

There is one final consideration in passing projects which will help to preserve

data.article_summary: 《AI构建了我的应用，但结果惨不忍睹》是一篇汇集了多个真实AI编码灾难故事的文章。故事包括Replit在代码冻结期间意外删除整个数据库，导致数据丢失；一个应用在遭遇DDOS攻击后，数百个假账户触发了大量邮件。还有用户使用AI工具在一小时内花费63美元解决长久未解的问题；另一个案例中，AI执行了危险命令“rm -rf ~/”，险些删除所有文件。此外，有用户通过一次调用全面重构代码，但结果无法使用，甚至一个简单网站构建花费了高额请求数。文章警示了AI编码可能带来的风险，并邀请读者订阅以获取更多类似的“AI恐怖故事”。

data.title: XMLUI
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为XMLUI的新项目，旨在将Visual Basic的简易开发模式带到现代网页开发中，特别是React组件生态系统。XMLUI允许开发者使用XML标记来组合组件，无需深入了解React或CSS。通过简单的XML代码，开发者可以定义选择框、数据源、表格等组件，并实现数据的动态绑定和展示。文章强调，XMLUI降低了开发门槛，使得非专业开发者也能轻松创建交互式应用，同时支持自定义组件和响应式设计。此外，借助LLM（大型语言模型）助手，开发者可以更高效地进行代码重构和维护。总体而言，XMLUI提供了一种替代复杂JavaScript开发的方法，简化了组件的使用和应用的创建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：XML在用户界面（UI）定义中的应用及其现代替代方案的争议

不同观点：
• thisislife2 指出，当前的HTML等技术似乎在重复过去的做法，提到了XHTML和XUL的历史，并提供了XUL被放弃后由社区维护的链接。
• mrweasel 认为，将Visual Basic作为参考是不恰当的，因为VB的吸引力在于其简单的UI构建器，而编辑XML文件的体验与VB的易用性相去甚远。
• cgannett 表达了对HTML不断被重新发明的幽默看法，但同时也认为某些新方法对其有实际用途。
• yoz-y 作为程序员，认为所有低代码或无代码方法最终都会遇到问题，倾向于使用编程语言本身进行数据处理，并将模板传入数据结构。
• mnafees 分享了其在Qt和KDE项目中的经验，认为XML用于UI定义是有意义的，但个人对Qt引入的QML不直观感到失望。
• zamalek 认为XAML在正确使用时非常出色，但容易被误用，这可能是其未流行起来的原因之一。
• cheschire 提到了XSLT的关联性，并质疑为何未被提及，认为这是从XML转换和样式化的一个重要步骤。
• cluckindan 担心如果新系统不使用编译器，可能会导致浏览器XSS保护问题，因为需要启用不安全的CSP指令。
• lstroud 回忆XUL在工作时很棒，但调试困难，且VB和Delphi的应用维护不易。
• sheepscreek 对新项目感到兴奋，期待其能将VB的易用性带入现代Web编程，并对具体工具和文档表示关注。
• jug 认为应利用现代Web标准和XSLT创建自定义UI标记语言，这样可以直接利用浏览器原生支持的功能。
• jeroenhd 指出XML UI的广泛应用，并提到服务器端渲染和客户端渲染之间的轮回，可能导致旧技术重新流行。
• stillpointlab 将新项目与Adobe的MXML和Flex平台进行比较，认为XML适合作为UI描述语言。
• fxtentacle 支持使用JUCE的C++类方法进行UI开发，认为XML方法依赖于框架，长远来看不可靠。
• WillAdams 对新系统的实际部署和使用场景提出疑问，期待一个从开发到部署的完整示例。

补充讨论：
• 对XML作为UI定义语言的历史和现代替代方案的看法不一，有人认为其有价值，有人则认为框架依赖性强且难以维护。
• 对Visual Basic的低代码特性与XML方法的易用性进行了对比，普遍认为VB的简单性难以复制。
• 对新系统的安全性（CSP问题）和实际部署（开发、测试、发布）提出了实际操作中的疑问和建议。
• 讨论中多次提到XSLT、XUL、XAML、QML等技术的关联性和历史背景，反映出技术轮回和演进的过程。

44625292.article_content:
In the mid-1990s you could create useful software without being an ace coder. You had Visual Basic, you had a rich ecosystem of components, you could wire them together to create apps, standing on the shoulders of the coders who built those components. If you’re younger than 45 you may not know what that was like, nor realize web components have never worked the same way. The project we’re announcing today, XMLUI , brings the VB model to the modern web and its React-based component ecosystem. XMLUI wraps React and CSS and provides a suite of components that you compose with XML markup. Here’s a little app to check the status of London tube lines.
A dozen lines of XML is enough to: Define a Select and fill its Items with data from an API call. Define a DataSource to fetch data from another API call. Use the value of the Select to dynamically form the URL of the DataSource . Use a resultSelector to drill into the result of the second API call. Bind that result to a Table . Bind fields in the result to Columns . This is a clean, modern, component-based app that’s reactive and themed without requiring any knowledge of React or CSS. That’s powerful leverage. And it’s code you can read and maintain, no matter if it was you or an LLM assistant who wrote it. I’m consulting for the project so you should judge for yourself, but to me this feels like an alternative to the JavaScript industrial complex that ticks all the right boxes. Components My most-cited BYTE article was a 1994 cover story called Componentware . Many of us had assumed that the engine of widespread software reuse would be libraries of low-level objects linked into programs written by skilled coders. What actually gained traction were components built by professional developers and used by business developers. There were Visual Basic components for charting, network communication, data access, audio/video playback, and image scanning/editing. UI controls included buttons, dialog boxes, sliders, grids for displaying and editing tabular data, text editors, tree and list and tab views. People used these controls to build point-of-sale systems, scheduling and project management tools, systems for medical and legal practice management, sales and inventory reporting, and much more. That ecosystem of component producers and consumers didn’t carry forward to the web. I’m a fan of web components but it’s the React flavor that dominate and they are not accessible to the kind of developer who could productively use Visual Basic components back in the day. You have to be a skilled coder not only to create a React component but also to use one. XMLUI wraps React components so solution builders can use them. User-defined components XMLUI provides a deep catalog of components including all the interactive ones you’d expect as well as behind-the-scenes ones like DataSource , APICall , and Queue . You can easily define your own components that interop with the native set and with one another. Here’s the markup for a TubeStops component. {$props.line}
Here’s markup that uses the component twice in a side-by-side layout. It’s easy to read and maintain short snippets of XMLUI markup. When the markup grows to a hundred lines or more, not so much. But I never need to look at that much code; when components grow too large I refactor them. In any programming environment that maneuver entails overhead: you have to create and name files, identify which things to pass as properties from one place, and unpack them in another. But the rising LLM tide lifts all boats. Because I can delegate the refactoring to my team of AI assistants I’m able to do it fluidly and continuously. LLMs don’t “know” about XMLUI out of the box but they do know about XML, and with the help of MCP (see below) they can “know” a lot about XMLUI specifically. Reactivity If you’ve never been a React programmer, as I have not, the biggest challenge with XMLUI-style reactivity isn’t what you ne
44625292.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为XMLUI的新项目，旨在将Visual Basic的简易开发模式带到现代网页开发中，特别是React组件生态系统。XMLUI允许开发者使用XML标记来组合组件，无需深入了解React或CSS。通过简单的XML代码，开发者可以定义选择框、数据源、表格等组件，并实现数据的动态绑定和展示。文章强调，XMLUI降低了开发门槛，使得非专业开发者也能轻松创建交互式应用，同时支持自定义组件和响应式设计。此外，借助LLM（大型语言模型）助手，开发者可以更高效地进行代码重构和维护。总体而言，XMLUI提供了一种替代复杂JavaScript开发的方法，简化了组件的使用和应用的创建。
44625292.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：XML在用户界面（UI）定义中的应用及其现代替代方案的争议

不同观点：
• thisislife2 指出，当前的HTML等技术似乎在重复过去的做法，提到了XHTML和XUL的历史，并提供了XUL被放弃后由社区维护的链接。
• mrweasel 认为，将Visual Basic作为参考是不恰当的，因为VB的吸引力在于其简单的UI构建器，而编辑XML文件的体验与VB的易用性相去甚远。
• cgannett 表达了对HTML不断被重新发明的幽默看法，但同时也认为某些新方法对其有实际用途。
• yoz-y 作为程序员，认为所有低代码或无代码方法最终都会遇到问题，倾向于使用编程语言本身进行数据处理，并将模板传入数据结构。
• mnafees 分享了其在Qt和KDE项目中的经验，认为XML用于UI定义是有意义的，但个人对Qt引入的QML不直观感到失望。
• zamalek 认为XAML在正确使用时非常出色，但容易被误用，这可能是其未流行起来的原因之一。
• cheschire 提到了XSLT的关联性，并质疑为何未被提及，认为这是从XML转换和样式化的一个重要步骤。
• cluckindan 担心如果新系统不使用编译器，可能会导致浏览器XSS保护问题，因为需要启用不安全的CSP指令。
• lstroud 回忆XUL在工作时很棒，但调试困难，且VB和Delphi的应用维护不易。
• sheepscreek 对新项目感到兴奋，期待其能将VB的易用性带入现代Web编程，并对具体工具和文档表示关注。
• jug 认为应利用现代Web标准和XSLT创建自定义UI标记语言，这样可以直接利用浏览器原生支持的功能。
• jeroenhd 指出XML UI的广泛应用，并提到服务器端渲染和客户端渲染之间的轮回，可能导致旧技术重新流行。
• stillpointlab 将新项目与Adobe的MXML和Flex平台进行比较，认为XML适合作为UI描述语言。
• fxtentacle 支持使用JUCE的C++类方法进行UI开发，认为XML方法依赖于框架，长远来看不可靠。
• WillAdams 对新系统的实际部署和使用场景提出疑问，期待一个从开发到部署的完整示例。

补充讨论：
• 对XML作为UI定义语言的历史和现代替代方案的看法不一，有人认为其有价值，有人则认为框架依赖性强且难以维护。
• 对Visual Basic的低代码特性与XML方法的易用性进行了对比，普遍认为VB的简单性难以复制。
• 对新系统的安全性（CSP问题）和实际部署（开发、测试、发布）提出了实际操作中的疑问和建议。
• 讨论中多次提到XSLT、XUL、XAML、QML等技术的关联性和历史背景，反映出技术轮回和演进的过程。

data.title: Coding with LLMs in the summer of 2025 – an update
data.author: antirez
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了2025年夏季使用大型语言模型（LLM）编程的最新进展。作者指出，LLM在代码生成、错误检测和项目优化方面的能力显著提升，使开发者能更高效地完成任务。文章提到，LLM不仅能理解自然语言描述并生成相应代码，还能提供实时代码建议和自动文档生成。此外，LLM的协作功能增强，开发者可以更轻松地与模型互动和分享项目。然而，作者也提醒注意模型的局限性，如对复杂问题的理解仍不够深入，需要人类监督。整体而言，LLM在编程中的应用前景广阔，将继续改变开发者的工作方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• [dakiol] 对私人LLM模型的普及感到担忧，认为这会导致编程对第三方付费工具的强依赖，偏离了编程作为开放自由工具使用的传统。他强调了保持编程独立性的重要性，并指出即使收入丰厚，200美元/月的费用也不能轻视。
• [quantumHazer] 对讨论中使用"博士水平的知识"这一术语提出异议，认为博士研究的主要目的是学会如何进行研究，而不是仅仅获取大量现有知识，并指出这是受AI实验室的市场宣传影响导致的误解。
• [airstrike] 认为关于LLM编码的讨论应更多关注编程领域和编程语言的选择，而不是仅关注"氛围编码"（vibe coding）。他指出，不同的问题领域和编程语言对LLM的使用效果有显著影响。
• [iandanforth] 关注于不使用代理或集成编码代理的策略，认为通过在Web UI和编辑器之间复制粘贴可以保持控制和提供正确的上下文。
• [bgwalter] 对人们为了获得资金或竞争优势而推出"AI"产品表示失望，认为这是在寻找小众证据来支持"AI"的使用。
• [skippyboxedhero] 分享了使用Claude的GitHub action的经验，指出其在小任务上表现良好，但在中大型任务上存在问题，仍需人工指导和检查。
• [lysecret] 认为Claude在处理大型结构化Python代码库时表现出色，能够实现新的适配器模式。
• [Keyframe] 认为Gemini 2.5 PRO和Opus 4在抽象层面如架构设计上表现较好，但在编码实现上需要明确的指导。
• [krupan] 提出了LLM在代码生成中的学习机制问题，担心如果人类专家编写代码减少，LLM的进步是否会停滞或退化。
• [1024core] 发现要求LLM先描述其计划的实现方式，再进行编码，可以提高代码质量，通过迭代反馈提高实现效果。
• [dcre] 支持在LLM使用中保持人工参与，认为通过CLI可以有效管理文件传输，避免复制粘贴。
• [theodorewiles] 提出如果一个代码库专为LLM设计，应如何构架的问题，认为可能需要许多可组合的小功能。
• [fumeux_fume] 目前将LLM用作高级的Stack Overflow，询问如何在不离开IDE的情况下有效集成LLM工具。
• [speedgoose] 认为最近编码代理已经足够好，可以减少手动上下文管理，支持在理解LLM行为的前提下使用"氛围编码"。

补充讨论：
• 关于LLM在编程中的使用效果和适用场景存在不同看法，部分用户认为在小任务上表现良好，但在中大型任务上仍需人工干预。
• 对LLM学习机制和未来发展的担忧，特别是如果人类编写的代码减少，LLM是否能持续进步。
• 关于如何有效集成LLM工具到现有开发环境（如IDE）中的实际操作建议和经验分享。
• 对私人LLM模型普及的担忧和对开放工具传统的维护。

争议焦点：
• 私人LLM模型的普及是否会导致编程对第三方付费工具的强依赖，偏离开放自由工具的传统。
• LLM在不同编程任务和语言上的适用性和有效性。
• 如何在使用LLM工具时保持人工控制和代码质量。

data.title: A human metaphor for evaluating AI capability
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI竞赛性能结果的评估和比较方法

不同观点：
• [chronic0262] 认为不应评论未事先披露方法学的自报AI竞赛性能结果，以确保结果的可靠性和透明度。
• [ants_everywhere] 支持理解AI工具的总体方法，认为如果目标是理解AI作为工具的原始性能，那么AI与人类个体之间的比较并不重要。但如果要比较AI与个体人类在特定任务上的表现，则需要控制相关变量。
• [d4rnd0d3z] 分享了自身经历，指出在某些高级问题（如广义相对论）的测试中，AI的表现（如Grok 4）可能不如人意，尤其是在需要深度专业知识和独特解答的情况下。
• [roxolotl] 指出AGI支持者与反对者之间的争论往往各执一词，缺乏统一的评估标准。认为目前关于如何评价这些工具的基本原则尚未达成一致，导致争论不休。
• [svat] 赞同Terence Tao的观点，强调细节和设置对结果的影响巨大，并批评了一些人误解Tao的评论，将其应用于特定声明（如OpenAI的声明）的倾向。
• [largbae] 认为将AGI作为目标是浪费精力，强调AI已经为人类提供了巨大的信息处理能力，无需AGI即可解决现实问题。
• [johnecheck] 认为OpenAI在Twitter上发布的结果缺乏详细信息，尽管令人兴奋但实际意义有限。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何公正、透明地评估AI的性能，尤其是在与人类表现进行比较时应采用哪些标准和控制变量。
• Terence Tao的评论被一些人误解，反映出人们对AI性能比较的强烈兴趣和潜在的偏见。
• 关于AI是否需要达到AGI才能有效解决现实问题，存在不同看法，部分人认为现有AI已经提供了足够的工具和能力。
• 对结果细节和方法学披露的重视，反映出对透明性和科学比较的迫切需求。

data.title: Group Behind Steam Censorship Policies Have Powerful Allies
data.author: davikr
data.article_summary: 最近，玩家们强烈批评了澳大利亚组织Collective Shout，因其推动了Steam支付处理器的改变，导致多款含有禁忌主题的成人游戏被下架。该组织在其网站上表示，已针对近500款游戏要求下架，其中81款仍希望从Valve的平台上删除。Collective Shout得到了多个反色情团体的支持，包括NCOSE和Exodus Cry。这些组织曾推动删除Steam上的某些内容，并以保护儿童为由倡导加强内容审查。NCOSE曾特别关注Steam，并可能通过向支付处理公司施压影响了Steam的政策。Exodus Cry则曾发起针对PornHub的运动。尽管Collective Shout声称某些游戏涉及“虐待儿童”，但具体证据尚不明确，许多游戏只是包含了儿童角色面临困境的情节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Steam平台的内容审查标准及其双重标准问题

不同观点：

Over the past week, gamers have heavily criticized
Australian group Collective Shout
. The radical feminist organization has
taken responsibility
for changes to Steam’s payment processors that resulted in the removal of
various adult games with taboo themes
. As Collective Shout
wrote on its official website today
, the group has targeted nearly 500 games for removal on Steam, with 81 titles that the group still wants delisted from Valve’s storefront. As concerned consumers have dug into Collective Shout’s history to better understand its future plans, many have missed a key aspect hiding in the public eye: Collective Shout has the backing of several prominent anti-porn groups.
On July 11th, Collective Shout
published an open letter
to the CEOs behind PayPal, MasterCard, Visa, Paysafe, Discover, and JCB. On the post, Collective Shout includes signatures from executives at such censorship-prone organizations as National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) and Exodus Cry. Other allies include the anti-porn groups Coalition Against Trafficking in Women and the U.K. org CEASE. Both NCOSE and Exodus Cry have previously encouraged the removal of certain online content they deem harmful, with NCOSE in particular taking a strong focus on Steam.

One organization wants ‘HuniePop’ banned. Another hates the dancing Ankha meme
Screenshot: HuniePot
In 2018,
NCOSE previously targeted
a
series of visual novels on Steam
, briefly threatening the removal of these titles on Valve’s digital storefront. Steam ultimately reversed its decision to ban these games, instead opening the door to adult content on the platform. Since 2018,
NCOSE
has
repeatedly
mentioned
Steam in
its various articles

censorship campaign against the platform

HuniePop
is a game available on Steam, a popular gaming platform that sells and distributes thousands of video games for all sorts of systems, including the PC, Mac, mobile devices, and more,” NCOSE wrote on its website in 2020. “Steam must be held accountable for not only allowing this game to be on their platform but for not providing proficient parental controls and safety features to make sure games of this nature are found by especially vulnerable children.”
Play video
Meanwhile,
Exodus Cry
led a viral online crusade against PornHub in 2020, resulting in significant changes to the world’s most popular adult content platform. Free Speech Coalition’s
Mike Stabile
has previously described Exodus Cry as “a faith-based activist group that believes all pornography and sex work should be banned.”

Exodus Cry argued in a news post
that online searches for “video games,” “Fortnite,” and “Pokemon” lead children to graphic sexual content. The article proceeded to criticize the viral

-inspired
Ankha Zone NSFW dancing meme

any

previously pulled a visual novel
over a hidden, inaccessible file of an 18+ scene with a character that Valve considered underage, even though
the game’s publisher denied the claim
. The visual novel was only restored to Steam when the offending file was removed.

data.title: Digital vassals? French Government 'exposes citizens' data to US'
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 法国参议院在一份报告中批评政府及公共部门过度依赖美国科技巨头，如微软，称此举威胁国家数字主权，可能导致“主权自杀”。报告指出，法国将关键数据基础设施外包给受美国域外法律管辖的公司，使公共数据暴露于美国监控之下，特别是根据《外国情报监视法》（FISA）和《澄清合法海外数据使用法》（CLOUD）。微软法务总监承认无法保证法国数据不会被交给外国当局。参议院还指责政府贬低欧洲替代方案，过于关注价格而忽视法律和战略风险。与此同时，其他欧洲国家如丹麦已开始减少对美国科技公司的依赖。法国议员呼吁欧盟暂停与美国的隐私保护协议，以应对主权风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲在数字主权、数据隐私和依赖美国科技巨头方面的问题

不同观点：
• Saline9515认为，法国政府选择微软产品并非因为成本或效率，而是由于对微软的熟悉程度以及避免承担自身无能的责任。他分享了一个关于切换到R或Python的失败尝试的实例。
• mananaysiempre关注欧盟与美国在数据隐私协议上的法律冲突，指出美国法律与欧盟法律在隐私保护上的不兼容性，并质疑欧洲委员会的决策。
• afarah1提出，减少数据收集是解决隐私问题的关键，而不仅仅是关注数据存储的司法管辖区。
• ColinWright引用了法国参议院的会议记录，显示微软法国无法保证法国公民的数据不会被美国政府获取。
• crop_rotation批评欧盟未能建立本土软件生态系统，并指出中国在这方面的优势。
• phtrivier认为，部分法国和欧盟政府开始意识到对美国科技巨头的过度依赖是一个问题，并开始推动更多的数据主权措施，但实现完全的数字主权需要时间。
• isodev建议，需要更多的公共披露，让公众了解使用美国产品的风险。
• hollowonepl和CalRobert都对欧洲依赖美国科技巨头表示担忧，并质疑这种依赖的合理性。
• SpicyLemonZest强调，实现数字主权需要一个强大的本土软件产业，但过渡过程中会面临诸多挑战。
• bpavuk提到，法国尝试通过Mistral和La Suite项目来推动本土解决方案，并认为La Suite表现良好。
• guiriduro建议，通过设立一个完全独立于美国总部的欧盟企业实体来管理美国科技巨头的业务，以此作为隐私保护的缓冲。
• hunglee2主张，欧盟需要建立一个类似于中国防火长城的机制，迫使外国科技公司遵守欧盟法律，并为本土运营商创造发展空间。
• rdm_blackhole总结，摆脱美国科技巨头的依赖需要面对培训、成本和时间等多重挑战，而欧盟在这方面已经错失了良机。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多种解决方案，包括采用开源软件、建立本土软件产业、设立隐私缓冲机制等，但都面临着实际操作中的困难和阻力。
• 部分评论还涉及对俄罗斯干预欧洲事务的担忧以及对媒体偏见的批评。
• 评论中也反映出对数据主权和隐私保护的公众意识不足，需要更多的透明度和公共教育。

The French Senate slams the French governement and public services deepening reliance on American tech giants, warning of a looming “sovereignty suicide". Getty
News
16 July 2025
Digital vassals? French Government ‘exposes citizens’ data to US’
Anne-Laure Dufeal
Share
France’s deepening reliance on US tech giants is raising alarms about digital sovereignty and exposing public data to foreign jurisdictions.
In a French Senate report on economic and digital sovereignty, Senators accused the French State of “political fault”. That was in regard to outsourcing essential data infrastructure to US companies subject to US extraterritorial laws, including
Microsoft
, despite repeated warnings and alternatives.
“France is subject to US extraterritorial law,” the report stated, warning that public data, including from health, education and critical sectors, was exposed to foreign surveillance under US legislation such as the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) and the Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act (CLOUD).
This legislation allowed the US Government to demand that companies subject to US law disclose the data they stored, simply by obtaining a judge’s authorisation.
The Senate report cited Microsoft France’s legal director, Anton Carniaux, as admitting the company could not guarantee that French data it hosted would not be handed over to foreign authorities.
“Carniaux … was asked by the [French Senate] commission to guarantee that French citizens’ data hosted by Microsoft would never be transmitted to foreign authorities without the agreement of the French authorities. He replied: ‘No, I can’t guarantee that,'” the report stated.
US tech giant Microsoft presented new plans promising to improve the European cloud customers’ data protection.
https://t.co/lkX1ysk1vy
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
June 18, 2025
In March 2025, the Ministry of Education signed a €74 million deal with a US company for equipping its departments and universities.
The country’s elite school for engineers, École Polytechnique, also decided earlier this year to move the school’s IT system to Microsoft.
That was done despite earlier instructions from the French Government urging school districts to avoid deploying Microsoft or Google collaborative tools due to sovereignty risks.
The CNLL (National Council for Free Software) warned that “legal, technical, and strategic risks are being deliberately ignored.”
Speaking with
Brussels Signal
on July 16, French MP Philippe Latombe blames France’s “bureaucratic inertia”.
“There is no real connection between political leaders and French civil servants, who think they will remain in their posts indefinitely. This creates bureaucratic inertia. They secured early contracts easily because they have always been there, which leads to habitual reliance by public buyers,” he said.
In their report, the French Senate accused the government of systematically discrediting European alternatives, claiming they were “too costly” or “not efficient enough”.
“The commission of inquiry found that European solutions were systematically denigrated by the government, wrongly judged to be too costly or inefficient,” the report read.
For Latombe, France needs to move beyond price, and consider other factors like the fact that French companies contribute to the national social system, such as social security contributions, taxes.
French MP Philippe Latombe has urged European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to suspend the US-EU Data Privacy Framework before President-elect Donald Trump assumes office.
https://t.co/ni5C4rYxxW
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
November 15, 2024
In November last year,
Latombe criticised
the US-EU Data Privacy Framework (DPF) deal, saying it no longer served EU interests due to the US president’s “impulsive” nature.
The DPF was designed to make it easier for companies to transfer personal data such as names, addresses and browsing history from the EU to the US.
Another striking example comes from the cybersecurity sector.
In early 2025, the French cybersecurity firm VADE merged with Germany’s Hornet Security, forming what appeared to be a promising EU-based leader in international cloud security. However, just a year later, in March 2025, US company Proofpoint acquired the entire Hornetsecurity Group.
“As a result, there is no longer a fully French solution in this strategic sector”, denounced Latombe.
Tech giant Meta has snubbed a ‘cease and desist’ request from the European digital rights watchdog over their use of personal data to train AI systems.
https://t.co/tvtJr51KkD
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
May 15, 2025
While France deepened its digital dependency, other European nations have been pushing back.
In June 2025, Denmark’s Minister for Digitalisation, Caroline Stage Olsen, announced a full pivot away from Microsoft, replacing it with LibreOffice, a Berlin-based open-source alternative.

data.title: Java was not underhyped in 1997 (2021)
data.author: SerCe
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Java在1997年时的巨大影响力以及其后来为何失去关注。作者Dylan Beattie回忆了1997年他在大学学习计算机科学时，Java是必修课，并且被广泛应用于各种课程中。Java在当时因其自动垃圾回收、并发处理、异常处理等创新特性备受推崇，甚至被认为能解决所有问题，取代桌面应用和微软Windows系统。Corel等公司曾计划将重要软件移植到Java平台，Java applets被视为网络应用的未来。然而，Java的实际表现不如预期，在桌面应用和游戏开发方面不如Visual Basic、C++，而在服务器端网络编程方面则面临Perl、PHP等竞争。Java虽好，但并未能如 hype 所预期的那样彻底改变计算机世界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java的“ hype”（炒作）历史及其技术能力与市场影响

不同观点：
• **Java技术能力的“未被充分炒作”**：
  - **jasode**指出，Java在技术特性上（如类型系统和包管理器）具备优势，但这些优势未被充分认识和利用，因此在技术圈中是“未被充分炒作”的。
  - 例子：Java的强类型系统有助于防止错误，但未像JavaScript或Python那样广泛使用。

• **Java市场效应的“过度炒作”**：
  - **jasode**也提到，Java在1990年代被过度炒作，尤其是其对整个计算领域的影响，如“Write Once, Run Anywhere”的承诺没有实现。

44590034.article_content:
Java Criminally Underhyped? Not Back in 1997.
Posted by
Dylan Beattie
on
01 July 2021
•
permalink
Earlier today, a fun little moment of
Twitter serendipity
alerted me to an article by Jackson Roberts, a computer science student at the University of Colorado, entitled “
Java is criminally underhyped
”. It’s a really interesting article, and Jackson’s observations correlate with a lot of my own thinking about languages and platforms, although I am squarely in the .NET / CLR camp on that particular front.
But Jackson ends his article:
I am curious why Java lost its hype in the first place. Programmer culture history is poorly documented and if you have insight, please
email me
or leave a comment.
And, well, the comment I was leaving got a bit long, so I figured I’d blog about it instead. You see, I studied computer science at the University of Southampton, from 1997 to 2000, and when I was an undergraduate, the hype about Java was unbelievable. Java was too important to ignore; it was released in January 1996, and by the time I started university in September 1997 it was a mandatory course for all first year students; it was used throughout my degree course, right up to the final year module on programming language design where our coursework assignment was to build a Scheme interpreter – in Java.
Java circa 1997 was probably the most hyped thing I have ever seen in my career.
For starters, it was the first really mainstream language to introduce a lot of features we now take for granted in most high-level languages. Memory management? Readers, even to a first-year comp sci undergraduate who had spent a grand total of six weeks working with
malloc
and
free
, Java’s automatic garbage collection was clearly a revelation. Concurrency? It has threads. They work. Job done. Exceptions? You mean I can just write functions that return what I want, instead of functions that leave the result in a
char*
pointer somewhere and return an arbitrary non-zero integer if it worked? Java introduced a lot of incredibly powerful ideas and patterns, and it’s hard to underestimate how much impact it would have on the next two decades of programming language design.
But Java wasn’t content with that. Java was going to solve ALL the problems. JavaScript? The language that would end up taking over the world wide web? JavaScript was a glue language. The idea was that all your
serious
applications would be deployed as Java applets, with JavaScript used for only the most superficial wiring between applets. Java applets were such a big deal in 1997 that some people seriously believed that they represented the end of desktop applications, the end of Microsoft Windows; even the end of the computer as we knew it.
Corel, who at the time were still a credible threat to Microsoft’s emerging monopoly, announced in 1996 that they were porting their WordPerfect office suite and their market-leading CorelDRAW! graphics software to Java. Check out
this Infoworld article from 1996
to see just how deep the hype hole really went:
“The success of Java-based network computers, and perhaps Java itself, will likely require the availability of vertical productivity applications for word processing, spreadsheets and databases. At the JavaOne conference, Corel Corp. (www.corel.com) made a first stab at offering such products with the announcement that it plans to deliver a suite of office applications based on its QuattroPro and WordPerfect products. Both products should be available for sale by early next year.”
Java was going to revolutionise desktop development: Java Swing and the Java Native Interface (JNI) meant you could write your app once, and run it on Windows, Linux and Solaris.
1
And thanks to the amazing power of JavaBeans, once you had implemented a particular service or algorithm, you could create a “bean” for it and it could be reused anywhere, by anybody, and building software would be as easy as putting together Lego bricks. JavaBeans were often cited as the last component model we would ever need.
There was an industry spec for a “
Network Computer
”, a device profile that mandated support for HTTP, Java, JPEG and a handful of other standards… hardware companies would build and sell Network Computers, developers would use Java’s “write once, run anywhere” model to build software for Network Computers, and the entire future would be Java applets running on set-top boxes (or “net-top boxes” as they were often dubbed.) Sun Microsystems actually shipped a thing called the JavaStation, a device based on their SPARCstation platform that ran JavaOS.
The problem is: Java was good, but it wasn’t
that
good. For Windows desktop apps, Visual Basic and Visual C++ could run rings around it. For games and anything where performance was a consideration, C++ all the way, especially as we entered an age of affordable 3D graphics cards and OpenGL became a big deal. And for server-side web programming, we had Perl, PHP, Microsoft Active Server Pages, and good ol
44590034.article_summary: 本文讨论了Java在1997年时的巨大影响力以及其后来为何失去关注。作者Dylan Beattie回忆了1997年他在大学学习计算机科学时，Java是必修课，并且被广泛应用于各种课程中。Java在当时因其自动垃圾回收、并发处理、异常处理等创新特性备受推崇，甚至被认为能解决所有问题，取代桌面应用和微软Windows系统。Corel等公司曾计划将重要软件移植到Java平台，Java applets被视为网络应用的未来。然而，Java的实际表现不如预期，在桌面应用和游戏开发方面不如Visual Basic、C++，而在服务器端网络编程方面则面临Perl、PHP等竞争。Java虽好，但并未能如 hype 所预期的那样彻底改变计算机世界。

data.title: Dual interfacial H-bonding-enhanced deep-blue hybrid copper–iodide LEDs
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于无毒铜碘杂化物的高效深蓝光LED。该材料具有接近 unity 的光致发光量子产率（99.4 ± 0.4%），发射波长为449 nm，色坐标为(0.147, 0.087)。通过使用这种杂化铜碘化合物作为唯一的发光层，并采用双界面氢键钝化策略，显著提升了LED的性能。该策略有效优化了电荷注入，实现了12.57%的最大外量子效率和3970.30 cd m^-2的最大亮度，色坐标为(0.147, 0.091)。此外，器件在环境条件下具有204小时的工作稳定性，并展示了4 cm^2大面积器件的高效性。研究表明，铜碘基杂化材料在固态照明和显示技术中具有广阔应用前景。

Abstract
Solution-processed light-emitting diodes based on non-toxic copper–iodide hybrids are a compelling solution for efficient and stable deep-blue lighting, attributed to their tunability, high photoluminescence efficiency, and environmental sustainability. Here we present a new hybrid copper iodide that exhibits near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield (99.4 ± 0.4%) with an emission wavelength of 449 nm and color coordinates (0.147, 0.087), alongside its emission mechanism and charge transport characteristics. We use the thin film of this hybrid as the sole active emissive layer (EML) to fabricate deep-blue LEDs and subsequently enhance the device performance via a unique dual interfacial hydrogen bond passivation strategy. This synergetic surface modification approach, integrating a new H-bond donor self-assembled monolayer with an ultra-thin PMMA capping layer, effectively passivates both heterojunctions of the copper–iodide hybrid EML and optimizes charge injections. We achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 12.57%, maximum luminance of 3970.30 cd m
−2
with color coordinates (0.147, 0.091), and an excellent operational stability (
T
50
) of 204 hours under ambient conditions. We further showcase a large-area device of 4 cm
2
that maintains high efficiency. Our findings reveal the potential of copper iodide-based hybrid materials for applications in solid-state lighting and display technologies, offering a versatile strategy for enhancing device performances.

data.title: How Tesla is proving doubters right on why its robotaxi service cannot scale
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 特斯拉在奥斯汀推出的机器人出租车服务因一次险些致命的事故显示出其技术仍不成熟，当时车辆试图非法穿越铁路，而火车即将驶来，安全员不得不介入控制。尽管特斯拉的完全自动驾驶（FSD）技术已有进步，但数据显示每340英里仍会出现关键故障，如闯红灯或逆行。专家认为，特斯拉过于急于推出服务，以转移投资者对其销售下滑和电动卡车项目失败的关注。当前技术远未达到安全扩展服务的要求，每次增加车辆都会增加事故风险。特斯拉CEO马斯克正押注于这一变革性技术，但其可靠性仍存疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的机器人出租车（Robotaxi）项目的可行性、安全性、及其与现有公共交通系统的比较。

不同观点：
• **质疑机器人出租车的规模化和实用性**：[general1726] 认为特斯拉的机器人出租车无法在城市中有效扩展，因为城市交通容量有限，将单人乘坐的汽车放入城市会造成交通拥堵。他建议使用如公交车、地铁等已有的大容量交通工具，并指出这些交通工具的发展是自然的演变结果，而特斯拉没有理解这一点。

• **质疑商业模式的可行性**：[moogly] 认为特斯拉作为一个前瞻性的汽车制造商，运营低利润的出租车服务并不合理。他还对个人汽车加入车队盈利模式表示怀疑，指出车辆磨损、保险、清洁和充电等问题。此外，他质疑特斯拉如果认为机器人出租车盈利，为什么不自己运营车队而是卖车。

• **安全性和品牌声誉问题**：[breadwinner] 和 [findthewords] 都提到了特斯拉FSD（全自动驾驶）的事故记录，特别是与Waymo的对比，指出Waymo在安全性上表现更好。他们认为特斯拉在安全性上不如竞争对手，且对仅依靠视觉的自动驾驶技术持怀疑态度。

• **专业司机能力与AI对比**：[labrador] 强调机器人出租车应具备与专业司机相同的能力，认为目前的AI技术无法替代专业司机，特别是在处理复杂或极端情况时。

Christiaan Hetzner
Updated
